Abhyadhika indicates ‘superior quality.’ The Lord is extremely satisfied with those who offer worship to His pure devotees, and He rewards them accordingly. Because of the Lord’s generous appraisal of His pure devotees, worship of the pure devotees is described as superior to worship of the Lord Himself.”

8\. sarva-bhutesu man-matih: consciousness of Me in all living entities.

Kapila Muni condemns devotees who fail to observe the Supreme Lord’s presence in all living entities: “I am present in every living entity as the Supersoul. If someone neglects or disregards that Supersoul everywhere and engages himself in the worship of the Deity in the temple, that is simply imitation.” (SB. 3.29.21) Krsna will repeat this point to Uddhava when He concludes His instructions in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.29.13-17: “O brilliant Uddhava, one who thus views all living entities with the idea that I am present within each of them, and who by taking shelter of this divine knowledge offers due respect to everyone, is considered actually wise... For him who constantly meditates upon My presence within all persons, the bad tendencies of rivalry, envy, and abusiveness, along with false ego, are very quickly destroyed… Until one has fully developed the ability to see Me within all living beings, one must continue to worship Me by this process with the activities of his speech, mind, and body.”

9\. mad-arthesv anga-cesta ca: the offering of ordinary, bodily activities in My devotional service.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “One offers bodily activities by understanding that one cleans the teeth or the body as service to the Lord.”

BBT purport: “The words mad-arthesv anga-cesta state that ordinary, bodily activities such as brushing the teeth, taking bath, eating, etc., should all be offered to the Supreme Lord as devotional service.”

10\. vacasa mad-guneranam: use of words to describe My qualities.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “One can even use local languages or dialects to glorify or sing the Lord’s qualities.”

BBT purport: “The words vacasa mad-guneranam indicate that whether one speaks in ordinary, crude language or with learned poetic eloquence, one should describe the glories of the Personality of Godhead.”

11\. mayy arpanam ca manasah: an offering of the mind to Me.

12\. sarva-kama-vivarjanam: rejection of all material desires.

13\. mad-arthe ’rtha-parityago: renunciation of wealth for My devotional service.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “One should give up one’s own articles for use in My festivals. One can give them to one’s guru and the devotees on these occasions. Or another meaning is that one should give up objects (anha*)* unfavorable for *bhakti.”*

BBT purport: “The words mad-arthe ’rtha-parityagah indicate that one should spend one’s money for festivals glorifying the Personality of Godhead, such as Ratha-yatra, Janmastami, and Gaura-purnima. Also, one is herein instructed to spend money to assist the mission of one’s spiritual master and other Vaisnavas. Wealth that cannot be used properly in the Lord’s service and is thus an impediment to one’s clear consciousness should be given up entirely.”

14\. bhogasya ca sukhasya ca: renunciation of material sense gratification and happiness.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “One should give up the attempt to enjoy women (bhogasya) and the happiness (sukhasya) derived from caring for children.”

BBT purport: “The word bhogasya refers to sense gratification, headed by sex enjoyment, and sukhasya refers to sentimental material happiness, such as excessive family attachment.”

15\. istam dattam hutam japtam mad-artham yad vratam tapah: the performance of all desirable activities, such as charity, sacrifice, chanting, vows, and austerities, with the intention to achieve Me.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Vows like Ekadasi, done to attain Me, are the austerity of the devotee... One can perform sacrifice using sesame and ghee, or offer food to the brahmanas and devotees as sacrifice… Giving donations \[dattam\], performing sacrifice \[hutam\], and chanting 'japa are three sacrifices \[istam\] of the devotees... One should chant japa of the Lord’s mantra or names a thousand or a hundred thousand times.”

BBT purport: The words dattarh hutam indicate that one should offer to brahmanas and Vaisnavas first-class foods cooked in ghee. One should offer the vibration svaha to Lord Visnu in an authorized sacrificial fire along with grains and ghee… The word japtam indicates that one should constantly chant the holy names of the Lord.”

Krsna ends this series of texts by declaring that these fifteen elements “constitute actual religious principles.” By following these principles, or dharma, Krsna indicates, “human beings who have actually surrendered themselves to Me automatically develop love for Me.” The Supreme Lord concludes Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.19.20-24 with a rhetorical quest ion: “What other purpose or goal could remain for My devotee?”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 228), Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes these texts to illustrate the depth of a devotee’s faith, surrender, and devotion: “He gives up material wealth in order to worship Me, since that wealth is contrary to bhakti. He gives up enjoyable objects like sandalwood in order to attain Me. He gives up happiness in the form of caressing sons, etc., in order to worship Me. He performs even his Vedic rites for Me, and so they awaken bhakti. By his acts of devotional service in these ways, done only for Me, with body, words, and mind, such surrendered souls develop bhakti for Me. What other results in both practice and perfection remain for those who want only bhaktii Devotees disregard all other goals, seeing them as subordinate to bhakti."

Clearly, a devotee’s conscious focus on attaining Krsna’s service is one-pointed. “Those who are on this path are resolute in purpose, and their aim is one. O beloved child of the Kurus, the intelligence of those who are irresolute is many-branched.” (Bhagavad-gita 2.41) Krsna reciprocates with such sincere, one-pointed service by becoming inclined to enrich the devotee’s attempt to reach Him with His mercy. Indeed, the purity of their service makes such devoted souls unlimitedly dear to Krsna (SB. 11.12.1-2, 11.14.15, 20).

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura shows an essential difference between the practices and goal of devotees and those of jnanis: “What other result remains for the niskama devotee \[who desires nothing but bhakti\]? The result of their practices is simply more hearing and chanting. A jnani gives up his sadhana after achieving his desired result. When the devotee attains his goal, he does not give up his sadhana of hearing and chanting. Rather, his bhakti practices in the form of hearing and chanting increase a thousand times as an anubhava \[a conscious action motivated by love of God\] of the perfection of bhakti, prema-rasa."

*Texts 25-26: Fixing the mind*

Prema, love for the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is the natural result those who surrender to Krsna achieve.

The Supreme Lord now describes an exalted but lesser result that comes to those in the mode of goodness who perform devotional service with their minds fixed on Him: “When one’s peaceful consciousness \[santa\], strengthened by the mode of goodness, is fixed on the Personality of Godhead, one achieves religiosity \[dharma\], knowledge \[jnana\], detachment \[vairagya\], and opulence \[aisvarya\].” (SB. 11.19.25)

The BBT purport explains the devotees’ achievements: supreme peacefulness (santa) due to their selfless, pure desire to please their Lord (see Caitanya-caritamrta, Madhya 19.149). By serving the Lord directly, devotees attain the supreme dharma. They also gain knowledge (jnana) of the Lord’s eternal abode and their own eternal form, the greatest level of material detachment (vairagya), which means they are free from both piety and sin and the ultimate opulence (aisvarya) of a home in the spiritual world.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that the practitioners described in text 25 are performing bhakti as part of karma or jnana and therefore achieve the most exalted material fruits, which are born of goodness: religiosity (dharma, piety in goodness), knowledge (jnana, knowledge of spirit and matter), detachment (vairagya, detachment from the lower modes of nature), and opulence (aisvarya).

And what does a person achieve who neglects both Krsna and the mode of goodness, but who fixes his mind on objects in the lower modes of nature? Krsna says: “When consciousness is fixed on the material body, home, and other, similar objects of sense gratification, one spends one’s life chasing after material objects with the help of the senses. Consciousness, thus powerfully affected by the mode of passion, becomes dedicated to impermanent things, and in this way irreligion, ignorance, attachment, and wretchedness arise.” (SB. 11.19.26)

The BBT purport differentiates this result from the results Krsna has previously mentioned: “Rajas-valam indicates that one’s passion grows so strong that one commits sinful activities and reaps all types of misfortune.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura makes a similar comment: “When the mind, absorbed in body and house, pursues material objects in rajas, it becomes attached to forbidden objects. Know that it achieves opposite results. One achieves adharma, ajnana, avairagya, and anaisvarya.”

*Text 27: Krsna’s definitions of dharma, jnana, vairagya, and aisvarya - a summary*

In text 27 Krsna summarizes His points by giving us a definition of each ol ilie terms Uddhava asked about in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.19.8: “Actual religious principles \[dharma\] are stated to be those that lead to My devotional service. Real knowledge \[jnana\] is the awareness that reveals My all-pervading presence. Detachment \[vairagya\] is complete disinterest in the objects of material sense gratification, and opulence \[aisvarya\] is the eight mystic perfections, such as anima-siddhi.” (SB. 11.19.27)

Several verses ago, in text 24, Krsna indicated that “actual religious principles” lead to His service. He has also indicated, in texts 14-15, that the highest knowledge is knowledge of His all-pervading feature as Paramatma, and explained the detachment that is vairagya, in texts 16-18. Back in chapter 15, He discussed the most attractive material opulences when He defined the siddhis that arise from His own body.

Krsna has now summarized the goal of all Vedic practices in one text, and that text restates a principle Narada Muni put forward in Canto One: “Learned circles have positively concluded that the infallible purpose of the advancement of knowledge, namely austerities, study of the Vedas, sacrifice, chanting of hymns, and charity, culminates in the transcendental descriptions of the Lord, who is defined in choice poetry.” (SB. 1.5.22)

*Texts 28-45: More questions from Uddhava (28-32), and the Supreme Lord’s replies (33-45)*

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura introduces Uddhava’s questions (more than twenty-two!) at the beginning of this final section of chapter 19: “After hearing about dharma and other qualities and their opposites, Uddhava asks in five verses about the defining qualities of other items starting with yama, disciplinary regulations.” Instead of presenting all of Uddhava’s questions, followed by all of Krsna replies, as the Bhagavatam does, I will present each of Uddhava’s questions, followed by Krsna’s answer and any relevant comments.

1\. Uddhava: How many types of disciplinary regulations (yama) and regular daily duties (niyama) are there?

Krsna: The twelve disciplinary regulations are nonviolence, truthfulness, not coveting or stealing the property of others, detachment, humility, freedom from possessiveness, trust in the principles of religion, celibacy, silence, steadiness, forgiveness, and fearlessness. The twelve regular daily duties (niyamas) are internal cleanliness, external cleanliness, chanting the holy names of the Lord, austerity, sacrifice, faith, hospitality, worship of Me, visiting holy places, acting and desiring only for the supreme interest, satisfaction, and service to the spiritual master.

Krsna notes the potency of the yamas and niyamas: “These twenty- four elements bestow all desired benedictions upon those persons who devotedly cultivate them.” (SB. 11.19.35)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment is instructive: “The yamas and niyamas mentioned by the Lord are the same as commonly mentioned by others in both number and characteristics. Uddhava’s question and Krsna’s answer resolves the doubt as to whether the Lord’s opinion is different from others concerning the number and characteristics of these items… Now Krsna describes the unique qualities of other items, which are different from the definitions given by other teachers, and which are to be accepted by persons performing sadhana. These are described until the end of the chapter.”

2\. Uddhava: What is mental equilibrium?

Krsna: Absorbing the intelligence in Me.

3\. Uddhava: What is self-control?

Krsna: Complete discipline of the senses is self-control.

4\. Uddhava: What is the actual meaning of tolerance?

Krsna: Tolerance means patiently enduring unhappiness.

The BBT purport adds: “Tolerance means to patiently endure unhappiness, such as that provoked by the insults or negligence of others. One must also sometimes accept material inconvenience to carry out the injunctions of scriptures, and that unhappiness must also be patiently endured.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “Tolerance means tolerance of suffering prescribed by the scriptures or tolerance of suffering arising due to the disrespect of others. Other attempts at tolerance, such as tolerating suffering from cold and heat, are foolish.”

5\. Uddhava: What is the meaning of steadfastness?

Krsna: Steadfastness occurs when one conquers the tongue and genitals.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Without controlling the tongue and genitals, other types of steadiness are useless.”

6\. Uddhava: What is charity?

Krsna: The greatest charity is to give up all aggression toward others.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Charity means giving up violence to all living entities, not just giving money.”

7\. Uddhava: What is austerity?

Krsna: Renunciation of lust is understood as real austerity.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Austerity means performing vows, such as Ekadasi or the Karttika-vrata, which are prescribed by scripture, while remaining indifferent to enjoyment.”

8\. Uddhava: What is heroism?

Krsna: Real heroism is to conquer one’s natural tendency to enjoy material life.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Real heroism is acting in opposition to the rajas and tamas in one’s nature - avoiding lust and anger, for example - and to oppose advertising one’s qualities, such as one’s learning. Heroism does not merely refer to prowess in battle.”

9\. Uddhava: What is the definition of reality?

Krsna: Reality is seeing the Supreme Personality of Godhead everywhere.

10\. Uddhava: What is the definition of truth (or truthfulness)?

Krsna: Truthfulness means to speak the truth in a pleasing way, as declared by great sages.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura indicates that truth, even as it is declared by great sages, should he spoken in a pleasing way. He writes that truth means seeing everything everywhere equally. One should see others’ suffering as one’s own, giving up one’s harsh qualities, like envy and hatred— Truth is not merely speaking the facts... Rtam means pleasant and truthful speech, not just speaking truthfully. Merely “speaking truth” would include announcing a person’s actual faults, which would mean criticizing that person. But such criticism is not agreeable to the devotee listeners. That criticism lacks the pleasing presentation of truth.

Srila Prabhupada, however, regularly indicated that it was often helpful to others to state spiritual truths bluntly:

The other day I was reading in your - what is called? - World Almanac. In the next hundred years people will live underground like rats. So our scientific advancement has created this atomic bomb to kill man, and it will be used. And we have to go underground to become again rat. From tiger, again rat. That is going to be. That is nature’s law. Daivi hy esa gunamayi mama may a duratyaya. If you defy the laws of your state and you are put into difficulty, similarly if you continue to defy the authority, the supremacy of the Supreme Lord, Personality of Godhead, then the same result: again you become rat. As soon as there is atomic bomb, everything, all civilization on the surface of the globe, will be finished. So people may not like it. It may be very unpalatable, but the fact is like that. Satyam bruyat priyam bruyat ma bruyat satyam abruyat. It is social convention that if you want to speak truth, you speak truth very palatable, flattering. Don’t speak unpalatable truth. But we are not meant for that purpose, social convention. We are preacher, we are servant of God. We must speak the real truth. You may like it or may not like it that a godless civilization cannot be happy in any stage. That is a fact. Therefore we have started this Krsna consciousness movement to awaken this godless civilization, that you try to love God. (Lecture to college students, Seattle, October 20, 1968)

11\. Uddhava: What is renunciation?

Krsna: Cleanliness is detachment from fruitive activities, whereas renunciation is the sannyasa order of life.

BBT purport: “If one is attached to material things, his body and mind are understood to be always polluted. Cleanliness therefore means to give up material attachment, not merely to frequently rinse one’s skin with water. Real renunciation is giving up one’s false sense of proprietorship over one’s relatives and wife, and not just giving away material objects.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: Cleanliness means detachment from material actions, not just physical cleanliness. Uddhava did not ask about cleanliness in his questions, but the gurus, being kind to the destitute, speak on subjects even if not asked.

12\. -13. Uddhava: What is wealth? What is desirable?

Krsna: The true desirable wealth for human beings is religiousness.

14\. Uddhava: What is sacrifice?

Krsna: I, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, am sacrifice.

BBT purport: “Sacrifice is the Personality of Godhead Himself, because the performer of sacrifice, to be successful, must absorb his consciousness in the Personality of Godhead and not in temporary, material rewards that may accrue from sacrifice.”

15\. Uddhava: What is religious remuneration?

Krsna: Religious remuneration means offering one’s devotion to the dcarya in order to acquire spiritual instruction.

BBT purport: “Real religious remuneration means that one should serve saintly persons who can enlighten one with spiritual knowledge. One may offer remuneration to his spiritual master, who has enlightened him, by distributing the same knowledge to others, thereby pleasing the acarya. Preaching work thus constitutes the highest form of remuneration.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Giving donations means that, after a festival, one reveals to one’s dear friends one’s experience of bliss during kirtana. It does not mean giving money or jewels.”

16\. Uddhava: What is strength?

Krsna: The greatest strength is the pranayama system of breath control.

BBT purport: “By performing the pranayama system of respiratory control, one can easily subdue the mind, and one who can in this way perfectly control the restless mind is the most powerful person.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Strength, or balam, means to control what is difficult to control. Thus pranayama is strength because it controls the mind, which is most difficult to control.”

17\. Uddhava: What is opulence?

Krsna: Actual opulence is My own nature as the Personality of Godhead, through which I exhibit the six unlimited opulences.

18\. Uddhava: What is the profit of a particular person?

Krsna: The supreme gain in life is devotional service to Me.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Gain means gaining bhakti, not children or family.”

19\. Uddhava: What is the best education?

Krsna: Actual education nullifies the false perception of duality held by the soul.

BBT purport: “Real education means to give up the false idea that anything is separate from the Lord, the source of all potencies. Similarly, one should not falsely consider the individual soul to be different or separate from the Supreme Soul.”

20\. Uddhava: What is modesty?

Krsna: Real modesty is to be disgusted with improper activities.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Modesty is disgust for sinful acts ... not just normal shyness.”

21\. Uddhava: What is real beauty?

Krsna: Beauty is to possess good qualities, such as detachment.

22\. Uddhava: What is happiness?

Krsna: Real happiness is to transcend material happiness and unhappiness.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Happiness is overcoming suffering and flat ion by becoming indifferent to them. Happiness does not mean enjoying sense objects.”

23\. Uddhava: What is unhappiness?

Krsna: Real misery is to be implicated in searching for sex pleasure.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “Suffering is not suffering from burns but expecting enjoyment from objects.”

24\. Uddhava: Who is learned?

Krsna: A wise man is one who knows the process of freedom from bondage.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “A learned person is he who knows how to be liberated from bondage, not he who lectures on scriptures.”

25\. Uddhava: Who is a fool?

Krsna: A fool is one who identifies with his material body and mind.

26\. Uddhava: What is the true path in life?

Krsna: The real path in life is the one that leads to Me.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “The path is that which gives definite attainment of Me - bhakti and jnana - not merely a path free of thorns.”

27\. Uddhava: What is the false path in life?

Krsna: The wrong path is sense gratification, by which consciousness is bewildered.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “The wrong path is the path that causes disturbance to the heart, or the pravrtti-marga, the path of temporary pleasure.”

28\. Uddhava: What is heaven?

Krsna: Actual heaven is the predominance of the mode of goodness.

29\. Uddhava: What is hell?

Krsna: I Jell is the predominance of ignorance.

30\. Uddhava: Who is indeed a true friend?

Krsna: Acting as the spiritual master of the entire universe, I am everyone’s true friend.

BBT purport: Our actual friend in life is the bona fide spiritual master, who saves us from all dangers. Among all gurus, Lord Krsna is Himself the jagat-guru, or spiritual master of the entire universe.”

31\. Uddhava: What is one’s real home?

Krsna: One’s home is the human body.

32\. Uddhava: Who is a rich man?

Krsna: One who is enriched with good qualities is actually said to be rich.

33\. Uddhava: Who is a poor man?

Krsna: One who is unsatisfied in life is actually poor.

34\. Uddhava: Who is wretched?

Krsna: A wretched person is one who cannot control his senses.

35\. Uddhava: Who is an actual controller (and who is controlled)? Krsna: One who is not attached to sense gratification is a real controller. One who attaches himself to sense gratification is the opposite - a slave.

Each of Krsna’s answers has been brief, but it included Uddhava’s hope to hear both the positive definitions and their opposites. The Supreme Lord then says something that surprises Uddhava: “There is no need (or a more elaborate description of these good and bad qualities, since to constantly see good and bad is itself a bad quality. The best quality is to transcend material good and evil.” (SB. 11.19.45)

(deal ly, these exalted qualities, along with avoiding their opposites, are a great help to those aspiring to realize ultimate truth, but they aie not truth in itself. Most of the elements Krsna describedspring from the material mode of goodness and therefore limit to the material realm (or to the realm of liberation) those whose practices are confined to these principles. Krsna therefore rejects both the good and the bad, because He wants to emphasize practices and attainment beyond the dualities inherent in material goodness. Krsna wants to shift Uddhava’s attention to beyond matter, even past liberation, to the spiritual worlds, the eternal lands of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, which have been the special focus of the Bhagavatam’s Tenth Canto. So Krsna will now again emphasize devotional service, the process to attain those worlds.

Uddhava has carefully heard Krsna’s wonderful, concise definitions, as well as His Lord’s revolutionary relativization and dismissal of His own words. Uddhava will ask Krsna about the ramifications of His rejecting His own statements in the first five texts of chapter 20.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.19.45 indicates that the Lord spoke only briefly on the good and bad qualities because they are on the material platform of duality. The BBT purport to texts 11.19.40-45 completes the dearya’s thought: “Indeed, the purpose of life is to transcend materially good and bad qualities and come to the liberated platform of pure Krsna consciousness. This point will be further explained in the following chapter.”

**Chapter 20: Pure Devotional Service Surpasses Knowledge and Detachment**

*Texts 1-5: Questioning Krsna’s assertion that one should not distinguish between pious and sinful actions*

Uddhava asks Krsna questions that focus on the Lord’s last statement in the previous chapter, where He said, guna-dosa-drsir doso gunas tubhaya-varjitah: to focus on material piety and sin is in itself a “bad quality,” since actual piety means to transcend both of them. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura tells us what is motivating Uddhava’s somewhat challenging inquiry: “At the end of the last chapter, Krsna said that one should overcome seeing good and bad. Although Uddhava understood the Lord, he still wants to hear what He meant directly from His mouth, along with some examples to illustrate His point. So in five verses, Uddhava opposes Krsna’s statement.”

Uddhava begins with a clear statement of his objections: “My dear lotus-eyed Krsna, You are the Supreme Lord, and thus the Vedic literatures, consisting of positive and negative injunctions, constitute Your order. Such literatures focus upon the good and had qualities of work. According to Vedic literature, the superior and inferior varieties found in the human social system, varnasrama, are due to pious and sinful modes of family planning. Thus piety and sin are constant points of reference in the Vedic analysis of the components of a given situation - namely the material ingredients, place, age, and time. Indeed, the Vedas reveal the existence of material heaven and hell, which are certainly based on piety and sin. Without seeing the difference between piety and sin, how can one understand Your own instructions in the form of Vedic literatures, which order one to act piously and forbid one to act sinfully? Furthermore, without such authorized Vedic literatures, which ultimately award liberation, how can human beings achieve the perfection of life? My dear Lord, to understand those things beyond direct experience — such as spiritual liberation or attainment of heaven and other material enjoyments beyond our present capacity - and in general, to understand the means and end of all things, the forefathers, demigods, and human beings must consult the Vedic literatures, which are Your own laws, for these constitute the highest evidence and revelation. My dear Lord, the distinction observed between piety and sin comes from Your own Vedic knowledge and does not arise by itself. If the same Vedic literature subsequently nullifies such distinction between piety and sin, there will certainly be confusion. (SB. 11.20.1-5)

In other words, the measure of piety and sin serve as points of reference in the Vedas and are to be applied to every situation. The attainment of heaven and hell are both based on one’s pious or sinful actions, so failing to distinguish between the two will not help one avoid hell or attain heaven, or, for that matter, to elevate oneself to the point of liberation. Is it possible, Uddhava asks, that You are recommending we neglect sastra? If we neglect the Vedas, how will we know anything beyond what we can perceive and infer? Your dismissing the distinction between piety and sin will only cause confusion.

*Texts 6-9: Krsna begins His reply with the three paths to elevation*

Sri Krsna answers His dear Uddhava by first describing the three paths lo spiritual advancement (karma, jnana, and bhakti), along with the qualifications required to he situated on each of those paths (SB. 11.20.6-9). He starts with a mention of jnana, hut quickly moves to karma, describing the mentality of those suited to making advancement on the path of work (SB. 11.20.9-12) before stressing the importance of using one’s human life to make spiritual advancement (SB.11.20.12-17).

Then Krsna shifts, and instead speaks about the practices of jnanis (SB. 11.20.18-24) before describing how to deal with falldowns on any of the paths He has recommended (SB. 11.20.25-26). In Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.27-30, Krsna glorifies and describes the processes of pure devotional service before comparing bhakti to karma and jnana in texts 31-33.

Nearing the conclusion of His response, He glorifies His devotees, for they want nothing other than to serve Him (SB. 11.20.34-35). Then in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.36, Krsna more directly responds to Uddhava’s question about His apparent negation of the differences between good and bad, piety and sin, by providing, as a frame of reference, transcendental, pure devotional service to Him. That is, His statement made in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.19.45 - “There is no need for a more elaborate description of these good and bad qualities, since to constantly see good and bad is itself a bad quality. The best quality is to transcend material good and evil” - can only properly be understood within the framework of devotional service.

The Supreme Lord then completes the chapter with a one-text summary (SB. 11.20.37) of the three methodologies of spiritual advancement and what practitioners of them attain.

The Supreme Personality of Godhead begins: “My dear Uddhava, because I desire that human beings may achieve perfection, I have presented three paths of advancement - the path of knowledge, the path of work, and the path of devotion. Besides these three there is absolutely no other means of elevation.” (SB. 11.20.6)

From the BBT purport: “Ultimately, the goal of philosophical speculation, pious regulated work, and devotional service is the same - Krsna consciousness.... Although all authorized processes of human perfection ultimately lead to Krsna consciousness, or love of God, various performers have specific propensities and qualifications and thus gravitate to different methods of self-realization. Lord Krsna here describes the three authorized processes together in order to emphasize that their ultimate goal is one. At the same time, philosophical speculation and regulated pious work can never he considered equal to pure love of Godhead, as the Lord has elaborately clarified in the previous chapters.”

These three paths differ, and the principles, injunctions, and prohibitions that govern them also differ. “Good” and “bad,” as well as “what is to be done” and “what is not to be done” are naturally defined by the specific requirements of each path. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes: “No other means of elevation exists other than these three. Austerity and yoga are included to some degree in jnana and bhakti, so they are not considered separately.”

*Texts 7—8: Who should take to each path?*

*Text 7: The qualifications for jnana or karma*

“Among these three paths, jnana-yoga, the path of philosophical speculation, is recommended for those who are disgusted with material life and are thus detached from ordinary, fruitive activities. Those who are not disgusted with material life, having many desires yet to fulfill, should seek perfection through the path of karma- yoga.” (SB. 11.20.7)

The Vedic path is inclusive, and a path of elevation is provided for all people, regardless of their tendencies and qualifications. The BBT purport defines the tendencies that qualifyone for the path of jnana as “Those who are frustrated in the ordinary material life of society, friendship, and love, and who understand that promotion to heaven simply brings further domestic miseries, take directly to the path of knowledge. Through authorized philosophical discrimination they transcend the bonds of material existence.” The same purport also describes what qualifies one for spiritual advancement on the karma path: “Those who are still desirous of enjoying material society, friendship, and love, and who are excited by the prospect of going with their relatives to material heavenly planets... are advised to remain in family life and offer the fruits of their work to the Supreme.”

*Text 8: Qualifications for bhakti*

Now Krsna speaks of the simple hut uncommon qualification that allows one to practice bhakti: “If somehow or other by good fortune one develops faith in hearing and chanting My glories, such a person, being neither very disgusted with nor attached to material life, should achieve perfection through the path of loving devotion to Me.” (SB. 11.20.8)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes about the qualifications for practicing bhakti: “Faith in the topics about the Lord (mat-kathadau jata-sraddha) is the qualification for bhakti-yoga.... By using the singular (‘one person’), it is indicated that a person who has developed such faith is rare compared to the number of jnanis and karmis. A person quadfied for bhakti is not overly attached to the body, house, or family. He is also not disgusted with the world, for disgust is the qualification for the practice of jnana. Being overly attached to body and house qualifies a person for karma-yoga. If he does not have such attachment, he becomes qualified for bhakti. Thus the distinctions between the qualifications for the three processes is considered... Excessive attachment is caused by beginningless ignorance. One loses one’s excessive attachment to ignorance by the unexpected association of great devotees… Even if a person is busy with sense enjoyment, the unexpected association of devotees gives him the qualification to practice bhakti.”

*Texts 9-12: Prescriptions for those making advancement on the karma path*

In Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.9, Krsna gives a prescription for those who have material desires and no taste for devotional service: “As long as one is not satiated by fruitive activity and has not awakened his taste for devotional service by sravanam kirtanam visnoh one has to act according to the regulative principles of the Vedic injunctions.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that those who are attached to matter should become purified by continuing to perform their prescribed duties until they become detached. He then asks, “When will he become qualified for jnana and bhakti!" and then answers his own question: “When he becomes detached, he becomes qualified for jnana." The deary a continues: “Or he should continue performing his karma until faith in topics about the Lord arises by the mercy of the devotees. Before he has such faith, he is qualified only for karma. When faith appears, as explained in the previous verse, he becomes qualified only for bhakti and is no longer qualified for karma. This faith should be uninterrupted. He has to have firm faith that he will reach perfection by hearing about the Lord, not by karma or jnana. This faith arises only from the association of pure devotees.”

Later in Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment, the acarya mentions “the opinions of others,” those who say that faith in bhakti may arise by seeing the excellence of other devotees (not specifically great devotees) or by noting that since sastra recommends bhakti over varnasrama, someone may understand this and take to bhakti (even if he doesn’t meet any great devotees).

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura appears to respect these view-points as valid.

In the next text, text 10 of chapter 20, Krsna lists the results that come to one on the path of karma who dutifully performs his duties prescribed by the Vedas with detachment from the results. The Supreme Lord concludes that a person who practices detached work, or niskama- karma-yoga, neither enjoys heaven nor suffers hell as a reaction to his dutifully performed work.

What does happen to such a follower? Krsna answers that question next: “One who is situated in his prescribed duty, free from sinful activities and cleansed of material contamination, in this very life obtains transcendental knowledge or, by fortune, devotional service unto Me.” (SB. 11.20.11)

Knowledge or bhakti: what determines the direction of such a person’s spiritual advancement? Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains further: “What does this performer of karma attain? Situated in this world, performing his duties, sinless because of performing detached, dutiful work (niskama-karma), pure in heart because of no sin, he attains jnana and liberation. If he unexpectedly attains the association of persons practicing suddha-bhakti, he also attains pure bhakti for Me. Then he attains prema. If he attains association with mixed bhaktas - karma-misra-bhaktas or jnana-misra-bhaktas - by that type of bhakti he attains santa-rati \[a neutral relationship with Krsna\]. ”

The BBT purport paraphrases Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “If one’s devotional service is mixed with a tendency toward fruitive activities or mental speculation, then one may achieve the neutral stage of love of Godhead, whereas those who are inclined to serve only Lord Krsna advance to the higher stages of love of Godhead in servitude, friendship, parental love, and the conjugal relationship.”

Again, one’s association determines one’s destination. Then what determines one’s association? In text 8 of this chapter Krsna used the word yadrcchaya to indicate that somehow or other, by good fortune, one gains the association of His pure devotees. The same word yadrcchaya also indicates t he independent, causeless, freely willed desire of the devotee to bestow bis association on others. Or it can also be understood as “by the grace of providence,” “by chance,” or more simply, “by the Supreme Lord’s will.”

*Texts 12-17: The opportunity afforded by a human birth*

Having described the fortune of walking toward Him on any one of the three paths (karma, jnana, or bhakti), Sri Krsna encourages us, in His words to Uddhava, to take proper advantage of our current human birth. Such a birth affords a unique opportunity for spiritual advancement, and therefore Krsna now exalts that opportunity to Uddhava: “The residents of both heaven and hell desire human birth on the earth planet because human life facilitates the achievement of transcendental knowledge and love of Godhead, whereas neither heavenly nor hellish bodies efficiently provide such opportunities.” (SB. 11.20.12) What makes a human birth so unique? The BBT purport cites Srila Jiva Gosvami, who points out that “in material heaven one becomes absorbed in extraordinary sense gratification and in hell one is absorbed in suffering. In both cases there is little impetus to acquire transcendental knowledge or pure love of Godhead. Excessive suffering or excessive enjoyment are thus impediments to spiritual advancement.”

Krsna continues: “A wise person, knowing that although the material body is subject to death it can still award the perfection of one’s life, should not foolishly neglect to take advantage of this opportunity before death arrives.” (SB. 11.20.14)

That one’s body is temporary doesn’t negate its value. Yet one should nevertheless maintain detachment from the body, for the relationship between the soul and the body is temporary. Krsna told Arjuna: “One who has taken his birth is sure to die, and after death one is sure to take birth again. Therefore, in the unavoidable discharge of your duty, you should not lament.” (Bhagavad-gita 2.27) Krsna will now offer Uddhava an example of what it means to live detached within one’s own body: “Without attachment, a bird gives up the tree in which his nest was constructed when that tree is cut down by cruel men who are like death personified, and thus the bird achieves happiness in another place.” (SB. 11.20.15) Krsna develops the thought in the next text: “Knowing that one’s duration of life is being similarly cut down by the passing of days and nights, one should be shaken by fear. In this way, giving up all material attachment and desire, one understands the Supreme Lord and achieves perfect peace.” (SB. 1 1.20.16)

To increase our fear, we join a terrified Arjuna as he sees Krsna’s universal manifestation on the battlefield of Kuruksetra (Bhagavad-gita 11.23, 25-31):

O mighty-armed one, all the planets with their demigods are disturbed at seeing Your great form, with its many faces, eyes, arms, thighs, legs, and bellies and Your many terrible teeth; and as they are disturbed, so am I. O Lord of lords, O refuge of the worlds, please be gracious to me. I cannot keep my balance seeing thus Your blazing deathlike faces and awful teeth. In all directions I am bewildered. All the sons of Dhrtarastra, along with their allied kings, and Bhisma, Drona, Kama - and our chief soldiers also - are rushing into Your fearful mouths. And some I see trapped with heads smashed between Your teeth. As the many waves of the rivers flow into the ocean, so do all these great warriors enter blazing into Your mouths. I see all people rushing full speed into Your mouths, as moths dash to destruction in a blazing fire. O Visnu, I see You devouring all people from all sides with Your flaming mouths. Covering all the universe with Your effulgence, You are manifest with terrible, scorching rays. O Lord of lords, so fierce of form, please tell me who You are. I offer my obeisances unto You; please be gracious to me. You are the primal Lord. I want to know about You, for I do not know what Your mission is.

Krsna’s reply to Arjuna (in Bhagavad-gita 11.32) defines how He greets everyone in this world - as the destroyer: kalo ’smi loka-ksaya-krt pravrddho lokan samahartum iha pravrttah, “Time I am, the great destroyer of the worlds, and I have come here to destroy all people.”

Now, as Krsna speaks to Uddhava in the Uddhava-gita, the Lord concludes this topic by stressing the rare but fortunate opportunity a human body affords: “The human body, which can award all benefit in life, is automatically obtained by the laws of nature, although it is a very rare achievement. This human body can be compared to a perfectly constructed boat having the spiritual master as the captain and the instructions of the Personality of Godhead as favorable winds impelling it on its course. Considering all these advantages, a human being who does not utilize his human life to cross the ocean of material existence must he considered the killer of his own soul.” (SB. 11.20.17)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura compares the failure to use one’s human birth for spiritual advancement to a poor man’s finding a touchstone that can change base metal into gold and then throwing it in the mud.

*Texts 18-24: Practices of jnanis - effecting the shift from the temporary to the eternal*

In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.18, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes: “Having praised the human body, which allows practice of both jnana and bhakti, Krsna speaks of the actions necessary for persons qualified for jnana.”

Krsna just stressed the advantages of a human birth, which can carry us from the temporary to the eternal. Now He is instructing the jnanis, but His instructions also support the bhaktas (sangasiddha-bhakti) because they stress useful methodologies for controlling the mind: “A transcendentalist, having become disgusted and hopeless in all endeavors for material happiness, completely controls the senses and develops detachment. By spiritual practice he should then fix the mind on the spiritual platform without deviation.” (SB. 11.20.18) For the jnani, the focus is on the eternal. The devotees develop a relationship with the supreme aspect of the eternal, Sri Krsna Himself, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and serve Him with devotion.

**Determination to bring the mind back**

How should one effect the shift from the temporary to the eternal? Sri Krsna advises: “Whenever the mind, being concentrated on the spiritual platform, is suddenly deviated from its spiritual position, one should carefully bring it under the control of the self by following the prescribed means.” (SB. 11.20.19)

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.19 quotes Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, who addresses an element of the process of controlling the mind: “When one first tries to control his mind, it is difficult. In fact, the mind becomes doubly restless. The urge to enjoy matter is so strong that the mind is naturally carried away by it. In such a situation one should control his mind by allowing it to have a little bit of sense gratification.”

**Controlling the mind by maintaining goodness**

“One should never lose sight of the actual goal of mental activities, but rather, conquering the life air and senses and utilizing intelligence strengthened by the mode of goodness, one should bring the mind under the control of the self.” (SB. 11.20.20)

**Be expert, intelligent, and practical when trying to control the mind**

“An expert horseman, desiring to tame a headstrong horse, first lets the horse have his way for a moment and then, pulling the reins, gradually places the horse on the desired path. Similarly, the supreme yoga process is that by which one carefully observes the movements and desires of the mind and gradually brings them under full control.” (SB. 11.20.21)

Offering an example, Krsna praises the practice of vigilantly focusing the mind on the spiritual platform by the method He described in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.19. The BBT purport adds to Krsna’s advice: “A learned transcendentalist withholds and supplies sense objects so that the mind and senses remain fully controlled, just as the horseman sometimes pulls sharply on the reins and sometimes allows the horse to run freely. The rider never forgets his actual goal or destination, and eventually places the horse on the right path. Similarly, a learned tran- scendentalist, even though sometimes allowing the senses to act, never forgets the goal of self-realization, nor does he allow the senses to engage in sinful activity. Excessive austerity or restriction may result in great mental disturbance, just as pulling excessively on the reins of a horse may cause the horse to rear up against the rider.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “Sri Krsna cites an example of how to check the mind’s urges. It is reasonable to fulfill the mind’s demands a little in order to control it completely. To control the mind is the main purpose of the yoga process. A person who wants to control his senses should follow the example Krsna gives of the horse tamer, who thinks: ‘Although the horse (arvatah) to be tamed (damy-asya) is unwilling to know my heart’s wishes (hrdaya-jnatvam), it should know them.’ Since he cannot suddenly bring the horse under control, he lirst follows its movements a little, but he continues to hold the rope. He does not let the horse go wild.’’

And from Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura: “If the mind that runs toward material enjoyment like a horse comes to know that its goal is the supreme Absolute Truth, its function can be properly used. When the consideration of worshiping Hari gradually awakens in a soul, it automatically controls the restlessness of the mind. Simply by engaging the mental functions in serving the eternal object, a living entity attains auspiciousness. Therefore in order to control the mind one should follow the path of yukta-vairagya, not phalgu-vairagya.”

**Preach to the mind**

“Until one’s mind is fixed in spiritual satisfaction, one should analytically study the temporary nature of all material objects, whether cosmic, earthly, or atomic. One should constantly observe the process of creation through the natural progressive function and the process of annihilation through the regressive function.” (SB. 11.20.22)

The BBT purport to this text adds: “One who has not achieved the platform of spontaneous Krsna consciousness must remain constantly vigilant so as not to be grossly cheated by the material energy of the Lord.”

Here, Krsna recommends that one should meditate repeatedly on the process of creation and its inverse, annihilation. In this way one will realize the fleeting nature of this world and its pleasures. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura categorizes this text as one for those who want to completely control the mind after having brought it slightly under control.

*Texts 23-24: Controlling the mind completely*

Lord Krsna continues: Those who become disgusted with the material world - and then detached from it - can think again and again about the illusory nature of material existence. Doing so helps them eventually break their false identification with the material body. Through the disciplines of yoga, logical analysis, spiritual knowledge, or through worship and adoration of Krsna (mamarcopasanabhir), and not by other means, these persons should focus the mind on the object of meditation (nanyair yogyam smaren manah).

For the devotees, Krsna is the object of meditation; for others, their focus is dependent on what they want to achieve. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.24, quoting Srila Sridhara Svami to indicate that the desire of the practitioner dictates the process he chooses to follow. “By these methods - and no other - one should remember the Paramatma.”

The BBT purport places Krsna’s recommendations squarely in the context of bhakti-yoga: “\[O\]ne engaged in the worship and adoration of the Personality of Godhead need not trouble himself with the disciplinary, regulatory, and purificatory procedures of yoga, nor with the grueling intricacies of Vedic studies and logic. Yogyam, or the most appropriate object of meditation, is the Supreme Personality of Godhead, as confirmed throughout Vedic literature. One who directly takes to the worship of the Lord should not employ other methods, for full dependence on the Lord is in itself the supreme process of perfection.”

*Texts 25-26: Dealing with falldowns*

*Text 25: Be steadfast on your path*

Krsna now speaks of those practitioners, both the jnana'yogis and the bhaktUyogis, who fall from the standard: “If, because of momentary inattention, a yogi accidentally commits an abominable activity, then by the very practice of yoga he should burn to ashes the sinful reaction, without at any time employing any other procedure.” (SB. 11.20.25)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura cites two additional supportive texts from the Bhagavatam to emphasize the immense purifying potency of bhakti:

“Only a rare person who has adopted complete, unalloyed devotional service to Krsna can uproot the weeds of sinful actions with no possibility that they will revive. He can do this simply by discharging devotional service, just as the sun can immediately dissipate fog by its rays.” (SB. 6.I.15)

And: “One who Iras thus given up all other engagements and has taken full shelter at the lotus feet of Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is very dear to the Lord. Indeed, if such a surrendered soul accidentally commits some sinful activity, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is seated within everyone’s heart, immediately takes away the react ion to such sin." (SB. 11 5.42)

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.25 adds words of caution: “The word yogena here indicates jnanena yogena and bhaktya yogena, since these two transcendental systems have the power to burn sinful reactions to ashes. It should be clearly understood that the word amhas, or ‘sin,’ here refers to an accidental falldown against one’s desire. Premeditated exploitation of the mercy of the Lord can never be excused.”

Nevertheless one should avoid retreating from the bhakti path to take shelter of other processes of atonement. The BBT purport continues: “Significantly, the Lord forbids any extraneous purificatory rites, since the transcendental yoga systems are themselves the most purifying processes, especially bhakti-yoga. If one gives up one’s regular prescribed duties to perform a special ritual or penance, trying to purify a sinful reaction, then one will be guilty of the additional fault of giving up one’s prescribed duties.”

Then what should we do? The BBT purport concludes: “One should pick oneself up from an accidental falldown and go on vigorously with one’s prescribed duties in life without being unnecessarily discouraged. One should certainly lament and feel ashamed, or there will be no purification. However, if one becomes overly depressed at an accidental falldown one will not have the enthusiasm to go on to perfection. Lord Krsna also states \[this\] in the Bhagavad-gita (9.30).”

*Texts 26: Piety and sin*

*Texts 26, Part one: Piety and sin defined*

Next, Krsna defines piety and sin in relation to the performance of the duties prescribed for one’s path: “It is firmly declared that the steady adherence of transcendentalists to their respective spiritual positions constitutes real piety and that sin occurs when a transcendentalist neglects his prescribed duty.” (SB. 11.20.26)

The BBT purport speaks directly to the Supreme Lord’s point: “Lord Krsna here explains more clearly that those persons directly engaged in self-realization either through piana-yoga or bhakti-yoga need not give up their regular duties and perform special penances to atone for an accidental falldown— To purify an accidental falldown, one who is engaged in transcendental realization need not adopt any procedure beyond bis own spiritual practice.”

*Text 26, Part two: The results*

Krsna continues to describe the results of acceptance and acting on the standard of piety and sin He has just established: “One who adopts this standard of piety and sin, sincerely desiring to give up all past association with sense gratification \[sanganam tyajanecchaya\], is able to subdue materialistic activities, which are by nature impure.”

The BBT purport explains that “the words sanganam tyajanecchaya indicate that one should not practice Krsna consciousness or self- realization superficially or casually; rather, one should sincerely and earnestly desire freedom from one’s past sinful life.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura quotes sastra to distinguish between karma, jnana, and bhakti. He explains that good and bad, sin and piety, exist in both jnanis and karmis according to whether or not they follow their individual paths properly. He also explains that the jnanis are both similar to and different from the bhaktas - similar in that “There should be no inclination for sin in the jnani or the devotee, but if by fate it occurs, sin is destroyed by those processes themselves, since jnana and bhakti are purifying by their very nature. Thus the Vedas generally say that the jnani and devotee do not fall within the qualifications of injunction and prohibition, good quality and bad quality.”

Now Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti shifts to the difference: “However, of the two, when the devotee commits sin, everywhere it is said that one should not see it as a fault, or think that the devotee is subject to material gunas, since it is explained that he is beyond the gunas.”

At the end of the previous chapter, Krsna made the radical statement that there was no need for a more elaborate description of good and had qualities, since to constantly see good and bad is itself a bad quality. “The best quality is to transcend material good and evil.” (SB. 11.19.45) At the beginning of this chapter Uddhava asked Krsna to explain why He would say such a thing, because it appeared nr blur the distinction between good and evil. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Fhakura has now explained this text in a way that answers Uddhava’s question. We can understand from Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti s comment that it’s only possible to transcend material good and evil, sin and piety, in the context of pure devotional service. Krsna will draw this conclusion later in the chapter, in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.36.

The BBT purport to text 26 further stresses the transcendental piety of a pure bhakta: “\[T\]he words yd nistha indicate that one must constantly practice Krsna consciousness. Thus, essential piety is to give up material sense gratification and engage in the loving service of the Lord. One who engages his senses, mind, and intelligence twenty-four hours a day in the Lord’s service is the most pious person, and the Lord personally protects such a surrendered soul.”

*Texts 27-36: The glories of pure devotional service*

*Texts 27-28: The beginning stage*

Previously, the Lord revealed the unrivaled power of bhakti, asserting that bhakti captures and controls the unlimitedly powerful Supreme Personality of Godhead (SB. 11.12.1-2 and SB. 11.14.20). Earlier in this twentieth chapter (text 6), Krsna presented the three accepted processes for spiritual elevation: karma, jnana, and bhakti. Quite appropriately, having just described the practices of karma (texts 9-12) and jnana (texts 18-24), in the next ten texts He gives a concise description of bhakti from beginning to end.

He starts with four characteristics of a beginner on the bhakti path (SB. 11.20.27-28):

1\. “Having awakened faith in the narrations of My glories \[jata-sraddho mat-kathasu\]...” Faith is born from hearing krsna-katha from devotees.

2\. “... being disgusted \[nirvinna\] with all material activities, knowing that all sense gratification leads to misery....” Even beginning bhaktas understand that the engine driving their material activities is sense pleasure, and that sense pleasures inevitably cause them (and others) misery. From the BBT purport to these texts: “The word nirvinna indicates that a sincere devotee, although somewhat entangled in the remnants of sense gratification, is completely disgusted with material life and under no circumstances willingly commits sinful activities.”

3\. but still being unable \[amsvara\] to renounce all sense enjoyment....” Despite their sincere desire to avoid sense pleasure, their conditioned nature overpowers their sincerity. From the BBT purport: “The word anlsvara indicates that because of one’s past sinful activities and bad habits one may not immediately be able to completely extinguish the enjoying spirit. The Lord here encourages such a devotee not to be overly depressed or morose but to remain enthusiastic and to go on with his loving service.”

What should the attitude of such devotees be? Krsna continues: My devotee should remain happy \[pritah\].... ”

Those just rescued from drowning in a turbulent ocean will continue to suffer discomfort. Even though they are now safe, they are still exhausted and water-soaked. Yet they will also be happy, knowing that they are safely on their rescuer’s boat. From the BBT purport: “The word prita indicates that a devotee feels exactly like the son or subject of the Supreme Personality of Godhead and is very attached to his relationship with the Lord.”

4\. “... and worship Me with great faith and conviction \[tato bhajeta mam\].” Their gratitude and strong faith in Krsna evoke in them a determined resolve to serve their Lord. From the BBT purport: “Therefore, although sincerely lamenting occasional lapses into sense enjoyment, he never gives up his enthusiasm to serve Lord Krsna.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes the devotee’s resolve: “Let my attachment for family be destroyed or increase! Let there be millions of obstacles to my worship or let the obstacles be destroyed! Let me go to hell if I have committed offenses by keeping those desires. But I will not give up bhakti. I will not accept karma or jndrxa even if Brahma personally comes and orders me to.”

The inclination toward bhakti is stronger for devotees on this level than their material attachments. Yet they still tend to indulge in sense gratification - and then criticize their indulgence. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti characterizes such a devotee’s mood: “Oh! These material enjoyments cause obstacles for me. They are unfavorable for attaining the feet of the Lord. My oath to give them up is in name only, for after a while I again enjoy them. I criticize them and then enjoy them!”

*Texts 29-30: Purifying the heart of material desires, advanced stages of bhakti*

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that the next two texts answer the question, Does the devotee remain forever “attacked” by enjoyment in the material world? His answer - and Krsna’s answer - is no.

Sri Krsna continues: “When an intelligent person engages constantly in worshiping Me through loving devotional service as described by Me, his heart becomes firmly situated in Me. Thus all material desires within the heart are destroyed. The knot in the heart \[hrdaya-granthi\] is pierced, all misgivings are cut to pieces, and the chain of fruitive actions is terminated when 1 am seen as the Supreme Personality of Godhead.” (SB. 11.20.29-30)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains his categorical “No” above, in his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.29: “It has already been said, sraddhamrta-kathayam me sasvan mad-anukirtanam: he has firm faith in the blissful narration of My sweetest pastimes and constant chanting of My glories (SB. 11.19.20). Worshiping Me by this process of bhakti that I have described, My devotee destroys all the \[material\] desires in his heart. \[This occurs\] since I am situated there. If I am there, sins cannot remain, just as there can be no darkness in a place where the sun is shining.”

It is the one-pointed focus on worshiping Krsna in a devotee’s consciousness that fully cleanses his heart. The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.29 describes this devotional process wonderfully: “A devotee of the Lord situates Sri Krsna on a beautiful throne within his heart and there offers the Lord constant service. Just as the rising sun gradually eliminates all trace of darkness, the Lord’s presence within the heart causes all material desires there to weaken and eventually disappear.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes in his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.20.30 that a devotee does not achieve perfection by his own power: “After the devotee passes through the stages of nistha, ruci, and asakti, ahankara (the hrdaya-granthih) is destroyed. This takes place on its own, not with the endeavor or desire of the devotee.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura then offers two sastric quotations to show that bhakti destroys all karma, even the karma one is currently suffering (prarabdha-karma): “Bhakti, devotional service, dissolves the subtle body of the living entity without separate effort, just as fire in the stomach digests all that we eat.” (SB. 3.25.33)

And, “Devotional service is the process of worshiping the Supreme Lord. It consists of fixing one’s mind on Him by becoming disinterested in all material designations, both in this life and the next. Bhakti destroys all karmas.” (Gopala-tapani Upanisad 1.15)

*Texts 31-33: Bhakti compared to other paths*

The Supreme Personality of Godhead continues His glorification of the superiority of bhakti: “Krsna’s bhakta, whose mind is fixed on Him, generallydoes not need to make a separate endeavor for jnana or vairagya to achieve the highest perfection.

In the Krsna Sandarbha (anuccheda 164), Srila Jiva Govami notes that devotees give up attempts at jnana. He offers Brahma’s words in Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.14.3to substantiate his assertion. He also quotes Srimad-Bhagavatam 6.17.28to show that devotees see liberation and heavenly enjoyment as hell, and Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.15.48to show that devotees who have realized the Lord do not view the attainment of impersonal liberation as the Lord’s mercy.

Sri Krsna continues: Devotional service is sufficient to award him the results desired by practitioners of all other processes (fruitive activities, penance, knowledge, detachment, mystic yoga, charity, religious duties, and all other means of perfecting life). If somehow or other (kathahcit) My devotee wants promotion to heaven, liberation, or residence in My abode, he easily achieves such benedictions.

The BBT purports and the acaryas’ comments on these texts underscore still further the greatness of bhakti. The BBT purport to text 11, for example, explains Krsna’s mood in declaring that devotees don’t need processes external to bhakti: “Devotional service to Lord Krsna, being itself the supreme transcendental process, never depends upon the secondary methods involving the cultivation of knowledge and renunciation. By chanting and hearing the glories of the Personality of Godhead a devotee automatically realizes all knowledge, and as the devotee’s attachment to the Lord increases, he automatically gives up attachment for the inferior material nature… Although a sincere devotee has surrendered heart and soul in loving service to the Lord, there may he lingering material attachments that prevent the devotee from perfectly realizing transcendental knowledge. Devotional service, however, will automatically eradicate such lingering attachments in due course of time. If the devotee tries to purify himself through cultivation of knowledge and renunciation, which fall outside the scope of devotional service, there is danger of his being deviated from the Lord’s lotus feet and falling down completely from the transcendental path.”

Only bhakti has the power to remove the soul’s primary material covering, the false ego, or ahankara, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains in his comment on text 31: “Since the knot in the heart is destroyed only by bhakti, which gives no credence to other methods, My devotees should not practice jnana and vairagya, since they neither nourish bhakti nor destroy ahankara and therefore do not benefit the devotee. For a person whose mind is fixed in Me (mad-atmanah), neither jnana, which differentiates self from body, nor vairagya, which renounces enjoyment, is beneficial. Rather, they belong to sattva-guna. Bhakti is beyond the gunas. It is therefore a fault to bring in jnana and vairagya when bhakti is present. Just as attachment and hatred are functions of avidya, jnana and vairagya are functions of vidya. Although jnana and vairagya are natural to bhakti, only bhakti is victorious in destroying ahankara… Moreover, jnana in the form of realization of the Lord, and vairagya in the form of distaste for material enjoyment, both beyond the gunas since they arise from bhakti, appear naturally in bhakti (SB. 11.2.42).'”

To show the power of bhakti and to establish its superiority over all other processes Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes Lord Brahma (SB. 10.14-4):“My dear Lord, devotional service unto You is the best path for self-realization. If someone gives up that path and engages in the cultivation of speculative knowledge, he will simply undergo a troublesome process and will not achieve his desired result. As a person who beats an empty husk of wheat cannot get grain, one who simply speculates cannot achieve self-realization. His only gain is trouble.” (Tattva Sandarbha, anuccheda 46)

*Texts 34-35: Krsna’s devotees want nothing other than to serve Him*

Despite Krsna’s willingness to fulfill any desire His devotees may have, Krsna’s devotees desire nothing for themselves, not even liberation. All they desire is to serve Him, and that desire is firmly fixed in their hearts. Krsna tells us more about 11 is devotees’ consciousness: “Because My devotees possess saintly behavior and deep intelligence, they completely dedicate themselves to Me and do not desire anything besides Me. Indeed, even if I offer them liberation from birth and death, they do not accept it.” (SB. 11.20.34)

In text 33, Krsna said, svargapavargam mad-dhama kathancid yadi vanchati: “If somehow or other My devotee desires promotion to heaven, liberation, or residence in My abode, he easily achieves such benedictions.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that text 33 elucidates Krsna’s use of the word kathancit, “somehow or other.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti adds, “Those who are pure devotees do not desire these things. Rather, people should seek out priti \[loving service\] at all times, since that is the supreme goal of life.”

*Texts 35: A prerequisite for exalted devotional consciousness*

Krsna continues to describe His devotees’ purity: “It is said that complete detachment is the highest stage of freedom. Therefore, one who has no personal desire and does not pursue personal rewards can achieve loving devotional service unto Me.” (SB. 11.20.35)

Only offerings made with pure affection truly please Krsna. After all, Krsna doesn’t need anything from us, because He is already the totality of existence - everything is already His. The BBT purport solaces the fallen souls of Kali-yuga: “ A person who has broader intelligence, whether he be full of all material desire, without any material desire, or desiring liberation, must by all means worship the supreme whole, the Personality of Godhead.’ (SB. 2.3.10) In this statement by Sukadeva Gosvami, the words tivrena bhakti-yogena are very significant. Srila Prabhupada remarks in this regard, ‘As the unmixed sun ray is very forceful and is therefore called tivra, similarly, unmixed bhakti-yoga of hearing, chanting, etc., may be performed by one and all regardless of inner motive.’ Undoubtedly, in this Age of Kali people are generally very fallen and polluted by material lust, greed, anger, lamentation, and so forth. In this age most people are sarva-kama, or full of material desires. Still we must understand that simply by taking shelter of Lord Krsna we will achieve everything in life.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that one who desires only lo serve Krsna and who does not depend on other process, such as jnana and vairagya, attains bhakti for Krsna.

*Text 36: Krsna answers Uddhava’s question directly*

At the end of the previous chapter, in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.19.45, Krsna spoke of seeing good and bad, pious and impious, as a fault. Uddhava questioned this statement in texts 1-5 of this twentieth chapter, as already noted. Now the Lord will reply to Uddhava’s query directly: “Material piety and sin, which arise from the good and evil of this world, cannot exist within My unalloyed devotees, who, being free from material hankering, maintain steady spiritual consciousness in all circumstances. Indeed, such devotees have achieved Me, the Supreme Lord, who am beyond anything that can be conceived by material intelligence.” (SB. 11.20.36)

Good or bad, pious or impious - Krsna’s devotees are transcendental, no longer controlled by the dualities in this world. Their devoted hearts focus only on pleasing Him. Krsna asserted this at the end of the previous chapter (guna-dosa-drsir doso gunas tubhaya-varjitah - the piety and impiety of this world falls within the realm of the actions and reactions of the three modes of material nature). Distinctions between material good and bad are relative, not absolute, and that which is good today may be bad tomorrow; that which is heroic in one culture may be horrific in another. Absolute goodness is centered on Krsna’s pleasure, and regardless of how this world judges things, pleasing the Supreme Absolute Truth is always absolutely true and good. Krsna is forever the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and the pure desire to act solely for His pleasure is the natural consciousness of every soul.

But can we criticize this principle for being easily misused or misapplied? After all, world history is filled with reprehensible actions justified by an “It’s for God’s pleasure.”

Because it’s true that those with impure motives can misquote and misuse truth, just as a surgeon with ill motives can easily slash an innocent’s throat, great care should be taken to ensure that only qualified persons wield such powerful words. As a general rule, therefore, devotees scrupulously act according to the standards of what is considered good and bad in the world but, as Arjuna’s fighting in the Battle of Kuruksetra proves, not at the cost of neglecting actions that truly please Krsna.

The opening paragraph of the BBT purport to text 36 provides a complete perspective:

The words buddheh param indicate that the material modes of nature cannot be found within a pure devotee absorbed in the transcendental qualities of the Lord. In the second chapter of the Bhagavad-gita Lord Krsna clearly explains that a pure devotee is recognized by complete detachment from personal desire; therefore, a pure devotee who is constantly engaged in selfless service to Lord Krsna may not always observe the innumerable details of Vedic rituals and regulations. Such occasional negligence is not to be considered a transgression— However, just as an ordinary person should not falsely claim the executive privileges of the personal assistants of a national leader, similarly, an ordinary conditioned soul may not foolishly claim that his immoral, whimsical, or speculative activities are sheltered by divine right, being the will of God. One must actually be a pure devotee of the Lord, empowered by the Lord Himself and completely surrendered to the will of the Lord, before one may be accepted as transcendental to ordinary piety and sin.

When Krsna tells us that there’s no need to consider good and bad qualities and that it’s better to transcend material good and evil, He is speaking of an absolute principle applicable to those on the absolute platform. Viewed from the absolute platform, both material “good” and material “had” are bad. As Sri Caitanya-caritamrta (Antya 4.176) states, “In the material world, conceptions of good and bad are all mental speculations. Therefore, saying, ‘This is good, and this is bad,’ is all a mistake.” Srila Prabhupada stressed the same point in a lecture on the Bhagavad- gita, given in 1975:

If you learn this science... the result is you become liberated from this asubha, inauspicious condition of life— What is that inauspicious condition of life? This materialistic life. If you want to get out of this materialistic way.... This is asubha. There is no subha. People are thinking, “We shall make it subha.” Subha means auspicious by material adjustment - by having nice car, nice road, skyscraper building, and so many machine and bodily comforts which is known as material advancement. But the sastra says it is all inauspicious, all inauspicious. If you want to become free from this inauspicious kind of life, then you should learn the science which Krsna is leaching, jfumam *vijuana*, not this *vijnana*, the so-called materialistic science. You should learn the real science, sa-vijnana.

That is how to surrender to Krsna, how to become not envious to Krsna. This is a great science. We have to learn.

Those acting on a more relative platform, whose motivations for action spring from something less than “purely for the pleasure of Krsna,” should aspire to act in the mode of goodness. This principle also holds true for those souls moving upward toward pure devotional service. They too should generally follow the standard definitions of piety and morality Krsna offered at the end of chapter 19.

One Sunday in 1968, at 26 Avenue in New York City, I asked Srila Prabhupada my first question. It was just after his Sunday Feast lecture, and in that lecture he had stated that devotees were in the mode of goodness. I asked him whether devotees were in the mode of goodness or were transcendental. Srila Prabhupada told me that devotees are transcendental, but they generally act in the mode of goodness.

As the BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.13.2 notes: “Srila Madhvacarya points out in this regard that an increase in the mode of goodness strengthens religious principles and the invigorated execution of religious principles strengthens the mode of goodness. In that way, one can advance higher and higher in the mode of spiritual happiness.”

But despite the fact that the devotees’ actions are “generally” in goodness, they are not bound to act in goodness. Their priority is to please Krsna. To instruct us on this point, Yudhisthira Maharaja hesitated to lie on Krsna’s order and had to visit hell because he transgressed dharma (Mahabharata, Drona Parva, chapter 10). A devotee will do anything to give Krsna pleasure, something demonstrated perfectly by Krsna’s topmost devotees, the Vraja gopikas. Thus exalted devotees transcend even limited, material goodness in service to their devotion to the unlimited Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Nevertheless, they “generally” act in goodness.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comments reveal Krsna’s mind as He concludes this topic: “I have said guna-dosa-drsir doso gunas tubhayct-varjitah, to see good and bad is itself a bad quality, and thus the best quality is to transcend seeing good and had qualities (SB. 11.19.45).

This ‘best quality’ resides in My devotees… Siva describes how the devotees see equally (sama-cittanam): ‘Devotees solely engaged in the devotional service of Narayana never fear any condition of life. For them the heavenly planets, liberation, and the hellish planets are all the same.’ (SB. 6.17.28)”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura ends his comment on this text in this way: “What to speak of seeing material faults in the perfect devotees who have attained the Lord by bhakti, one should not find fault even in the sadhakas who commit sins: ‘But those who always worship Me with exclusive devotion, meditating on My transcendental form - to them I carry what they lack and preserve what they have’ (Bhagavad-gita 9.22).”

*Text 37: Summary of the results of different paths*

Krsna concludes this chapter with a summary: “Persons who seriously follow these methods of achieving Me, which I have personally taught, attain freedom from illusion, and upon reaching My personal abode they perfectly understand the Absolute Truth.” (SB. 11.20.37)

In the Bhagavata Sandarbha (anuccheda 72), Srila Jiva Gosvami discusses karma and jnana in relation to attaining Krsna’s lotus feet through bhakti: “Those who follow My paths - the ways of attaining Me through jnana, karma, and bhakti - attain My abode. This means that in the beginning of its practice, bhakti sometimes takes a little help from karma and jnana. The bhaktas attain My abode, which is auspicious for bhakti. They know this place as the Supreme Brahman.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura speaks potent words to conclude his own comments on the twentieth chapter of the Eleventh Canto: “Unrestricted sense gratification, fruitive activities, and mental speculation cannot be the ultimate religion for the living entities. Since these things are born from aversion to the Lord’s service they are temporary and incomplete. The devotees who follow the Lord’s instructions become liberated from the clutches of all inauspiciousness by accepting the path of devotional service.
