But the master of the atmaramas, the Supreme Lord, can do this, because He has the greatest powers to free me.”

The serpent Kaliya made a similar prayer when he asked Krsna to remove his inborn sinful disposition: “O Supreme Personality of Godhead, among all the species within Your material creation, we serpents are by nature always enraged. Being thus deluded by Your illusory energy, which is very difficult to give up, how can we possibly give it up on our own?” (SB. 10.16.58)

Ultimately, as described in Canto Eleven, chapter 25, the modes of nature rule the material world on Krsna’s order. Nothing but surrender to and the merciful disposition of the controller of the modes can release us from the modes’ murderous embrace. As Krsna says in the Bhagavad-gita (7.14), “This divine energy of Mine, consisting of the three modes of material nature, is difficult to overcome. But those who have surrendered unto Me can easily cross beyond it.”

*Texts 16-17: Aila accepts responsibility for having become degraded*

“Because I allowed my intelligence to become dull and because I failed to control my senses, the great confusion in my mind did not go away, even though Urvasi herself gave me wise counsel with well- spoken words.” (SB. 10.26.16)

Urvasi’s “well-spoken words,” the BBT purport explains, were her admonishment to Aila to “never trust women or believe their promises.” The BBT purport continues: “Despite this frank advice, he became fully attached and thus suffered great mental anguish.” Urvasi criticized women as a class in Srimad-Bhagavatam 9.14.36—38. Throughout this Eleventh Canto chapter of the Bhagavatam, the two most significant words Aila uses when referring to Urvasi are stri and purhscalya. Stri means “wife,” “the bearer of one’s children,” or “female.” Stri, as Srila Prabhupada explains in several places, refers to one who “expands” by creating or pushing one to acquire more things - children, home, things to fill the home, and money. Ultimately, then, stri means “one who increases one’s affection for the material world.’”Purhscalya means “prostitute,” or a woman who moves from one man to another.

Emperor Aila now confronts the issue squarely: “How can I blame her for my trouble when I myself am ignorant of my real, spiritual nature? I did not control my senses, and so I am like a person who mistakenly sees a harmless rope as a snake.” (SB. 11.26.17)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura documents Aila’s change in attitude: “I previously said that my discrimination had been stolen by a prostitute. But now I do not blame her. What wicked act has she done to me? None. What harm can a rope do to a person who thinks it a snake? No harm at all. Only an ignorant person will find fault with the rope, which he fears out of ignorance. Since I have uncontrolled senses, I have lived with this type of illusion.”

Although Maharaja Pururava had accused Urvasi of being a thief and turning him into a fool, he now condemns only himself; he understands that ignorance was his only enemy. So the king withdraws his “charges” against Urvasi and shoulders the responsibility for having created his lamentable situation.

Yet despite the fact that Aila accepts his fault, it is still important to acknowledge that although the chemistry that sparks the desire for sex between men and women is natural, it is not innocent, because it is based on the ignorance of accepting the body as the self. Sex is ex- ploitative because both men and women are primarily interested in their own pleasure, and it is painful because once the fleeting pleasure recedes, each participant is left alone under the crushing wheel of samsara. Therefore despite the natural attraction between men and women, both men and women have to take responsibility for their actions and protect themselves from ignorance.

Dealings between conditioned souls are the play of may a, which is powered by the three modes of material nature. If we wish to make real change at the deepest levels of our being, we’ll have to get at the heart of the false ego: our aversion to Krsna. This aversion can only be cured by surrendering to Krsna as His eternal servant in the form of guru. By following the guru’s instructions to serve Krsna, hear about Krsna, and chant about Krsna, one’s aversion is reversed and attraction to Him is gradually developed. One thus turns toward Krsna and His service. Finally realizing the need for such deep change, Pururava, Aila, makes a decisive move to rectify his consciousness.

*Texts 18-21: The illusion of the attractive material body*

Pururava marvels at the power of the Lord’s maya, because it causes a material body, which he now recognizes as repugnance thinly veiled by skin, to appear alluring. “What is this polluted body anyway - so filthy and full of bad odors? I was attracted by the fragrance and beauty of a woman’s body, but what are those so-called attractive features? They are simply a false covering created by illusion.” (SB. 11.26.18)

Aila next notes that his desire to possess Urvasi as “his own” enjoy- able object was founded on another illusion: ignorance of who actually owns the body - anyone’s body. Aila continues: “One can never decide whose property the body actually is. Does it belong to one’s parents, who have given birth to it, to one’s wife, who gives it pleasure, or to one’s employer, who orders the body around? Is it the property of the funeral fire or of the dogs and jackals who may ultimately devour it? Is it the property of the indwelling soul, who partakes in its happiness and distress, or does the body belong to intimate friends who encourage and help it? Although a man never definitely ascertains the proprietor of the body, he becomes most attached to it. The material body is a polluted material form heading toward a lowly destination,yet when a man stares at the face of a woman he thinks, ‘What a good-looking lady! What a charming nose she’s got, and see her beautiful smile!”’ (SB. 11.26.19—20)

Aila condemns himself further by asking: “What difference is there between ordinary worms and persons who try to enjoy this material body composed of skin, flesh, blood, muscle, fat, marrow, bone, stool, urine, and pus?” (SB. 11.26.21)

*Text 22: A theoretical understanding alone provides insufficient protection*

Maya can easily overwhelm one’s knowledge with her dazzling sparkle, so “even one who theoretically understands the actual nature of the body should never associate with women or with men attached to women. After all, the contact of the senses with their objects inevitably agitates the mind.”

Acknowledging this truth, Caitanya Mahaprabhu instructs Sanatana Gosvami: “A Vaisnava should always avoid the association of ordinary people. Common people are very much materially attached, especially to women. Vaisnavas should also avoid the company of those who are not devotees of Lord Krsna.” (Sri Caitanya-caritamria, Madhya 22.87) Srila Prabhupada acknowledges the issue and stresses the solution in his purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.2.17:

Women and wealth are very difficult problems for the devotee making progress on the path back to Godhead. Many stalwarts in the devotional line fell victim to these allurements and thus retreated from the path of liberation. But when one is helped by the Lord Himself, the whole process becomes as easy as anything by the divine grace of the Lord. To become restless in the contact of women and wealth is not an astonishment, because every living being is associated with such things from remote time, practically immemorial, and it takes time to recover from this foreign nature. But if one is engaged in hearing the glories of the Lord, gradually he realizes his real position. By the grace of God such a devotee gets sufficient strength to defend himself from the state of disturbances, and gradually all disturbing elements are eliminated from his mind.

In a room conversation in London on September 2, 1973, Prabhupada adds: “The prescribed methods are there. We have to adopt it. Without adopting the prescribed method, nobody can advance. But in this age the prescribed method is very simple: simply to hear the holy name of the Lord - harer nama eva kevalam kalau nasty eva nasty eva nasty eva gatir anyatha.”

*Text 23: Out of sight, out of mind*

Aila continues: “Because the mind is not disturbed by that which is neither seen nor heard, the mind of a person who restricts the material senses will automatically be checked in its material activities and become pacified.” (SB. 11.26.23)

Wherever I go, my wayward mind follows me. Does simply restricting the material senses work? The BBT purport to text 23 answers this doubt: “It may be argued that even while closing one’s eyes, while dreaming, or while living in a solitary place, one may remember or contemplate sense gratification. Such an experience, however, is due to previous sense gratification that one repeatedly saw and heard about. When one restricts the senses from their objects, especially from intimate contact with women, the mind’s material propensity will slacken and, like a fire without fuel, eventually die.”

*Text 24: Aila concludes*

Aila’s conclusion opposes the trends and habits of modern life: “Therefore one should never let his senses associate freely with women or with men attached to women. Even those who are highly learned cannot trust the six enemies of the mind; what to speak, then, of foolish persons like me.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s terse comment underscores the essence of Aila’s concluding words: “The five senses and the mind are untrustworthy.”

*Text 25: Emperor Pururava acts according to his realization*

“Having thus chanted this song, Maharaja Pururava, eminent among the demigods and human beings, gave up the position he had achieved in the planet of Urvasi. His illusion cleansed away by transcendental knowledge, he understood Me to be the Supreme Soul within his heart and so at last achieved peace.” (SB. 11.26.25)

Thus Aila gave up the Gandharva body he had previously attained as he renounced Urvasi’s planet.Somehow, somewhere, Aila had managed to learn spiritual knowledge, but it had been stolen away during his association with Urvasi. His previous understanding now returned and, as Krsna told Uddhava, “he understood Me to be the Supreme Soul within his heart.”

*Texts 26-34: What to do once one knows what not to do*

After His dramatic recitation of Aila’s song, Lord Krsna offers Uddhava some further guidance: remain in the association of good devotees (texts 26-27); know that devotee association has a powerful effect on the consciousness (texts 28-29); the greatest attainment is service to Krsna (text 30); and serving devotees removes the obstacles to spiritual advancement, shelters one from suffering, offers one refuge, and grants one spiritual vision (texts 31-34).

*Texts 26-27: Good association*

**Keep yourself in Vaisnava association**

“An intelligent person should therefore reject all bad association and instead take up the association of saintly devotees, whose words cut off the excessive attachment of one’s mind \[mano-vyasangam\]. (SB. 11.26.26)

**The characteristics of devotees**

“My devotees fix their minds on Me and do not depend upon anything material. They are always peaceful, endowed with equal vision, and free from possessiveness, false ego, duality, and greed.” (SB. 11.26.27)

In his comment on text 26, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura emphasizes each element in Krsna’s words defining the exalted qualities of His devotees: “Only the devotees can cut excessive and dangerous material attachment. Pious acts, visiting holy places, worshiping deva- tas, and knowledge of scripture cannot cut material attachments to the same extent. ‘Who are these devotees? What words do they speak to award auspiciousness?’ These two verses answer those questions. These devotees do not depend on karma, jnana, the devatas, human beings, or others for their personal gain. If someone objects, Well, they do not depend on You, the Lord, either?’ Krsna answers, ‘Their minds are fixed on Me alone.’ Objection: ‘But Karhsa and others also concentrated their minds on You.’ Krsna: ‘But My devotees are \[different; they are\] peaceful and without anger.’ ‘Can they remain without anger even if someone hates them?’ ‘They see friends, enemies, and neutral parties as the same, for they have conquered ahankara - they have no false sense of self and no sense of possessiveness. Thus they remain as calm when they are praised as when they are disrespected.’ ‘But can they see even their wife and sons in the same equal way?’ ‘They have given up all attachment. Such persons are My devotees.’ ”

*Texts 28-29: The potent effect of devotee association*

**These great souls speak always of Krsna**

“O greatly fortunate Uddhava, in the association of such saintly devotees there is constant discussion of Me, and those partaking in this chanting and hearing of My glories are certainly purified of all sins.” (SB. 11.26.28)

**The result of hearing about Krsna in the devotees’ association**

“Whoever hears, chants and respectfully takes to heart these topics about Me becomes faithfully dedicated to Me and thus achieves My devotional service.” (SB. I 1.26.29)

*Text 30: Devoted service to Krsna is the greatest attainment*

“What more remains to be accomplished for the perfect devotee after achieving devotional service unto Me, the Supreme Absolute Truth, whose qualities are innumerable and who am the embodiment of all ecstatic experience?” (SB. 11.26.30)

Krsna’s name, form, qualities, pastimes, and personality are supremely delectable. Those who associate with Krsna’s exalted devotees will hear krsna-katha, because exalted devotees are always speaking it. Those who hear this katha will be purified, and those who continue to hear it will become attracted to Krsna and ultimately attain love for Him. By the power of one’s love for Krsna, one attracts Krsna’s mercy and ultimately His association. The association of devotees is supremely valuable.

Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.25.25states, “In the association of pure devotees, discussion of the pastimes and activities of the Supreme Personality of Godhead is very pleasing and satisfying to the ear and the heart. By cultivating such knowledge one gradually becomes advanced on the path of liberation, and thereafter he is freed, and his attraction becomes fixed. Then real devotion and devotional service begin.’’

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura comments that instead of becoming involved with the Mayavada path, whoever engages in hearing and chanting the topics of Lord Hari and gives complete respect to the philosophy embedded in those topics — that Lord Hari is the ultimate, conclusive, philosophical truth — understanding in particular that the practice of devotional service is the sole duty of the living being, will become free from all false trust in things separate from Krsna and attain the service of the Personality of Godhead. Nothing else remains to be achieved for such a devotee. To forego serving the objects of enjoyment manufactured by the modes of nature and instead accept servitude under the Absolute Truth, who possesses unlimited transcendental qualities, is the symptom of having attained great fortune.

*Texts 31—34: The glories of Vaisnava association*

*Text 31: Serving devotees removes obstacles to spiritual advancement*

“Just as cold, fear, and darkness are eradicated for one who has approached the sacrificial fire, so dullness, fear, and ignorance art destroyed for one engaged in serving the devotees of the Lord.” (SB. 11.26.31)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “When one uses fire for cooking, cold, fear, and darkness are also destroyed as a secondary result. In the same way, when one serves devotees in order to perfect one’s own worship, the stupefying influence of karma, the fear of samsara, and the obstacles to worship are also destroyed.”

*Text 32: Devotees shelter those who are suffering in material existence*

“The devotees of the Lord, peacefully fixed in absolute knowledge, are the ultimate shelter for those who are repeatedly rising and falling within the fearful ocean of material life. Such devotees are just like a strong boat that comes to rescue persons who are at the point of drowning.” (SB. 11.26.32)

Krsna compares material existence to a deep, dangerous ocean in which each conditioned soul must drown. Serving Krsna in the association of devotees secures us a place on the most suitable boat for crossing that ocean. Because devotees are themselves sheltered on the boat of Krsna’s lotus feet, their shelter is Krsna. So devotees both provide the means for others to cross the ocean and are themselves the means. The demigods make a similar point in Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.2.30-31: “O lotus-eyed Lord, by concentrating one’s meditation on Your lotus feet, which are the reservoir of all existence, and by accepting those lotus feet as the boat by which to cross the ocean of nescience, one follows in the footsteps of mahajanas. By this simple process, one can cross the ocean of nescience as easily as one steps over the hoofprint of a calf.... When acaryas completely take shelter under Your lotus feet in order to cross the fierce ocean of nescience, they leave behind on earth the method by which they cross, and because You are very merciful to Your other devotees, You accept this method to help them.”

*Text 33: Devotees are the only refuge*

“Just as food is the life of all creatures, just as I am the ultimate shelter for the distressed, and just as religion is the wealth of those who are passing away from this world, so My devotees are the only refuge of persons fearful of falling into a miserable condition of life.” (SB. I 1.26.33)

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura fills out Krsna’s comparison: “Just as food is the life force (prana) of those living entities who are in need of food - since without food the body’s vital airs cannot function - so for those who desire to attain devotional service, the devotees are devotional service itself, because without them devotional service cannot be perfected. Just as for those who are distressed, who have no protector, I alone am the shelter and the protector, so for those who desire to attain devotional service, the devotees alone are the protectors. And just as for men who have died and are fearful of the noose of time, religion alone is the wealth and the shelter, so for persons who are in the process of attaining devotional service and are afraid that the nooses of lust and anger will catch them and drag them here and there, the devotees are their only protectors, their only shelter.”

*Text 34: Devotees grant accurate, spiritual vision*

Devotees should be our intimates because devotees are nondifferent from their Lord: “My devotees bestow divine eyes, whereas the sun allows only external sight, and that only when it is risen in the sky. My devotees are one’s real worshipable deities and real family; they are one’s own self, and ultimately they are nondifferent from Me.” (SB. 11.26.34)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura underscores Krsna’s words: “\[F\]or those who have dedicated themselves to the path of the devotees, the devotees bestow all things necessary. The devotees give the eyes to see Me directly. This means that they give the nine types of worship. The eyes cannot fulfill their functions without the sun. The devotees, situated externally, give the means to worship Me. They are like the perfectly risen sun; their illumination allows us to see. The devotees alone, and not Indra and others, are worthy of worship for those treading the path of bhakti. The devotees alone, and not one’s parents or relatives, are one’s friends. The devotees alone, and not the body or one’s own atma, are the objects of love. The devotees alone are Me, the Supreme Deity. One should not give them up and worship only Me in My form as the Deity in the temple.”

*Text 35: Pururava acts!*

“Thus losing his desire to be on the same planet as Urvasi, Maharaja Pururava began to wander the earth free of all material association and completely satisfied within the self.” (SB. 11.26.35)

Both Sridhara Svami and Jiva Gosvami concur that this text sums up the point of chapter 26, the Aila-gita.

**Chapter 27: Lord Krsna’s Instructions on the Process of Deity Worship**

*Texts 1-5: Uddhava asks about and then glorifies Deity worship*

Uddhava says to Sri Krsna: “My dear Lord, O master of the devotees, please explain to me the prescribed method of worshiping You in Your Deity form. What are the qualifications of those devotees who worship the Deity, on what basis is such worship established, and what is the specific method of worship? All the great sages repeatedly declare that such worship brings the greatest benefit possible in human life. This is the opinion of Narada Muni, the great Vyasadeva, and my own spiritual master, Brhaspati.” (SB. 11.27.1-2)

Uddhava’s question begins, kriya-yogam samacaksva: please explain the yoga of activity. But he quickly names the particularly uplifting activity he wants to hear about: bhavad'dradhanam, worshiping You, Krsna, in the form of Your Deity.

Uddhava then goes on to describe that a number of great sages also speak of the value of Deity worship. Srila Jiva Gosvami emphasizes in the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 183) that Deity worship (arcana) is meant for everyone. There, Sri Jiva mentions that arcana is required for householders, but that all initiated devotees should practice it, or at least witness others worshiping the Deities.

Sri Uddhava concludes his question: “O lotus-eyed one, O Supreme Lord of all lords of the universe, please explain to Your devoted servant this means of liberation from the bondage of work.” (SB. 11.27.5)

At this specific point in the Uddhava'gita, one wonders why Uddhava is asking Krsna to describe Deity worship. Krsna has just spoken about Maharaja Aila’s suffering and finally becoming detached from Urvasi. In addition to Aila’s decision to stop seeking pleasure in the temporary, the king also needs to become attached to the spiritual, eternal aspects of reality. The temporary may fill all conditioned souls with frust ration and pain, but renunciation is an act of negation. One cannot simply give up the negative without doing something life-giving. Spiritual attachment is a positive act. So Uddhava asks Krsna to speak about Deity worship, because Deity worship makes becoming spiritually advanced easier to achieve, especially for those who are still struggling with material attachment.

Here are four excerpts from letters Srila Prabhupada wrote in 1968 to encourage his disciples to perform Deity worship:

Deity worship should be practiced by everyone. That cleanses the contaminated body very nicely.

\[T\]he more we are engaged in decorating the Deities, washing the room, the more we are engaged in Deity worship, the more we become purified. That is practical.

You have already stated in your letter, it is very nice, that you would much prefer to channel all your desires to Krishna, and you ask me how is this possible when enveloped in maya, seeing only material forms. You have also written to say that if you can see the Absolute Beauty, which is all-attractive, then you could not help but be attracted and would scorn mundane beauty. This is actually the remedy. So you may take immediately to the arcana, the Deity worship.

Decorate the Deity as nicely as possible with nice flowers and dress.

You will forget all other false beauty.

Srila Sridhara Svami also introduces Uddhava’s questions in his comment on these texts: “Uddhava, wondering how those whose minds are agitated by lust and other such disturbances become free from material association, remembers the auspicious process of worshiping Lord Krsna in His Deity form and therefore asks the Lord about it. Sridhara Svami also notes that Uddhava has thus far heard of processes for those who hope to become free of material association, and he now inquires how even those who don’t want such freedom can be transformed so that they may achieve the highest goal of life.

Srila Jiva Gosvami notes another reason why Uddhava asks about Deity worship at this point in his conversation with Krsna. He explains that the process of advancement (through detachment) described in Canto Eleven, chapter 26, is based on saintly association, which is difficult to achieve for those attached to children, wife, and so on. “Therefore, Uddhava inquires about the process of bhakti consisting of Deity worship, which has been spoken of in sastra, with the desire of delivering such attached persons.”

Srila Prabhupada also described Deity worship and the purpose behind it in a lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 7.9.40, which he gave in Mayapur in 1976:

When we forget Krsna, then He comes to convince us that “this is not good. You are trying to satisfy your senses. It will never end. Simply you’ll be implicated from one body to another for satisfying your senses, sometimes eating stool also— Better just surrender unto Me, and what I say, you do. Just begin your service. Surrender. Give Me something eatable.” Patrarh puspam phalam toy am, yo me bhaktya prayacchati. This is the beginning. The Deity worship is the beginning of devotional service.

Therefore arcana, Deity worship, is very essential. Everyone should try. The system is: anyone comes to the temple, he brings something - patram puspam phalam toy am - just to offer to the Deity. It is the beginning. That is the beginning of love, dadati: give something. Dadati pratigrhnati bhunkte bhojayate caiva. This is the beginning of love. If I love you, I must give you something, and whatever you’ll give me I shall accept it. So give something to Krsna and take His instruction. This is the beginning of love. Therefore the Deity is there. The instruction is here. If people take advantage, automatically he becomes a devotee, a lover of Krsna. That is the success of life.

*Texts 6-9: Sri Krsna replies - introduction to Deity worship*

There are unlimited prescriptions to follow while worshiping the Deity, Sri Krsna says, “so I shall explain this topic to you briefly, one step at a time.” (SB. 11.27.6) Krsna starts with the three basic methodologies one can apply while worshiping the Deity: vaidika (sacrifices performed with mantras, such as the Purusa-sukta, and according to the four Vedas and their auxlilary texts), tantrika (sacrifices performed according to the practical, explanatory texts, such as the Pancaratras and Gautamiya-tantra), and misra (a prescribed mixture of these two, such as the use of the eight-syllable mantra prescribed in both the Vedic literatures and the tantras).

Krsna suggests we listen faithfully as He explains exactly how a person who has achieved twice-born status through the relevant Vedic prescriptions should worship Him with devotion (bhaktya). Whether the Deity’s form appears on the ground, as the fire, sun, water, or in the worshiper’s heart, the devotee should make appropriate offerings without deception (amayaya), simply for the pleasure of his worshipable Lord, with loving devotion (bhakti-yukto ’rcet).

*Texts 10-18: Foundational principles of Deity worship*

In nine texts Krsna describes the foundational processes one worshiping a Deity is required to know. Here are some of the basic principles He mentions. One should cleanse oneself with water, earth, and mantras. One should fix his mind on Krsna and worship Him through his prescribed duties, including sandhya (chanting mantras at the three junctures of the day - morning, noon, and twilight). The Lord can manifest as a Deity in eight forms: stone, wood, metal, earth, paint, sand, the mind, and in jewels. Deities can be established either temporarily or permanently. Only Deities established for a specific period of time or for a specific function can be called and later asked to leave.Deities composed of different substances should be bathed in a way appropriate to the substance of which the Deity is composed. The Deity should be worshiped with the most excellent physical items the worshiper can obtain, but those who are free from material desires can even worship the Deity in the heart using mental paraphernalia.The most pleasing items to offer depend on the type of Deity one is worshiping.

At the end of text 17 and in text 18 Krsna says that it is the worshiper’s bhakti that makes the worship pleasing to Him: “Actually, whatever is offered to Me with faith by My devotee — even if only a little water - is most dear to Me. Even very opulent presentations do not satisfy Me if they are offered by nondevotees. But I am pleased by any insignificant offering made by My loving devotees, and I am certainly most pleased when nice presentations of fragrant oil, incense, flowers, and palatable foods are offered with love.”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 300), Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes texts 17 and 18. He says that the words bhaktena \[the devotee, who has bhakti\] and sraddha \[faith\] that Krsna uses refer to having respect. Srila Jiva continues: “Offenses are filled with disrespect. The offense may be rejecting the Lord’s Lordship or His order. The cause of offense is disrespect, and disrespect should be avoided.”

*Texts 19-47: Procedures in worshiping the Deity*

*Texts 19-43: Practical procedures*

Krsna now describes the practical procedures of Deity worship. Here is a concise list of most of the elements Krsna mentions. Worshipers should be clean, use a seat made of kusa grass, sit and face the Deity directly, sit facing east or north, sanctify the body, cleanse the Deity of old flowers and other previously offered items, sanctify the Deity’s asana and the vessels and other items for the worship by sprinkling water on them and chanting mantras. One should meditate on, worship, and become absorbed in thoughts of Krsna’s form, and then welcome the Lord by offering Him water to wash His feet and mouth along with other items of worship. One should then worship in the proper order the Lord’s Sudarsana disc, Pancajanya conch shell, club, sword, bow and arrows, plow, musala weapon,Kaustubha gem, flower garland, and the Srivatsa on His chest. Then one should worship the Lord’s associates, who should all be facing Him. As opulently as possible, one should bathe the Lord each day, and “lovingly decorate Me with clothing, a brahmana thread, various ornaments, marks of tilaka, and garlands, and he should anoint My body with fragrant oils, all in the prescribed manner.” (SB. 11.27.32)The devotee should then “present Me with water for washing My feet and mouth, fragrant oils, flowers, and unbroken grains, along with incense, lamps, and other offerings.” (SB. 11.27.33)

After this, devotees should offer the Deity appropriate and palatable foods. On special occasions - or daily, if possible - the Deity should be “massaged with ointment, shown a mirror, offered a eucalyptus stick for brushing His teeth, bathed with the five kinds of nectar, offered all kinds of opulent foods, and entertained with singing and dancing.” (SB. 11.27.35)

Devotees should offer the Deity a fire sacrifice while meditating on Him as the Supersoul in the fire. They should meditate on the wonderful details of the Lord’s form and dress, and offer into the fire oblations of ghee. They should also offer oblations to the demigods, while reciting the Purusa-sukta prayers.

Krsna then tells Uddhava how to end the puja: “Having thus worshiped the Lord in the sacrificial fire, the devotee should offer his obeisances to the Lord’s personal associates by bowing down and should then present offerings to them. He should then chant quietly the mula-mantra of the Deity of the Lord, remembering the Absolute Truth as the Supreme Personality, Narayana.” (SB. 11.27.42) Again the worshiper should offer the Lord water to wash His mouth along with fragrant perfume and betel nuts.

*Texts 44-47: Concluding one’s worship*

Concluding His description of the worship, Krsna says: “Singing along with others, chanting loudly and dancing, acting out My transcendental pastimes, and hearing and telling stories about Me, the devotee should for some time absorb himself in such festivity. The devotee should offer homage to the Lord with all kinds of hymns and prayers, both from the Puranas and from other ancient scriptures, and also from ordinary traditions. Praying, ‘O Lord, please be merciful to me!’ he should fall down flat like a rod to offer his obeisances. Placing his head at the feet of the Deity, he should then stand with folded hands before the Lord and pray, ‘O my Lord, please protect me, who am surrendered unto You. I am most fearful of this ocean of material existence, standing as I am in the mouth of death.’” (SB. 11.27.44-46) At the end of the pitja, the devotee should place the Lord’s remnants on his head.

*Text 48: Which form of the Lord should one worship?*

“Whenever one develops faith in Me - in My form as the Deity or in other bona fide manifestations - one should worship Me in that form. I certainly exist both within all created beings and also separately in My original form, since I am the Supreme Soul of all.” (SB. 11.27.48)

In his comment on text 48, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura speaks about the importance of faith: “Although worship of the Deity form has mainly been described here, faith is the cause of My appearing. Without faith, one will not realize My presence in the Deity although I am directly present. Those who are ignorant see Me as matter (virad avidusam, SB. 10.43.17). Thus this verse shows that faith is necessary. To show the principal means of seeing Him, He mentioned the Deity and other forms in this chapter: ‘But if one has great faith, I can be seen in all things. I was easily visible in the pillar in Hiranyakasipu’s palace.’ ”

*Texts 49-53: Results of worshiping the Deity and of supporting such worship*

One who worships using the methods Krsna describes “will gain from Me his desired perfection in both this life and the next.” (SB. 11.27.49)

Krsna now indicates the service religious people with financial resources should offer: “The devotee should more fully establish My Deity by solidly constructing a temple, along with beautiful gardens. These gardens should be set aside to provide flowers for the regular daily worship, special Deity processions, and holiday observances.” (SB. 11.27.50)

By performing Deity worship, those with wealth can make their lives successful: “One who offers the Deity gifts of land, markets, cities, and villages so that the regular daily worship and special festivals of the Deity may go on continually will achieve opulence equal to My own. By installing the Deity of the Lord one becomes king of the entire earth, by building a temple for the Lord one becomes ruler of the three worlds, by worshiping and serving the Deity one goes to the planet of Lord Brahma, and by performing all three of these activities one achieves a transcendental form like My own.” (SB. 11.27.51-52)

*Text 53: The Ultimate result of worshiping the Deity*

The Lord now describes the ultimate result - pure devotional service - of worshiping Him: “But one who simply engages in devotional service \[bhakti-yogena\] with no consideration of fruitive results \[naira-peksyena\] attains Me. Thus whoever worships Me \[yah pujayeta mam\] according to the process I have described will ultimately attain pure devotional service \[bhakti-yogam\] unto Me.” (SB. 11.27.53)

In the Bhakti Saruiarbha (anuccheda 297), Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that Krsna means that one attains Him by unmotivated (nairapeksyena) love (prema-bhakti-yogena). “That prema is the result of worshiping Him.” This truth, Sri Jiva says, is expressed in the second line of text 53: “I le who worships me (yah pujayeta muni) attains prema (bhakti-yogam).”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura adds that one who worships the Lord’s Deity, free from jnana and karma, or who engages others in won ship by accepting their wealth, land, and shops for the Deity s service, attains prema (bhakti-yogam). By that prema (bhakti-yogena), of course, they also attain Krsna Himself.

*Texts 54—55: Disasterous results for those who steal the Deity’s property*

Do not usurp the property of the demigods, brahmanas, Vaisnavas, or the Lord: “Anyone who steals the property of the demigods or the brahmanas, whether originally given to them by himself or someone else, must live as a worm in stool for one hundred million years. Not only the performer of the theft but also anyone who assists him, instigates the crime, or simply approves of it, must also share the reaction in the next life. According to their degree of participation, they each must suffer a proportionate consequence.” (SB. 11.27.54-55) On that somber note, the Lord ends His exposition on Deity worship.

**Chapter 28: Jnana-yoga**

*Texts 1-9: Seeing duality in matter is inaccurate, illusory, and entangling*

Now nearing the end of His instructions to Uddhava, Sri Krsna, who has already spoken from a number of philosophical perspectives, gives a brief synopsis on jnana-yoga, something He has already described in more detail. In his comment on the first text of chapter 28, Srila Jiva Gosvami explains two reasons why Krsna returns to the topic of jnana after speaking so much about bhakti in the previous chapter: “Now, in order to eradicate the tendency of seeing things externally while engaged in devotional service, or, in order to show how devotional service is easy to practice and gives excellent results, it is stated how the process of speculative knowledge and its detailed practice are difficult and do not give such excellent results.”

Both Sri Jiva’s reasons are to the point. First, devotees should examine everything deeply, and Krsna’s presentation of jnana-yoga and how to practice it can help. Second, by presenting jnana-yoga, bhakti-yoga is glorified - both its practice and result. Indeed, Uddhava will later reject jnana for bhakti in the opening texts of the Uddhava-gita’s final chapter (SB. 11.29.1-6).

Because the primary goal of a jnana-yogi is to perceive the oneness of everything in existence, the jnana'yogi should forsake illusion. “Rather, one should see this world as simply the combination of material nature and the enjoying souls, all based on the one Absolute Truth.” (SB. 11.28.1)

The BBT purport explains: “Material situations and activities appear to be good, passionate, or ignorant according to the interaction of the modes of nature. These modes are produced by the illusory potency of the Lord, which is itself not different from its master, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. So a devotee of the Lord remains aloof from the illusory, temporary manifestations of material nature. At the same time, he accepts material nature as the potency of the Lord and thus essentially real. The example may be given that modeling clay is shaped by a child into various playful forms such as tigers, men, or houses. The modeling clay is real, whereas the temporary shapes it assumes are illusory, not being actual tigers, men, or houses. Similarly, the entire cosmic manifestation is modeling clay in the hands of the Supreme Lord, who acts through maya to shape the glaring temporary forms of illusion, which absorb the minds of those who are not devotees of the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

It is from the perspective of unity that in this chapter Krsna instructs Uddhava to “neither praise nor criticize the conditioned nature and activities of other persons. Rather, one should see this world as simply the combination of material nature and the enjoying souls, all based on the one Absolute Truth.” (SB. 11.28.1)

From this lofty perspective, interactions in this world should all be seen as interactions between Krsna’s mayasakti (material energy) and jiva-sakti (the living entities). Thus one should neither praise nor condemn those who act properly or those who don’t. Rather, one should understand that both good and bad actions are simply collaborations between Krsna’s bewildering potency and eternal but illusioned souls.

The material world is real but temporary. Impersonalists may adopt ibis emphasis on the oneness of existence and so do Vaisnavas, although Vaisnavas understand that oneness as Krsna’s all-pervasive presence through His energies. Seeing material existence as false, nonexistent, and unreal that is, as an illusion - and considering the eternal Brahman to be the only reality, is called Mayavada. Ibis is the same philosophy that asserts that Krsna’s body and pastimes, along with His eternal devotional service, are maya - simply aspects of that nonreality. Krsna condemns this idea along with those who hold it when He tells Arjuna: “Fools deride Me when I descend in the human form. They do not know My transcendental nature as the Supreme Lord of all that be. Those who are thus bewildered are attracted by demonic and atheistic views. In that deluded condition, their hopes for liberation, their fruitive activities, and their culture of knowledge are all defeated.” (Bhagavad-gita 9.11-12)

The Srimad-Bhagavatam does not accept the Mayavada perspective. Rather, it discusses the three aspects of the Supreme Absolute Truth, each of which is real, transcendental, and beyond illusion. As the great self-realized brahmana Jada Bharata said: “What, then, is the ultimate truth? The answer is that nondual knowledge is the ultimate truth. It is devoid of the contamination of material qualities. It gives us liberation. It is the one without a second, all-pervading, and beyond imagination. The first realization of that knowledge is Brahman. Then Paramatma, the Supersoul, is realized by the yogis who try to see Him without grievance. This is the second stage of realization. Finally, full realization of the same supreme knowledge is realized in the Supreme Person. All learned scholars describe the Supreme Person as Vasudeva, the cause of Brahman, Paramatma, and others.” (SB. 5.12.11)

Krsna is offering Uddhava important instructions in order to guide jnanis who wish to perfect their vision of the Absolute Truth. He says that those who desire to see the oneness of existence will fail if they accept as substantive truth the apparent duality in material interactions: “Whoever indulges in praising or criticizing the qualities and behavior of others will quickly become deviated from his own best interest by his entanglement in illusory dualities.” (SB. 11.28.2)

The BBT purport to this text notes how relevant this instruction is for devotees of Krsna: “A conditioned soul desires to lord it over material nature and thus criticizes another conditioned soul whom he considers inferior. Similarly, one praises a superior materialist because one aspires to that superior position, in which one may dominate others. Praising and criticizing other materialistic people are thus directly or indirectly based on envy of other living entities and cause one to fall down from sva-artha, one’s real self-interest, Krsna consciousness.... Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura indicates that rather than trying to separate conditioned souls by materialistic distinctions, one should bring them together to chant the holy names of the Lord and propagate the sankirtana movement of Lord Caitanya— Material life is always imperfect, full of ignorance, and disappointing in the end. Rather than praising and criticizing the high and low features of ignorance, one should be absorbed in Krsna consciousness, on the spiritual platform of eternity, bliss, and knowledge.”

Krsna compares the experiencing of material dualities to dreaming and deep sleep, and notes that one who experiences reality in a dualistic way is doomed to illusion and death. Material duality, in which we tend to absorb ourselves, is only relative, not ultimate truth. Krsna continues: “What, therefore, is actually good or bad within this insubstantial world of duality, and how can the extent of such good and bad be measured?” (SB. 11.28.4)

Things that appear good and those that appear bad in the relative world of illusion are false and have no lasting worth. In text 5, Krsna compares these things to “shadows, echoes, and mirages” that can only mimic reality. Those conditioned souls who remain focused on the shadows, echoes, and mirages and miss reality will have to live in fear. They will be especially afraid at the moment of death. The only way to free oneself from the illusion of the relative world is to see everything in relation to the Absolute Truth - the Supreme Person and His energies.

Sri Krsna continues to explain to Uddhava the absolute oneness of reality: “The Supersoul alone is the ultimate controller and creator of this world, and thus He alone is also the created. Similarly, the Soul of all existence Himself both maintains and is maintained, withdraws and is withdrawn. No other entity can be properly ascertained as separate from Him, the Supreme Soul, who nonetheless is distinct from everything and everyone else. The appearance of the threefold material nature, which is perceived within Him, has no actual basis. Rather, you should understand that this material nature, composed of the three modes, is simply the product of His illusory potency.” (SB. 11.28.6-7)

One who understands this, Krsna says, “does not indulge in material criticism or praise. Like the sun, he wanders freely throughout this world. By direct perception, logical deduction, scriptural testimony, and personal realization, one should know that this world has a beginning and an end and so is not the ultimate reality. Thus one should live in ibis world without attachment.” (SB. 11.28.8-9)

Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that the central illusion of the material world can be divided into two parts. The first is the duality of judging between good and bad, young and old, auspicious and inauspicious, beautiful and ugly, and so many other expressions of duality. This category of illusion is dissolved when one understands the temporary nature of the qualities on both ends of the spectrum. That is, young becomes old, beautiful ugly, auspiciousness inauspiciousnss, and good bad over time - and over time, vice versa.

The second category of illusion is to see anything in the material world as separate from the Absolute Truth. By definition of absolute” this simply cannot be true. Absolute is all-encompassing and all-inclusive; nothing can be separate from or independent of it.

Those who free themselves from these two illusions can serve Krsna anywhere without fear. This is true nondual existence, where one lives in Krsna’s mercy by seeing Him in every event. Srila Prabhupada lectured about this in Vrndavana in 1976:

Not that because one is Krsna conscious there will be no material suffering. Actually, those who are Krsna conscious, they have no material suffering. Although it appears that they are suffering, they are not suffering. They can accept any so-called suffering and accept it as mercy of Krsna. They never take it as suffering. Tat te ’nukampam su-samiksamano bhuhjana evatma-krtam vipakam. A devotee, when he’s in suffering, so-called suffering, he accepts it as the mercy of Krsna. Tat te ’nukampam. And he rather thanks Krsna, that “I had to suffer many more times, but You have minimized it, giving me little suffering. So it is Your mercy.” And if anyone lives on that attitude, everything taken as Krsna’s mercy, then he is guaranteed to go back home, back to Godhead.

*Texts 10-11: Uddhava asks a question*

Hearing Krsna’s words inspires Uddhava to ask a question because the position of the eternally pure spirit soul, as he has understood it from Krsna in these texts and previous texts, appears contradictory. So in Srimad-Bhagavatam 10.28.10-11, Uddhava asks how the soul, which is by nature full of knowledge, “inexhaustible, transcendental, pure, self-luminous, and never covered by anything material,” is capable of experiencing material existence. And, Uddhava notes, it can’t be the body that experiences material existence, because the body is not conscious. Who, then, experiences material existence?

The BBT purport to text 11 restates Uddhava’s question: “In itself \[the body\] does not have any awareness of life. If the soul is transcendental to material life and the body is not even conscious of it, the following question arises: How does our experience of material existence actually take place?”

*Texts 12-13: Krsna places the responsibility for the experience of material existence on the eternal soul*

In texts 12-16 Krsna begins His summary of jnana-yoga by describing why the pure spirit soul remains apparently materially compromised. In texts 17-24 He details the philosophical basis for the cure for illusion, before describing in two sections (texts 25-26 and 31-37) the nature of those who have perfected their consciousness by practicing jnana. Between these two sections, in texts 27-30, the Supreme Lord guides the jnanis who are on the path but still imperfect. Krsna finally devotes seven texts (38-44) to teach jnanis how to overcome obstacles on the path.

First, Lord Krsna begins with the nature of a pure soul’s entanglement in the contaminating net of matter: “As long as the foolish spirit soul remains attracted \[sannikarsanam\] to the material body, senses, and vital force, his material existence continues to flourish, although it is ultimately meaningless. Actually, the living entity is transcendental to material existence. But because of his mentality of lording it over material nature, his material existential condition does not cease, and, just as in a dream, he is affected by all sorts of disadvantages.” (SB. 11.28.12-13)

The BBT purport to text 12 explains that the soul’s illusory connection to the material body has, at its root, the misuse of free will: “Here the word sannikarsanam indicates that the pure spirit soul voluntarily connects himself with the material body, considering this a most fruitful arrangement.”

*Texts 14-16: The soul’s development of a false sense of identity*

Krsna compares the soul’s “material life” to a dream: dreamers experience the events that occur in their dreams as if they are real, but when they wake (hey realize (hat (hose events were unreal. For conditioned souls, enjoyment and its suffering occur, but they have no substance because they are part of the material dream. When conditioned souls awaken to their actual identity, they are no longer confused by their dream experiences. While they are “dreaming” - that is, falsely identifying with the dreamlike world of matter - they experience “lamentation, elation, fear, anger, greed, confusion, and hankering, as well as repeated birth and death.” (SB. 11.28.15)

But, Krsna explains these states are completely external to the soul: “Lamentation, elation, fear, anger, greed, confusion, and hankering, as well as birth and death, are experiences of the false ego and not of the pure soul.” (SB. 11.28.15)

Now the Lord speaks about why suffering is imposed on the eternal, blissful soul: “The living entity who falsely identifies with his body, senses, life air, and mind, and who dwells within these coverings, assumes the form of his own materially conditioned qualities and work. He is designated variously in relation to the total material energy, and thus, under the strict control of supreme time \[kala\], he is forced to run here and there within material existence.” (SB. 11.28.16)

The BBT purport equates kala, the irresistible time factor, with the Supreme Lord: “The word kala refers directly to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who imposes the limiting segments of time upon the conditioned souls, keeping them tightly bound under the laws of nature.”

*Texts 17-24: The philosophical basis of the cure - focus on the Absolute Truth*

Krsna now offers an absolute, all-inclusive vision that will cure a soul of illusion. These texts, describing the philosophical basis of jnana, can certainly lead one toward an impersonal goal, but the same philosophical points can also help a bhakta attain the lotus feet of Krsna.

Krsna begins: One should live in this world free from material attachment, focusing one’s consciousness on the Absolute Truth, which exists independently and which “alone was present before the creation of the universe and which alone will remain after its destruction.” That Absolute Truth “is also the time factor and the ultimate cause. Even in the middle stage of this creation’s existence, the Absolute Truth alone is the actual reality.” (SB. 1 1.28.18)

Sri Krsna continues: The only perceptions that are true are those that include the relationship of the object being perceived with the Absolute Truth. Other perceptions are only superficial designations imposed by the mind and false ego on the Absolute Truth. Seeing or naming an object as if it had no relationship with the Absolute Truth is the definition of illusion. But know that the ability and ingredients required to see objects in relation to the Absolute Truth also come from the Absolute Truth.

To attain this focused vision of reality, one needs transcendental knowledge “sharpened by worship of a bona fide spiritual master.” (SB. 11.28.17) One also needs to fine-tune his discrimination with the help of “scriptural evidence, austerity, direct perception, reception of the Puranas’ historical narrations, and logical inference.” (SB. 11.28.18)

“Thus clearly understanding by discriminating logic the unique position of the Absolute Truth, one should expertly refute one’s misidentification with matter and cut to pieces all doubts about the identity of the self. Becoming satisfied in the soul’s natural ecstasy, one should desist from all lusty engagements of the material senses.” (SB. 11.28.23)

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura comments on text 23: “When one becomes able to give up this temporary world, in which he lives because of his own desires, he can destroy all doubts. Then he will achieve the ecstasy of the self and become satisfied. Highlighting one’s mental tendencies to perceive the Absolute Truth in all existence, one comes to understand that all other limited things are not meant for one’s own sense enjoyment. The world of matter is no longer the field of enjoyment for the liberated soul; when one appreciates this he understands that since the Absolute Truth has created this material manifestation in all its aspects, He alone is reality. Thus as ecstatic love for Lord Krsna develops, all doubts are driven away and one finally understands that satisfying the transcendental Cupid is one’s only business. Then all petty lusts leave of their own accord.”

Sri Krsna continues: In this way, with purified consciousness, one can he fixed in his actual identity as a soul, free from the misconception that he is his body, senses, life-air, intelligence, false ego, the material elements, the objects of the senses, or even the primeval state of material equilibrium.

*Texts 25-26: The perfected jnani*

Now Krsna describes the flexibility in executing the standard practices of jnana-yoga allowed a perfected jnani who has discerned Him: “For one who has properly realized My personal identity as the Supreme Godhead, what credit is there if his senses - mere products of the material modes — are perfectly concentrated in meditation? And on the other hand, what blame is incurred if his senses happen to become agitated? Indeed, what does it mean to the sun if the clouds come and go?” (SB. 11.28.25)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “My devotee with knowledge and discrimination has no relationship with the good and bad produced by the senses and mind. What is the virtue of having steady senses for those who have realized My form? And what is the fault if one’s senses are unsteady?”

Thus the perfected devotee jnani, having realized Krsna’s form, is neither attracted to nor repulsed by any occurence in the realm of matter. In his realized state, he is truly aloof from all interactions of either gross or subtle matter that stem from the modes of material nature.

Krsna then describes the transcendental Absolute Truth on whom these perfected jnanis have focused their meditation: “The sky may display the various qualities of the air, fire, water, and earth that pass through it, as well as such qualities as heat and cold, which continually come and go with the seasons. Yet the sky is never entangled with any of these qualities. Similarly, the Supreme Absolute Truth is never entangled with the contaminations of goodness, passion, and ignorance, which cause the material transformations of the false ego.” (SB. 11.28.26)

*Texts 27-30: Imperfect jnanis*

In text 25 of this chapter, Krsna said of the perfected jnanis: What blame is there if their senses happen to become agitated? What does it matter to the sun if the clouds come and go? But now He cautions the jnanis who have not yet perfected their realization of Him: “Nevertheless, until by firmly \[drdhena\] practicing devotional service to Me \[mad-bhakti-yogena\] one has completely eliminated from his mind \[parivarjaniyol all contamination of material passion \[rajo\], one must very carefully avoid associating \|sangah\| with the material modes, which are produced by My illusory energy \[gunesu maya-racitesu\].” (SB. 11.28.27)

Although the material nature is nondifferent from Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, association (sangah) with the illusory energy (gunesu maya-racitesu) must still be rejected (parivarjaniyo) until one’s consciousness is free of passion (rajo).

One becomes free by the steady, fixed (drdhena) practice of devotional service to Krsna (mad-bhakti-yogena). Srila Sridhara Svami’s terse comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.28.27 speaks to this point: “One who is not complete in knowledge cannot act however he likes, as a liberated person may do.”

Krsna provides a vivid example to instruct those yogis who may resist His warning: “Just as an improperly treated disease recurs and gives repeated distress to the patient, the mind that is not completely purified of its perverted tendencies will remain attached to material things and repeatedly torment the imperfect yogi.” (SB. 11.28.28)

What becomes of the imperfect souls who don’t heed Krsna? Krsna answers this question in texts 29 and 30: Envious demigods send family members, disciples, and others to inhibit the progress of these attached, imperfect yogis (ku-yoginah), but their progress cannot be stopped and will be resumed in their next life. Different from yogis, ordinary persons continue their material existence endlessly, for their cultivation is of material desires and pleasure.

The attached yogis’ detour for a birth teaches and corrects them, and thus these yogis “will never again be trapped in the network of fruitive work.” (SB. 11.28.29)

In his comment on text 27, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura instructs devotees: “The living entity should always reject impure association, knowing that this material world is simply the product of may a. Devotees not firmly engaged in devotional service will he impelled to act on the mental platform and become false devotees. False devotees end up with materialistic tendencies, created by the mode of passion.”

*Texts 31-37: The realizations of perfected jnanis*

After a break of four texts (27-30) in which Krsna advised the imperfect jnana-yogis, in the next seven texts Krsna returns to those who have already perfected themselves and describes their understanding.

Text 31: They are aloof - they do not identify with the body or with bodily activities.

Text 32: They may see the dualities of material existence, but they are not bewildered by them. Rather, they remain fixed in the Absolute Truth when confronted by those dualities.

The BBT purport adds: “A sane person can clearly distinguish between a dream experience and his real life. Similarly a manisi, or intelligent person, can clearly perceive polluted material sense objects to be creations of the Lord’s illusory energy and not factual reality.”

Texts 33-34: Everything in the realm of matter changes continuously, and the ignorant identify themselves with these shifts. Successful jnanis, however, know themselves as eternal - they neither transform nor change. They are not affected by ignorance because they have realized the Absolute Truth.

Text 35: They see the Supreme Lord, who “is self-luminous, unborn, and immeasurable. He is pure transcendental consciousness and perceives everything. One without a second, He is realized only after ordinary words cease. By Him the power of speech and the life airs are set into motion.” Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that the Lord’s self- manifesting illumination makes everything else evident — Himself, the Supreme Absolute Truth, and the jiva.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura states: “Why in devotional service would any merging occur of the pure soul, that entity called ‘you,’ with the Supersoul? The Supersoul represents the full sun globe since He is, after all, distinct from the individual jiva. The Supersoul is self-luminous and self-manifest, whereas the jiva is manifest by the Supersoul. He is unborn, whereas the jiva, because of the material coverings that create his designations, takes birth. He is all-pervading and so cannot be measured, but the jiva is infinitesimal.”

Text 36: He realizes that “whatever apparent duality is perceived in the self is simply the delusion of the mind.” (SB. 11.28.36) From the BBT purport: “The word vikalpa, or ‘duality,’ here refers to the mistaken idea that the spirit soul is partly composed of matter in the form of the gross body or subtle mind— Foolish persons consider the material body or mind an intrinsic or fundamental component of the self. In fact the living entity is pure spirit, free from any tinge of matter.”

Text 37: “The duality of the five material elements is perceived only in terms of names and forms. Those who say this duality is real are pseudoscholars vainly proposing fanciful theories without basis in fact.”

From the BBT purport: “Material names and forms, subject as they are to creation and annihilation, have no permanent existence and so do not constitute essential, fundamental principles of reality. The material world consists of variegated transformations of the potency of God. Although God is real and His potency is real, the particular forms and names that temporarily or circumstantially appear have no ultimate reality.”

*Texts 38-44: Overcoming obstacles on the jnana path*

In these texts Sri Krsna makes recommendations to help aspiring yogis who become diseased or otherwise disturbed: Some difficulties can be overcome by yogic meditations and sitting postures practiced along with controlled breathing. Other obstacles can be overcome by proper prescriptions of austerities, mantras, or medicinal herbs. The Lord now offers a solution for those experiencing difficulties: “These inauspicious disturbances can be gradually removed by constant remembrance of Me, by congregational hearing and chanting of My holy names, or by following in the footsteps of the great masters of yoga.” (SB. 11.28.40)

Srila Sridhara Svami and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura make similar comments on this text:

Srila Sridhara Svami: By meditation on Me, and so on, lust and other obstructions \[can be counteracted\], and by following in the footsteps of the great yoga masters, hypocrisy, false pride, and so on, can be defeated.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura: By following the prescription of devotional service in the form of chanting and hearing the names of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and by meditating on Him, all inauspicious desires and obstructions are destroyed.

Sri Krsna continues: “By various methods, some yogis free the body from disease and old age and keep it perpetually youthful. Thus they engage in yoga for the purpose of achieving material mystic perfections. This mystic bodily perfection is not valued very highly by those expert in transcendental knowledge. Indeed, they consider endeavor for such perfection useless, since the soul, like a tree, is permanent, but the body, like a tree’s fruit, is subject to destruction. (SB. 11.28.41-42)

Srila Sridhara Svami comments on text 41: Krsna is saying that the ideas He expresses in this text are not His ideas, and that He condemns any goal of yoga practice other than the attainment of transcendental knowledge. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura adds that neither the practice of hatha-yoga to improve one’s health nor the attempt to attain the eighteen mystic perfections simply for material gain are devotional service.

In text 42 Krsna compares the soul to a tree and the body to the fruit of a tree. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati clarifies Krsna’s tree analogy in his comment on this text: “A tree bears fruit from time to time. Then the fruits are finished, although the tree continues to exist. Similarly, those who are self-realized understand that the two material bodies, the subtle and the gross, are temporary \[like the fruits\] and themselves give birth to momentary fruits. In this way, they desist from yogic austerities \[because they realize that such austerities bring temporary results and mean nothing when compared to eternity\].”

Sri Krsna continues: “Although the physical body may be improved by various processes of yoga, an intelligent person who has dedicated his life to Me does not place his faith in the prospect of perfecting his physical body through yoga, and in fact he gives up such procedures.” (SB. 11.28.43)

The sober tone of Krsna’s words is continued by Srila Sridhara Svami and emphasized by Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura:

Srila Sridhara Svami: But, someone may object, isn’t it sometimes seen that... by the practice of pranayama, and so on, the conditions of old age and disease are eliminated? Yes, that is true. But still, one should not give up samadhi to become attached to these things, as spoken by this verse beginning yogam. One who has intelligently taken shelter of Me does not place faith in that bodily perfection; he does not trust it.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura: Apart from the uselessness of hatha-yoga, one should also avoid becoming attached to the practice of raja-yoga and similar methods, including the execution of pranayama, and so on. Rather, the instruction heard from scripture is that one should take advantage of saintly association and eliminate all anarthas by gradually increasing one’s devotional service. The devotees of the Supreme Lord are unbiased instructors. They do not pay high regard to practices outside the scope of the direct service of Lord Mukunda because those tend to make one fall prey to lust and greed. In this regard, one can consult Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.6.35: “It is true that by practicing restraint of the senses by the yoga system one can get relief from the disturbances of desire and lust, but this is not sufficient to give satisfaction to the soul, for this \[satisfaction\] is derived from devotional service to the Personality of Godhead.”

*Text 44: Sri Krsna’s conclusion*

In this chapter’s final text, Sri Krsna offers advice on how to overcome obstacles on the path of transcendence: “The yogi who has taken shelter of Me remains free from hankering because he experiences the happiness of the soul within. Thus while executing this process of yoga, he is never defeated by obstacles.”

Srila Sridhara Svami comments: “\[O\]ne who has taken shelter of Me (Krsna) need not fear obstructions… his experience is focused on his own happiness, the happiness of the soul. Obstructions are based on material hankering, which ceases to exist for one who has taken shelter of Me. Thus unobstructed by disturbances he remains full in his own transcendental pleasure.”

The BBT’s purport ends the chapter by glorifying the removal of obstacles through surrender to Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “According to Srila Sridhara Svami, the Supreme Lord has briefly described to Uddhava the essential wisdom of all the Upanisads, with the conclusion that pure devotional service to the Lord is the real means of ultimate liberation. In this regard Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura emphasizes that although hatha-yogis and raja-yogis try to make progress along their prescribed paths, they confront obstacles and often fail to achieve their desired goals. However, one who surrenders to the Supreme Lord will certainly be victorious on his spiritual path back borne, back to Godhead.”

**Chapter 29: Bhakti-yoga**

Krsna’s instructions to Uddhava in chapters 6 through 28 of the Eleventh Canto describe a number of topics but focus especially on jnana-yoga and bhakti-yoga. Now, after having summarized jnana-yoga in chapter 28, Krsna concludes His teachings to Uddhava with a summary of bhakti-yoga, which He already described in chapters 12, 14, 20, and 27 and presented again and again as the conclusion of all other paths.

*Texts 1-6: Uddhava inquires of Krsna*

*Text 1: Uddhava asks whether there’s an easier way than practicing jnana?*

Uddhava has, of course, been listening closely to Krsna, and now he tells his Lord that he considers the jnana practices Krsna recommends to be too difficult to perform because they require extreme detachment and a rigorous control of the mind. He therefore asks Krsna whether there is an easier way to attain perfection. Uddhava also knows that on its own, jnana leads only to liberation and does not recognize as its goal the eternal service of Krsna. So Sri Uddhava says: “My dear Lord Acyuta, I fear that the method of yoga described by You is very difficult for one who cannot control his mind. Therefore please explain to me in simple terms how someone can more easily execute it.” (SB. 11.29.1)

*Text 2: Uddhava describes what’s difficult about the practice of jnana-yoga*

“O lotus-eyed Lord, generally those yogis who try to steady the mind experience frustration because of their inability to perfect the state of trance. Thus they weary in their attempt to bring the mind under control.” (SB. 11.29.2)

Srila Sridhara Svami is graphic in his definition of the essential problem faced by jnana-yogis: “Those who are engaged in the attempt to subdue the mind become depressed and frustrated. Why ? Because they are unable to concentrate the mind and bring it under control. They feel harassed, and the task of trying somehow or other to bring the mind under control exhausts them.”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 326), Srila Jiva Gosvami writes about the reason behind Uddhava’s question in these first two texts of chapter 29: “Because of the difficulties \[in the practice of jnana-yoga\], in most cases one will not achieve the final result. And because bhakti, about which Uddhava desires to hear, is easy to execute \[so one will definitely achieve the results\], bhakti alone should be practiced— Paying no attention to the practices or results of jnana or other types of yoga, devotees practice bhakti alone, aiming their practice only at the form of Krsna. This will be explained in the next four verses.”

*Text 3: Uddhava’s recommendation*

“Therefore, O lotus-eyed Lord of the universe, swanlike men happily take shelter of Your lotus feet, the source of all transcendental ecstasy.”

Srila Sridhara Svami’s comments shift as dramatically as Uddhava’s words as the acarya turns from the difficulties of jnana-yoga to glorifying the krsna-sarana: “Those who are swanlike men, expert in discriminating between the essential and the nonessential, take shelter of and serve with great happiness Your lotus feet, which fill one with all ecstasy.”

In the same text Uddhava also makes an observation about those who do not accept the shelter of Krsna’s lotus feet: “But those who take pride in their accomplishments in yoga and karma fail to take shelter of You and are defeated by Your illusory energy.” (SB. 11.29.3)

Text 3 makes clear the fatal flaw that allows even expert practitioners on non 'bhakti paths to be conquered again by Krsna’s illusory energy. Srila Sridhara Svami continues: “Why are these others defeated by Your illusory energy? Because they are puffed up due to their yoga and karma and therefore do not accept Your shelter. Bewildered by Your illusory potency, they proudly think, ‘We are very knowledgeable in yoga and expert in fruitive activities.’ Thus they do not attain liberation.”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 326), Srila Jiva Gosvami adds further illumination for the devotees: “These pure devotees, although attacked by desires for yoga and karma, and by Your maya, do not become obstructed, because they do not become proud. Rather, they think i hey have achieved success in their pursuit of the goal of life (purusartha-sadhana) due to the Lord’s unconditional mercy on the fallen, unlike yogis and others who think (hey have achieved success by their own efforts.”

*Text 4: Krsna’s affection for His devotees*

In stark contrast to the exchanges with the Absolute Truth experienced by practitioners like nondevotee jnanis and yogis, Uddhava next speaks of the Lord’s affectionate interactions with His devotees - His pure servants: “My dear infallible Lord, it is not very astonishing that You intimately approach Your servants who have taken exclusive shelter of You.”

Uddhava offers an example from the Ramayana to illustrate the unequivocal love the Supreme Lord has for His devotees: “After all, during Your appearance as Lord Ramacandra, even while great demigods like Brahma were vying to place the effulgent tips of their helmets upon the cushion where Your lotus feet rested, You displayed special affection for monkeys such as Hanuman because they had taken exclusive shelter of You.” (SB. 11.29.4)

Srila Sridhara Svami emphasizes this point by saying that the Lord becomes intimate, even subordinate, to those servants who take exclusive shelter of Him: “Your devotees, in contrast to those on other paths, become all-successful by Your mercy.”

This highlights the essential difference between the bhakti path and paths such as jnana and yoga, which depend on the practitioner’s expertise for their success. Bhakti, on the other hand, depends only on the merciful dispensation of Krsna, who responds to His devotee’s sincere, love-laden attempts to serve Him.

In his comment on text 4, Jiva Gosvami adds that these pure devotees “are indifferent to the execution of jnana, yoga, karma, and so on.” To further clarify the difference in the results gained through the path of bhakti and those gained through other paths, Srila Jiva Gosvami writes: “O Lord, You bestow even on the demons the liberation that is the ultimate fruit of jnana and yoga, which great controllers like Siva and Brahma desire. But for Your servants like the Pandavas You become subordinate, acting as their chariot driver, personal attendant, menial servant, friend, and messenger. You respectfully approach them and stand by their thrones (SB. 1.16.16). Therefore devotion to You in the the form of Sri Krsna, as described here, is the most important.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura is somewhat cautionary in his comment on text 4, as he directs his words to devotees and stresses the rarity of an intimate friendship in pure devotional service with the Lord: “Even the devotees born in the monkey community and who have attained Rama’s exclusive shelter are capable of achieving friendship with the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Nevertheless, the Supreme Lord, whose lotus feet are worshiped by demigods like Brahma, is very difficult to achieve.”

*Text 5: All gain and no loss when one takes shelter of Krsna*

Uddhava speaks with disdain about accepting any goal that favors abandoning serving Lord Krsna’s divine and fragrant lotus feet: “Who, then, could dare reject You, the very Soul, the most dear object of worship, and the Supreme Lord of all - You who give all possible perfections to the devotees who take shelter of You? Who could be so ungrateful, knowing the benefits You bestow? Who would reject You and accept something for the sake of material enjoyment, which simply leads to forgetfulness of You? And what lack is there for us who are engaged in the service of the dust of Your lotus feet?” (SB. 11.29.5)

All the acarya commentators agree that only an ingrate unaware of spiritual reality could reject the shelter of the all-merciful Lord. Nor do devotees serve Krsna to gain a truth higher than Krsna, for no such truth exists; Krsna is the independent foundation on which all other truths rest. Krsna Himself states: “And I am the basis of the impersonal Brahman, which is immortal, imperishable, and eternal and is the constitutional position of ultimate happiness.” (Bhagavad-gita 14.27) And “O conqueror of wealth, there is no truth superior to Me. Everything rests upon Me, as pearls are strung on a thread.” (Bhagavad-gita 7.7)

Uddhava aspires only to serve Krsna; he has no aspiration even for liberation. Krsna said earlier, mad-bhakto vanapeksakah, “My devotee is detached even from the desire for liberation” (SB. 11.18.28). He also told Uddhava, “Because My devotees possess saintly behavior and deep intelligence, they completely dedicate themselves to Me and do not desire anything besides Me. Indeed, even if I offer them liberation from birth and death, they do not accept it.” (SB. 11.20.34)

Rather than seeing devotional service as a means to liberation, a devotee sees liberation without service to Krsna as hell - kaivalyam narakayate.Nor is service rendered to Krsna only to attain liberation truly devotional. Rather, it is sell-serving and therefore unattractive to Krsna, being far, far from the endearing service offered with prema by the residents of Vrndavana, and especially by the Vraja gopikas, who conquer Krsna with their love (SB. 11.12.10-13).

*Text 6: Devotees remain indebted to their Lord for His appearance and instructions*

Uddhava concludes: “O my Lord! Transcendental poets and experts in spiritual science could not fully express their indebtedness to You, even if they were endowed with the prolonged lifetime of Brahma, for You appear in two features - externally as the acarya and internally as the Supersoul - to deliver the embodied living being by directing him how to come to You.” (SB. 11.29.6)

Srila Sridhara Svami notes that full surrender of the self is the only legitimate response after thoughtfully considering the benefits the Lord bestows: “Regarding repayment to the Lord in the sense of absolving one’s debt to Him, the wise, the knowers of the Absolute Truth, cannot find the means of doing this, for they remember the help He has bestowed... What help is that? He has appeared externally as the spiritual master and internally as the Supersoul. In these forms He has cleansed the consciousness and eliminated all inauspiciousness in the form of the desire for sense gratification.”

Both Jiva Gosvami’s comments and those of Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura add further sweetness to Sridhara Svami’s comments:

Jiva Gosvami: O Lord, even the omniscient, wise souls who worship You in overflowing devotional ecstasy for as long as Brahma lives cannot find the means to repay their debt to You. Therefore they cannot reject You.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “But,” the Lord may object, “since I bestow all desired perfections only on those who worship Me, My granting of these different desires is not unconditional but is done conditionally.” This objection is replied to in the negative: Their worship of You has also been bestowed by You. Thus no one, even by rendering service for a thousand maha'kalpas, can undo their debt to You, the causeless bestower of the supreme benefit.
