*Texts 7-11: Krsna responds by describing the path of bhakti*

*Texts 7-8: Krsna’s introductory words*

That supreme controller of all controllers, who assumes the three forms of Brahma, Visnu, and Siva, displayed His all-attractive smile as He lovingly responded to Uddhava. The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: “I shall describe to you the principles of devotion to Me \[mama dharman su-marigalan\], by executing which a mortal human being will conquer unconquerable death.” (SB. 11.29.8)

*Texts 9-11: Krsna describes the practices of bhakti in three texts*

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura indicates in his comment on text 9 that this section will describe different levels of devotional service, both pure and mixed.

*Text 9: Fix your mind on Me*

*kuryat sarvani karmani*

*mad-artham sanakaih smaran*

*mayy arpita-manas-citto*

*mad-dharmatma-mano-ratih*

“Always remembering Me, one should perform all his duties for Me without becoming impetuous. With mind and intelligence offered to Me, one should fix his mind in attraction to My devotional service.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that text 9 is an instruction for both the practice of pure devotional service and the practice of mixed devotional service (varnasrama-dharma, for example), because the Lord has spoken in a way that allows both meanings to be understood.

Those performing pure devotional service should do everything they do for him, including all material actions, such as brushing one’s teeth, and all spiritual actions, such as hearing and chanting. If one is performing one’s duties according to varnasrama-dharma for Him, one should make the bhakti part more important. Krsna also explains that one should lix ones consciousness on persons whose minds are dedicated to Him (mayy arpita-manas-cittah). In other words, one should he attached to His devotees, or those whose minds (aima-manah) have been offered to Krsna.

*Text 10: Take shelter of a holy place*

“One should take shelter of holy places where My saintly devotees reside, and one should be guided by the exemplary activities of My devotees, who appear among the demigods, demons, and human beings.”

The BBT purport offers wise advice: “Narada Muni is one of the great devotees of the Lord who appeared among the demigods. Prahlada Maharaja appeared among the demons, and many other great devotees, such as Ambarisa Maharaja and the Pandavas, appeared among human beings. One should take shelter of the devotees’ exemplary activities and also the holy places where devotees reside. Thus one will remain safe on the path of devotional service.”

*Text 11: Celebrate festivals*

“Either alone or in public gatherings, with singing, dancing, and other exhibitions of royal opulence, one should arrange to celebrate those holy days, ceremonies, and festivals set aside specially for My worship.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that text 11 describes activities common to all levels of bhaktas.

*Texts 12-19: Activities of jnana-yoga*

Krsna now stops describing bhakti so He can try to attract those inclined tojnana, the process of understanding Him, the Absolute Truth, through philosophical speculation.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments on text 12: “Having described the duty of those who have taken shelter of devotional service, now the duty of those who have taken shelter of knowledge is stated in eight verses (SB. 11.29.12-19).”

Srila Jiva Gosvami gives a slightly different but nevertheless wonderful explanation of Krsna’s shift in topic by calling texts 12-15 a lesser methodology than the one He described in texts 8—11: “Krsna has spoken of pure devotion to Himself for the benefit of \[fit candidates\] in four verses (SB. 11.29.8-11). The Lord now mercifully describes in four more verses (SB. 11.29.12—15) something else to inspire devotion to Himself: \|The Lord considered,\] ‘Most people are subject to rivalry and so on, and even if they somehow or other become favorably disposed to spiritual life, they only worship Me in the form of the Supersoul, who is in all hearts.’ Thus the Lord exercised His mercy to remove from them the qualities of envy and so on. To turn them to Him, He describes a philosophy similar to His statement in the Bhagavad-gita (10.42), vistabhyaham idam krtsnam. But in place of the worship of the Supersoul (as He is described in Gita, 10.42), who is His own plenary portion, the Lord in this text beginning mam (Me) now directly recommends worship of Himself.”

According to Srila Jiva Gosvami, Krsna first gives the theory (texts 12-15) and then the practice (texts 16-19) to remove envy and rivalry.

*Texts 12-15: The theory - how to remove envy and the sense of rivalry*

“With a pure heart one should see Me, the Supreme Soul, within all beings and also within oneself, to be both unblemished by anything material and also present everywhere, both externally and internally, just like the omnipresent sky. O brilliant Uddhava, one who thus views all living entities with the idea that I am present within each of them, and who by taking shelter of this divine knowledge offers due respect to everyone, is considered actually wise. Such a man sees equally the brahmana and the outcaste, the thief and the charitable promoter of brahminical culture, the sun and the tiny sparks of fire, the gentle and the cruel. For him who constantly meditates upon My presence \[mam\] within all persons, the bad tendencies of rivalry, envy, and abusiveness, along with false ego, are very quickly destroyed.” (SB. 11.29.12-15)

The BBT purport to text 12 cites Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura: “\[T\]he Lord has spoken the present verse to attract those who are inclined toward philosophical speculation about the Absolute Truth.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura’s powerful comment to texts 13 and 14 addresses the ramifications of the vision Krsna just recommended: “If one is able to see the Supreme Lord everywhere in this world, it is inevitable that he will achieve the Absolute (kaivalya). But when one sees things as if they are separate from the Supreme Personality of Godhead, one does not have a mood of service but a mood of enjoyment.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment on text 15 describes how envy, rivalry, and false ego disappear immediately when one adopts the understanding Krsna recommends: “In order to rid oneself of rivalry and other bad qualities, one must practice seeing Me everywhere. Rivalry exists with equals, envy with superiors, and abusive behaviors with inferiors. The implied idea is that one will be unable to engage in rivalry and so on if one sees Krsna everywhere, because, Krsna says, ‘How can those thoughts be directed toward Me?’”

*Texts 16-19: The practice - offer obeisances to all living beings*

“Disregarding the ridicule \[smayamanan\] of one’s companions, one should give up the bodily conception and its accompanying embarrassment. One should offer obeisances before all - even the dogs, outcastes, cows, and asses - falling flat upon the ground like a rod.” (SB. 11.29.16)

This practice, according to Srila Jiva Gosvami, is Krsna’s prescription for removing both envy and rivalry. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “ ‘Those who are smiling’ (smayamanan) refers to one’s friends who laugh at him, saying, ‘Ah, such a big man and he is offering obeisances to someone insignificant.’ Or, one may have the mentality based on bodily identification that I am very great and he is very small, so why should I offer obeisances to him? Both of these situations create embarrassment. Giving up one’s embarrassment and seeing the indwelling Supreme Lord everywhere, one should offer obeisances even to dogs and outcastes.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura highlights how relevant this vision is when chanting Krsna’s holy names: “Sriman Mahaprabhu advised everyone to become lower than a blade of grass and more tolerant than a tree, to consider oneself inferior to all others and to offer respects to all. When such a state is attained, one can achieve success in the worship of the Lord’s holy name.”

*Text 17: How long should one continue this practice?*

“Until one has fully developed the ability to see Me within all living beings, one must continue to worship Me by this process with the activities of his speech, mind, and body.” (SB. 11.29.17)

The BBT purport advises: “Until one fully realizes the Supreme Lord within all beings, he shotdd continue the process of offering obeisances to all creatures. Although one may not be able to actually fall on the ground before all creatures, at least within his mind or by his words one should offer respect to all living beings. This will accelerate the devotee’s self-realization.”

Again Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura teaches us the relevance of Krsna’s words in relation to bhakti: “If one makes it his aim to worship the Supreme Personality of Godhead with his body, mind, and words, becoming more tolerant than a tree and personally free from the desire for prestige, offering honor to all others, he will never be troubled by any living entity, nor will he ever have anything to fear. In such a condition it is possible for him to worship incessantly.”

*Text 18: The results of this practice*

“By such transcendental knowledge of the all-pervading Personality of Godhead, one is able to see the Absolute Truth everywhere. Freed thus from all doubts, one gives up fruitive activities.” (SB. 11.29.18)

*Text 19: This is the best of processes*

Are other processes superior to this? Sri Krsna replies: “Indeed, I consider this process - using one’s mind, words, and bodily functions for realizing Me within all living beings - to be the best possible method of spiritual enlightenment.” (SB. 11.29.19)

Srila Sridhara Svami notes that this is the best of processes. Srila Jiva Gosvami too comments that awareness of Krsna in all living beings (mad-bhavah sarva-bhutesu) is the best of all methods of worship.Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura identifies the intended audience for Sri Krsna’s instructions in this section: “There is no easier and more appropriate method for jnanis to attain the Supreme.”

Krsna previously summarized the primary processes devotees should practice in Srirnad-Bhagavatarn 11.29.9-11. Srila Jiva Gosvami and Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura have both shown how this path that Krsna has especially prescribed for jnanis (SB. 11.29.13-19) can be assimilated into devotional service.

*Texts 20-22: Bhakti’s unique position*

Returning now to bhakti, Krsna speaks of bhakti’s unique glory and potency.

*Text 20: Bhakti, the process established by the Lord Himself*

“My dear Uddhava, because I have personally established it, this process of devotional service unto Me (mat-dharmasya) is transcendental and free from any material motivation. Certainly a devotee never suffers even the slightest loss by adopting this process.” (SB. 11.29.20)

The BBT purport comments: “Although great sages and authorities have established various methods of human progress, the Supreme Lord Himself has introduced the system of bhakti-yoga, wherein one directly takes shelter of the Lord in loving service. One who serves the Lord without personal motivation can never be defeated in his progress and will certainly go back home, back to Godhead, in the near future.”

*Text 21: Bhakti makes significant what would otherwise be meaningless*

“O Uddhava, greatest of saints, in a dangerous situation an ordinary person cries, becomes fearful, and laments, although such useless emotions do not change the situation. But activities offered to Me without personal motivation, even if they are externally useless, amount to the actual process of religion.” (SB. 11.29.21)

The BBT purport echoes the mood of Srila Sridhara Svami in his comment on this text: “Even the most insignificant activity, when offered to the Supreme Lord without personal desire, can elevate one to the perfection of spiritual life. Actually, Lord Krsna always protects and maintains His devotee. But if a devotee cries to the Lord for protection or maintenance, desiring to continue his devotional service unimpeded, Lord Krsna accepts such apparently unnecessary appeals to be the highest religious process.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that, not to speak of the actual dharma of pure devotional service, even Vedic principles (which in the tenth chapter of the Eleventh Canto Krsna called useless ), when offered to Him without desire for fruitive results, blossom into eternal fruits. Sri Jiva continues: “If such action \[as offering Vedic principles\] is not futile, then by the logic of ‘not to speak of’ it is strongly hinted that the religious principle of worshiping the Lord in His form as Sri Krsna \[is particularly never futile\],” and he gives the example of Kamsa and others who worshiped Krsna by their fear. “Just by being in relation to Me, their endeavors, even though based on fear and other negative emotions, did not prove futile but resulted in liberation.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains Krsna’s words in a somewhat different way. He writes that we need not try to experience fear, lamentation, and so on, since when those emotions “meet their object” they arise automatically. Similarly, devotional worship, “when it obtains its own natural object (Krsna), develops automatically.”

Does this mean that devotees shouldn’t try to be successful in their Krsna conscious practices? Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura con?ludes: “Nevertheless, when devotees free from deceit constantly endeavor to attain devotional service, their endeavors simply reveal the extent of their extreme attachment to devotional service and thus should be seen as a great transcendental quality.”

*Text 22: Bhakti is the crown jewel of spiritual processes*

Sri Krsna’s final words in this chapter glorify bhakti, and this is His concluding instruction to Uddhava. His statements are both powerful and intriguing: “This process is the supreme intelligence of the intelligent and the cleverness of the most clever, for by following it one can in this very life make use of the temporary and unreal to achieve Me, the eternal reality.”

Bhakti is so unique! By its potency one can exchange a temporary benefit for an eternal benefit. Prahlada Maharaja once explained this to his school friends: “One who is sufficiently intelligent should use the human form of body from the very beginning of life - in other words, from the tender age of childhood - to practice the activities of devotional service, giving up all other engagements. The human body is most rarely achieved, and although temporary like other bodies, it is meaningful because in human life one can perform devotional service. Even a slight amount of sincere devotional service can give one complete perfection.” (SB. 7.6.1)

From the BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.29.22: “As described in this chapter, one who desires personal prestige in the Lord’s service cannot be considered intelligent and clever. Similarly, one who is anxious to become a sophisticated transcendental philosopher is not the most intelligent. Nor is one who is expert in accumulating money. The Lord here states that the most intelligent and clever person is the devotee who offers his temporary, illusory material body and possessions to Him with love and without personal motivation. The devotee thus obtains the eternal Absolute Truth. In other words, real intelligence is to actually surrender to Lord Krsna, without personal desire or duplicity. That is the Lord’s opinion.”

In his comment on this same text, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes the opportunity to serve Krsna with devotion as suitable for those who are the most intelligent. Why? Because by practicing devotional service, everything temporary, which will eventually be wrested from our grasp, can be used to attain Krsna, “the supreme gain, the supreme eternal, the supreme Absolute Truth.”

In explaining why the intelligent take to bhakti, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura unfurls the banner of bhakti’s supreme position: “The devotee is the most intelligent of those with intelligence, but he is not intelligent in dissecting difficult scriptures. He is clever among those who are clever, but he is not clever at earning a gold coin in exchange for a penny. What, then, is he clever at? In Bharata-bhumi, the devotee, using his mortal, temporary body, can attain Me, who am without death. He attains Me who possess an eternal form and who exist at all times. He thus attains his true existence. By his bhakti alone he can even control Me.”

Then Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti speaks even more profoundly as he explains his own words:

The meaning is this. The person who in this world can receive a thousand coins by giving one coin is said to be both intelligent and skillful. One who obtains diamonds or a gold coin in exchange for a small coin is called intelligent and skillful. A person who can take a gold coin from a sober, intelligent person is called intelligent and skillful. But who is intelligent enough to obtain a cintamard, a wish-fulfilling stone, or a kamadhenu, a cow of the heavenly world?

The inhabitants of Bharata-bhumi, who are mortal and bom in low families, can offer Me their bodies, which are actually not worth a penny, for they are often deformed and will eventually be afflicted with old age and disease. But \[through their offering\] they can attain Me, the ocean of sweetness. Accepting their offerings, I, who am supposed to be the cleverest, give Myself with joy to the devotees, along with My priceless ornaments, bracelets, and crown. So aren’t these inhabitants of Bharata-bhumi the most intelligent and skillful?

What does it mean to give one’s body to the Lord? It means to engage the ear and other organs in hearing, chanting, remembering, and service. If the tongue is engaged in chanting, if the ears are engaged in hearing, if the hands are engaged in service, then one is giving one’s body to the Lord.

But the Lord is attained even by offering to Him only one part of the body! What intelligent person would not do this?

“This verse,” Cakravarti Thakura explains, “is the touchstone among verses, the essence of all the Lord’s teachings. He who has this verse shining in his heart shines in the assembly of devotees.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura thus indicates that one will advance in Krsna consciousness by keeping this text in his heart.

*Texts 23-49: The Uddhava-gita ends*

*Texts 23-28: Sri Krsna glorifies the Uddhava-gita*

Krsna has now finished instructing Uddhava. Next He glorifies in six textsthe power of what He has said: “Thus have I related to you - both in brief and in detail - a complete survey of the science of the Absolute Truth. Even for the demigods, this science is very difficult to comprehend. I have repeatedly spoken this knowledge to you with clear reasoning. Anyone who properly understands it will become free from all doubts and attain liberation.” (SB. 11.29.23-24) Sridhara Svami tells us that texts 23 and 24 of this twenty-ninth chapter sum up what the Uddhava-gita, which spanned chapters 7through 20 of the Eleventh Canto, is about. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura notes that even the demigods, who are in the mode of goodness, find it difficult to attain full knowledge of the Absolute Truth, because they (as well as the “empirically-inclined human beings”) are indifferent to the Supreme Lord and therefore “bound up in various kinds of false logic.”

According to Srila Jiva Gosvami, in text 24 Krsna is saying that mere liberation, not He Himself, is the fruit of the knowledge He has just spoken. But glorifying the value of studying, hearing, and sharing this knowledge with others, Sri Krsna adds, in texts 25 and 26: “Anyone who fixes his attention on these clear answers to your questions will attain to the eternal, confidential goal of the Vedas - the Supreme Absolute Truth. One who liberally disseminates this knowledge among My devotees bestows the Absolute Truth, and to him I give My very own self.” (SB. I 1.29.25—26)

About text 26 Srila Jiva Gosvami writes that the words, “I give My very own self” indicate that the Lord places Himself under the control of such a person. Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura adds. The expert devotees of the Supreme Personality of Godhead magnanimously bestow mercy on the living entities, and then these living entities obtain the opportunity to turn favorably toward devotional service. The Supreme Lord is in all ways obliged to those who \[in this way\] engage in the kirtana of hari-katha. But for those who are devoted to sense gratification and their own selfish happiness, the Supreme Lord is very difficult to attain.”

Sri Krsna continues: “He who loudly recites this supreme knowledge, which is the most lucid and purifying, becomes purified day by day, for he reveals Me to others with the lamp of transcendental knowledge.” (SB. 11.29.27)

Srila Sridhara Svami explains that those who recite this knowledge aloud purify themselves as well as others. Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that this purification occurs regardless of whether or not one understands the meaning of what one is reciting.

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura glorifies the devotees’ purity in his comment on this text: “Those who can understand the topics of devotional service become capable of driving off the darkness of ignorance with the torch of pure devotion. Becoming devoted to the Lord s service, that soul becomes supremely pure and clean. It is impossible for any darkness of ignorance to remain in such a supremely pure person.

Sri Krsna says further, speaking now about the power of His Uddhava-gita: “Anyone who regularly listens to this knowledge with faith and attention, all the while engaging in My pure devotional service, will never become bound by the reactions of material work. (SB. 11.29.28)

*Text 29: Have you understood?*

The Supreme Lord now asks Uddhava whether or not he has assimilated His message: “My dear friend Uddhava, have you now completely understood this transcendental knowledge? Are the confusion \[mohah\] and lamentation \[sokah\] that arose in your mind now dispelled?” (SB. 11.29.29)

As Krsna asked Arjuna in the Bhagavad-gita He now asks Uddhava. Each time He asks this question, He indicates that He is ready to repeat His instructions should Arjuna or Uddhava require Him to. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that Uddhava’s bewilderment was caused by Krsna, and that the Lord’s inquiry is playful, because He certainly knows that Uddhava is an eternally liberated soul. Srila Jiva Gosvami describes the nature of Uddhava’s confusion as “forgetting how the Lord and His energies are connected.” Uddhava’s anxiety about becoming separated from the Lordis a meaningless fear, because no such separation is actually possible. Uddhava is lamenting, Sri Jiva notes, because he thinks that when Krsna departs, he will not again be able to attain the Lord. Srila Jiva Gosvami then expresses what Krsna has hidden for Uddhava behind his words: “If all these different results are attainable simply by listening to or reciting this conversation we are having, then what doubt can remain in you \[about your always being with Me\], and what doubt need remain for others whom I have chosen?”

Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura says that the Lord’s mercy “dispels a living entity’s bewildering desire for sense gratification, with no possibility of his again falling under the sway of lust and lamentation.”

*Texts 30-34: The Uddhava-gita, the sum total of knowledge*

*Texts 30-31: Who should and shouldn’t hear the Uddhava-gita*

Seeing that Uddhava has understood His message, Krsna continues: “You should not share this instruction with anyone who is hypocritical, atheistic, or dishonest, or with anyone who will not listen faithfully, who is not a devotee, or who is simply not humble. This knowledge should be taught to one who is free from these bad qualities, who is dedicated to the welfare of the brahmanas, and who is kindly disposed, saintly, and pure. And if common workers and women are found to have devotion for the Supreme Lord, they are also to be accepted as qualified hearers.” (SB. 11.29.30-31)

Although the Lord somewhat strictly draws the line about suitable candidates for hearing His message, His generous-hearted devotees are still more liberal in distributing His purifying words. Srila Prabhupada addresses this topic in his purport to Bhagavad-gita 3.29: “Men who are ignorant cannot appreciate activities in Krsna consciousness, and therefore Lord Krsna advises us not to disturb them and simply waste valuable time. But the devotees of the Lord are more kind than the Lord because they understand the purpose of the Lord. Consequently they undertake all kinds of risks, even to the point of approaching ignorant men to try to engage them in the acts of Krsna consciousness, which are absolutely necessary for the human being.

*Text 32: The Uddhava-gita contains the perfection of knowledge*

The knowledge Krsna spoke will bring one all success. Anyone interested in deeper knowledge, knowledge about the soul, should examine this conversation, for, as Krsna states, “one who has drunk the most palatable nectar cannot remain thirsty.” (SB. 11.29.32)

*Texts 33-34: The perfection of all processes*

People usually attain their goals through analytic knowledge, ritualistic work, mystic yoga, mundane business, or political rule. Should Krsna s devotees find themselves with unwanted desires and goals, they nevertheless find their Lord the sole means to all ends. Krsna asks: What need does My devotee have to practice other methods? “\[B\]ecause you are My devotee, whatever men can accomplish in these multifarious ways you will very easily find within Me.” (SB. 11.29.33)

For pure devotees, however, the Lord is not a means to an end other than the end of attaining His service. Yet the results they achieve are greater than those of practitioners of all other paths and processes: A person who gives up all fruitive activities and offers himself entirely unto Me, eagerly desiring to render service unto Me, achieves liberation from birth and death and is promoted to the status of sharing My own opulences.” (SB. 11.29.34)

When describing the liberation of achieving opulences similar to those of the Lord (sarsti-mukti), Srila Jiva Gosvami cites Vedic texts that confirm the transcendental results Krsna just mentioned. From the Priti Sandarbha, anuccheda 13: “Sruti says sa tatra paryeti jaksan kridan ramamana - in the spiritual world he moves about, eats, plays, and enjoys (Chandogya Upanisad 8.12.3). Apnoti svarajyam sarve smai dew balim dharanti - he attains dominion over heaven, and the devatas offer him gifts (Taittinya Upanisad 1.6.2). Tasya sarvesu lokesu kama-caro bha-vati - he wanders freely in all the worlds (Chandogya Upanisad 7.23.2). Sarvesvarah - the liberated soul controls all beings (Brhadaranyaka Upanisad 4.4.22).”

In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.29.34, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes: “When a person, by the chance mercy of My devotee, gives up all his materially motivated daily and periodic duties and offers his full identity of ‘I’ and ‘mine’ by words and mind to his guru, who is My svarupa and who gives him My mantra, from that moment, that mortal person desires to work for Me, in bhakti-yoga, which is different from other forms of yoga and jnana. Such surrender is expressed in the Padma Parana: ‘O Lord! I offer everything related to “I” and “mine” in this life and the next to your lotus feet.’ ”

*Texts 35-40: Sri Uddhava’s response*

*Texts 35-36: Gratitude*

After having heard from Sri Krsna about the entire path of yoga, “Uddhava folded his hands to offer obeisances. But his throat choked up with love and his eyes overflowed with tears; so he could say nothing.” (SB. 11.29.35) He then steadied his mind and let himself feel the extreme gratitude that washed over him as he remembered the Lord’s kindness. He tried to ward off the painful feelings of his impending separation from the Lord that were rising within him. Then he “bowed down to touch the Lord’s lotus feet with his head and then spoke with folded hands.” (SB. 11.29.36)

*Texts 37-40 Ignorance dispelled*

Sri Uddhava said: “O unborn, primeval Lord, although I had fallen into the great darkness of illusion, my ignorance has now been dispelled by Your merciful association. Indeed, how can cold, darkness, and fear exert their power over one who has approached the brilliant sun?” (SB. 11.29.37)

In his comment on this text, Srila Jiva Gosvami suggests that Uddhava feels that Krsna’s presence, not to speak of His instructions - and especially His merciful glance - have themselves been enough to ward off illusion. Uddhava’s illusion has now been dispelled. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes Uddhava’s illusion as “the great darkness of the idea that Dvaraka, deprived of My Lord, who had been shining brilliantly among the Yadus, will now become a temporary place.” He adds, “Krsna has driven that delusion away.”

Uddhava continues: “In return for my insignificant surrender. You have mercifully bestowed upon me, Your servant, the torching to transcendental knowledge. Therefore, what devotee of Yours who has any gratitude could ever give up Your lotus feet and take shelter of another master?” (SB. 11.29.38) ,

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes Uddhava s thinking: “I have offered You my body along with my consciousness, intelligence, and senses, whereas You have offered me in return the lamp of divine knowledge and filled my consciousness with You. Therefore l am now fully satisfied, experiencing at every moment Your sweetness I am also experiencing You as present in all times and places along with all Your entourage. Therefore please do whatever You wish to do with my body. Wherever You want to place it, please do that, and if You wish to keep it here, then do that. After all, what grateful servant can give up Your lotus feet to seek shelter elsewhere, even in his own home? But it one who remains in one’s home gains a direct experience of You then he should stay there. He will not be at fault for that. Rather, he should simply remain in whatever position he has been assigned.”

Uddhava next reveals the detachment Krsna’s words have evoked m him: “The firmly binding rope of my affection for the families of the Dasarhas, Vrsnis, Andhakas, and Satvatas - a rope You originally cast over me by Your illusory energy for the purpose of developing Your creation - is now cut off by the weapon of transcendental knowledge of the self.” (SB. 11.29.39) ,

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains more about Uddhava s cutting off affection for his family members, who were, after all, great devotees of Krsna: “I have two kinds of bondage of affection for the Yadavas. The ropes of affection of false identification that You cast through Your illusory energy in order to increase Your creation, I this affection being expressed in such terms as\] ‘May the Yadu dynasty increase perpetually in the form of sons and grandsons and thus our goo prosperity continue until the end of Brahma’s day. May we expand in all directions and into all countries while remaining all-victorious this ego-based bond of affection has been cut off by the weapon of proper knowledge of the self. But that affection I have for them that is based on tasting the sweetness of Your personality and qualities, discussing You and rendering service to You, still ornaments me.”

Uddhava wants to extinguish all desires extraneous to his focus on loving service to the lotus feet of Krsna. His final words now express that desire, which is blazing in the core of his heart: “Obeisances unto You, O greatest of yogis. Please instruct me, who am surrendered unto You, how I may have undeviating attachment to Your lotus feet.” (SB. 11.29.40)

Srila Sridhara Svami writes that Uddhava’s love for Krsna will not be lost even when he attains liberation; he will remain a surrendered, loving devotee of his Lord. Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that Uddhava speaks more prayers at this point, crying pitifully as he falls to the ground in obeisance. In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 335), Sri Jiva also notes Uddhava’s intention in speaking these words, quoting Srila Sridhara Svami: “You have already shown me so much favor, but I have one more request. Please instruct me how to gain unending attachment to Your lotus feet, an attachment that will remain even after liberation.”

*Texts 41-44: Krsnas final instructions to Uddhava*

Srila Jiva Gosvami’s comments on this section introduce Krsna’s final instructions to Uddhava: “You have already achieved the attraction for My lotus feet that you have prayed for, and by your feelings of separation from Me, that attraction will automatically increase. So you do not need to consider any other means for achieving that attraction. Nevertheless, for the sake of instructing the general populace, you should carry out My instructions, which will inevitably be difficult for you to execute because you are feeling such separation from Me... And then, when you have succeeded in carrying out My desire that you instruct the world, your own personal desire will be achieved.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also explains Krsna’s reason for giving Uddhava the specific instructions He will now deliver: “My dear Uddhava, among the Yadavas, who are My personal entourage, you are most equal to Me. You are My very image.Therefore, whatever I could have done I can still do through you. As previously I sent you to Vraja-bhumi, I now want to send you to Badarikasrama. There, My plenary expansions Sri Nara-Narayana Rsi, the Lords of the greatest of sages, want to see Me. When I visited various places on the surface of the earth, such as Mithila, and the subterranean regions, Vaikuntha, and other places, the residents of each of these places became perfectly satisfied by receiving My audience and instructions. But I am unable to go to Badarikasrama now, because I have completed the prescribed time 125 years - of My incarnation. Therefore, since you have asked Me to instruct you, who are surrendered to Me, this is what I ask of you at the moment.”

On His order, Krsna says, Uddhava should go to Badarikasrama. There, he should purify himself by touching the holy waters that have emanated from Krsna’s lotus feet and then should bathe in those waters. “Rid yourself of all sinful reactions with the sight of the sacred Alakananda River.” (SB. 11.29.41-44)

Krsna tells Uddhava to perform austerities at Badarikasrama: Dress yourself in bark and eat whatever is naturally available in the forest.” And while doing all this, Krsna says, maintain a pleasant but profound consciousness. “Thus you should remain content and free from desire, tolerant of all dualities, good-natured, self-controlled, peaceful, and endowed with transcendental knowledge and realization.” (SB. 11.29.41-44)

Srila Jiva Gosvami states that the qualities of being happy, free from desires, and so on, are innate to Uddhava’s character. He also says that Lord Hari is sending Uddhava to Badarikasrama because for Uddhava to remain in Dvaraka would be too painful, since he had seen the Lord enact so many of His pastimes there.

Supported by these practices and seeking no pleasure from the realm of matter, Krsna tells Uddhava how to increase his attachment to Him: “With fixed attention, meditate constantly upon these instructions I have imparted to you and assimilate their essence. Fix your words and thoughts upon Me, and always endeavor to increase your realization of My transcendental qualities.” (SB. 11.29.41-44)

Uddhava should deeply meditate on the Uddhava-gita, because m it Krsna spoke many layers of instructions. The Lord wants Uddhava to assimilate the essence of what He taught him. Through this meditation and while doing all other things, Uddhava should focus his thoughts solely on Krsna. All his endeavors should be similarly focused on deepening his realization of Krsna’s nature and qualities. As a result, Uddhava will feel an ever-increasing attachment to Krsna. And, Krsna concludes, “In this way you will cross beyond the destinations of the three modes of nature and finally come back to Me.”

Again, Sri Krsna is instructing Uddhava for others’ benefit, because Uddhava is already perfect. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes about these texts that Krsna addresses Uddhava with the words “O Uddhava” because Uddhava quite literally fits the description of lus name - uddhava means “festival.” By his Krsna conscious presence, he creates a festival for everyone. Now, Krsna continues, I have given you the ability to create special festivals for all people by bestowing on you My personal potencies of knowledge, renunciation, and so on, which are present within Me. Merely by your glance, all the sinful reactions of the Alakananda will be washed away and eradicated.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura continues: ‘“When Nara-Narayana and the other rsis residing at Badarikasrama ask you, you should teach them the knowledge you have learned directly from Me about bhakti, jnana, and vairagya, for it contains special discriminations.

“By absorbing your words and mind in Me, be mad-dharma - always absorbed in contemplation of My brilliant intelligence, omniscience, omnipotency, and so on, which are all fixed within Me. In this way the Lord offers Uddhava the benediction of becoming qualified to be perfectly absorbed in meditation on His different qualities… Having carried out My order, you will come to Me. Or in other words, being led by Me through My mystic power, you will return here (to the eternal abode of Dvaraka) and will again be in My close association.”

*Texts 45-47: Uddhava departs for Badarikasrama*

Sukadeva Gosvami said: “Thus addressed by Lord Krsna, whose intelligence destroys all the suffering of material life, Sri Uddhava circumambulated the Lord and then fell down, placing his head upon the Lord’s feet. Although Uddhava was free from the influence of all material dualities, his heart was breaking, and at this time of departure he drenched the Lord’s lotus feet with his tears. Greatly fearing separation from Him for whom he felt such indestructible affection, Uddhava was distraught, and he could not give up the Lord’s company. Finally, feeling great pain, he bowed down to the Lord again and again, placed the slippers of his master upon his head, and departed.” (SB. 11.29.45-46)

The BBT purport to text 46 explains that Uddhava did not go immediately to Badarikasrama. Rather, after leaving Dvaraka, he turned west to again meet the Lord at Prabhasa, the holy place on the bank of the Sarasvati, after the Yadu dynasty had been destroyed: “According to the Srimad-Bhagavatam (3.4.5), while Uddhava was en route to Badarikasrama lie heard about the Lord’s journey to Prabhasa. Turning back and following behind Lord Krsna, he met the Lord as He salt alone just after the withdrawal of the Yadu dynasty. After being again mercifully instructed by the Personality of Godhead (along with Maitreya, who also had just arrived), Uddhava felt his knowledge of the truth reawaken, and then, by the order of the Lord, he went on his way.”

In his comment on text 45, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura tells us that although Uddhava was not absorbed in material dualities, he was nevertheless “decorated by lamentation and bewilderment based on his pure love for Krsna.” .

Sukadeva Gosvami’s narration of Uddhava’s departure to Badarikasrama continues: “Thereupon, placing the Lord deeply within his heart, the great devotee Uddhava went to Badarikasrama. By engaging there in austerities, he attained to the Lord’s personal abode, which had been described to him by the only friend of the universe, Lord Krsna Himself.” (SB. 11.29.47)

Thus Uddhava completed his journey back to Krsna by attaining the eternal land of Dvaraka in the spiritual world, with the Lord awarding him what He had promised him: “O Vasu, I know from within your mind what you desired in the days of yore when the Vasus and other demigods responsible for expanding the universal affairs performed sacrifices. You particularly desired to achieve My association. This is very difficult to obtain for others, but I award it unto you. (SB. 3.4-11)

In the Priti Sandarbha (anuccheda 217), Srila Jiva Gosvami comments that due to Uddhava’s strong desire, he also attained Krsna in Vrndavana in an expanded form:“The gopis of Vrndavana have given up the association of their husbands, sons, and other family members, who are very difficult to give up, and they have forsaken their relatives and the path of dharma to obtain the lotus feet of Mukunda, Krsna, which even the Vedas pursue. Oh, let me be fortunate enough to be one of the bushes, creepers, or herbs in Vrndavana, because the gopis bless them with the dust of their lotus feet.” (SB. 10.47.61)

*Texts 48-49: A benediction before Sukadeva Gosvami concludes*

“Thus Lord Krsna, whose lotus feet are served by all great yoga masters, spoke to His devotee this nectarean knowledge, which comprises the entire ocean of spiritual bliss. Anyone within this universe who receives this narration with great faith is assured of liberation. (SB. 11.29.48)

Srila Sridhara Svami indicates the immense potency of the Uddhava-gita: “One who, with transcendental faith, engages in even a little service (to the Uddhava-gita), in which the ocean of the bliss of the path of devotional service to the Supreme Lord is brought together under one heading, becomes liberated. What to speak of his own liberation, by his association the whole universe becomes liberated.”

Sukadeva Gosvami completes the Uddhava-gita by offering his respects to both the conclusive knowledge he has offered Maharaja Pariksit and to the speaker of that knowledge, Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “I offer my obeisances to that Supreme Personality of Godhead, the original and greatest of all beings, Lord Sri Krsna \[krsna-samjnam\]. He is the author of the Vedas, and just to destroy His devotees’ fear of material existence, like a bee (bhrriga-vat) He has collected this nectarean essence of all knowledge and self-ralization. Thus He has awarded to His many devotees this nectar from the ocean of bliss, and by His mercy they have drunk it.” (SB. 11.29.49) Srila Sridhara Svami concludes his comments on this chapter by offering his obeisances to Sri Krsna: “Because He has bestowed His mercy on the whole universe by answering Uddhava’s questions, it is to Him, the supreme reservoir of ecstasy in the form of the son of Nanda Maharaja, that I offer my homage.”

In his own comment on this closing text, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura describes Krsna as the Supreme Personality of Godhead and the Supreme Truth with no beginning. He adds that Krsna is the only worthy shelter for us all: “By giving instructions He wards off the living entity’s fear of material existence. He bestows the essence of knowledge and realization, pure love of Krsna, on the spirit souls, who are indifferent to devotional service. He is the promulgator of the Vedic literature, and He gives the essence of the Vedas to the Vaisnavas, who take to that essence like bees to nectar. Giving up all other dharmas and accepting His shelter is the only proper resort for all beings.”

The BBT’s final purport in this chapter expands on Srila Sukadeva Gosvami’s use of the phrase bhrriga-vat, “like a bee”: “Just as a bee extracts nectar from a flower without harming the flower, Lord Sri Krsna extracts the essence of all Vedic knowledge without disturbing the elaborate system of Vedic advancement. In other words, Lord Sri Krsna establishes Himself as the goal of Vedic knowledge without destroying preliminary, inferior processes that may be applicable to grossly materialistic men. Sri Sukadeva Gosvami thus concludes by offering his obeisances to the spiritual master of the entire universe, Lord Sri Krsna.”

## Dialogue 7. Lord Krsna’s disappearance

**Chapters 30 and 31: The Seed of the Pastime Bears Fruit - Krsna and the Yadu Dynasty Leave the Earth**

**Chapter 30: The Disappearance of the Yadu Dynasty**

*Texts 1-3: Pariksit Maharaja inquires further*

Starting in Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.3.24, Sri Uddhava has already described in essence the events that precede these last two chapters of the Eleventh Canto: “Once upon a time, great sages were made angry by the sporting activities of the princely descendants of the Yadu and Bhoja dynasties, and thus, as desired by the Lord, the sages cursed them. Then after a few months, foreboding omens manifest in Dvaraka.”

Uddhava had seen these omens in Dvaraka, and because the dhama is fully spiritual and eternally protected by Lord Krsna, he had become anxious and sought the Lord’s shelter; he could understand with his piercing intelligence that the omens could only indicate the Lord’s imminent departure from the earth. In the Eleventh Canto recounting of this event, Uddhava says: “My Lord, it appears that You will now withdraw Your dynasty, and thus You Yourself will finally give up Your pastimes within t his universe. You are the supreme controller and the master of all mystic power. But although You are fully capable of counteracting the brahmanas’ curse against Your dynasty, You are not doing so, and Your disappearance is imminent.” (SB. 11.6.42)

Alter hearing Uddhava’s words, Krsna spoke to Uddhava the instructions that form the Uddhava-gita (chapters 6-29), and then, following Krsna’s order, Uddhava left.

Having heard all this,Pariksit Maharaja asks two questions in the first two texts of chapter 30: “After the great devotee Uddhava left for the forest, what did the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the protector of all living beings, do in the city of Dvaraka?... \[H\]ow could the best of the Yadus give up His body, the dearmost object of all eyes?” (SB. 11.30.1-2)

Aware that Krsna’s disappearance is imminent, Maharaja Pariksit wants to hear the mysterious pastime surrounding Krsna’s giving up of His body, for the Lord’s body is eternal, blissful, and complete in knowledge - and nondifferent from Him. In his comment on text 2, Srila Jiva Gosvami provides some context to Maharaja Pariksit s questions: ‘“How did He give it up?’ In other words, ‘He did not give it up.’ And thus King Pariksit reveals the inner thought of his heart. The reason \[for his questions\] is as follows: ‘Because of \[that body\] being the embodiment of supreme ecstasy, on account of it being the reservoir of the transcendental love of everyone, it could not be... afflicted or destroyed by the curse of the brahmanas. How could He give up that most dear transcendental body, which was the most favored of all eyes, including the eyes of Lord Mahadeva?... It is not possible that He has given it up! It is impossible for that body to be given up, because it is constituted as eternal knowledge and bliss.... It is the same as saying that a person with a gold pot filled with water left the pot behind because it was too heavy to carry as he walked down the road. Actually, the labor of carrying the full pot was too great, but the person poured the water out and kept what was truly valuable - the gold pot.’ ”

In his comment on text 1, Srila Sridhara Svami notes that Sukadeva Gosvami narrated Krsna’s mausala-lila to encourage a sense of renunciation in Maharaja Pariksit, since the king’s own time in the world is almost at an end. In the mausala4lld, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains, at Prabhasa, Krsna will cause the demise of those Yadus who are demigods helping the Lord in His pastimes on earth (SB. 10.1.21-23). After reestablishing them in their heavenly abodes, He Himself will return to the spiritual realm with those among the Yadus who are His personal expansions.

Before Sukadeva Gosvami responds to Pariksit Maharajas request to hear more about the Lord’s departure pastime, Maharaja Pariksit describes the Lord’s unlimited beauty and the power of His form. It’s important for him to speak about the Lord’s form in these ways because it seems too impossible that Lord Krsna could have given up His body and died like any ordinary conditioned soul.

But how does one describe a body that is spiritual and unlimitedly beautiful, a body whose all-attractive beauty is beyond what a material mind can experience? The king cannot do it, so instead he speaks of the overpowering effect Krsna’s form has on others: “Once their eyes were fixed upon His transcendental form, women were unable to withdraw them, and once that form had entered the ears of the sages and become fixed in their hearts, it would never depart. What to speak of acquiring fame, the great poets who described the beauty of the Lord’s form would have their words invested with transcendentally pleasing attraction. And by seeing that form on Arjuna’s chariot, all the warriors on the battlefield of Kuruksetra attained the liberation of gaining a spiritual body similar to the Lord’s.” (SB. 11.30.3)

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 226), Srila Jiva Gosvami cites Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.15.49 to give us further insight into what it’s like to experience Krsna’s transcendental form. \[The four Kumaras say:\] “Let us remain in hellish existence because of sinful actions, if our minds can achieve prema at your lotus feet like bees which are not injured by the thorns as they taste the honey, if our words can remain glorious at your lotus feet like tulasl leaves, and if our ear holes can remain filled with hearing your qualities.”

Considering the electrifying potency of Krsna’s form, clearly His appearance in this world as well as His departure from it are mysterious. Krsna Himself speaks about the confidentiality of these pastimes, as well as the power of understanding them, in Bhagavad-gita 4-9: “One who knows the transcendental nature of My appearance and activities does not, upon leaving the body, take his birth again in this material world, but attains My eternal abode, O Arjuna.”

To properly understand Krsna’s coming to the material world and His departure from it, one must hear from one who knows these pastimes in truth.Srila Prabhupada explains this in his purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.1.13: “The conditions for hearing the transcendental message of the Absolute Truth are set forth herein. The first condi- tion is that the audience must be very sincere and eager to hear. And the speaker must be in the line of disciplic succession from the recognized deary a, The transcendental message of the Absolute is not understandable by those who are materially absorbed.”

Here are four statements, one by Sukadeva Gosvami and three by Srila Prabhupada that describe the supramundane nature of Krsna’s pastimes, including His appearance and disappearance from this world.

Sukadeva Gosvami replied: My dear King, the cursing of the brahmanas was only a plea, but the actual fact was the supreme desire of the Lord. He wanted to disappear from the face of the earth after dispatching His excessively numerous family members. (SB. 3.4.29)

As the sun appears in the morning and gradually rises to the meridian and then again sets in one hemisphere while simultaneously rising in the other, so Lord Krsna’s disappearance in one universe and the beginning of His different pastimes in another take place simultaneously. As soon as one pastime is finished here, it is manifested in another universe... But wherever the Lord is present, all His different pastimes as described in the revealed scriptures take place at regular intervals. (SB. 3.2.7, purport)

\[S\]ometimes a governor goes to inspect a prison. He gets reports from the prison superintendent, so he has no business going there, but still he sometimes goes, thinking, “Let me see how they are doing.” This may be called a pastime because he is going by his free will. It is not that he has become subject to the laws of the prison. But still a foolish prisoner may think, “Oh, here the governor is also in prison. So we are equal. I am also governor.” Rascals think like that. “Because Krsna has descended as an avatara," they say, “I am also an avatara.” So here it is said, na veda kascid bhagavams cikirsitam: “No one knows the purpose of Your appearance and disappearance.” Tavehamanasya nrnam videimbanam. the Lords pastimes are bewildering. No one can understand their real purpose. (Teachings of Queen Kunti, p. 84, 1992 ed.)

In Srimad-Bhagavatam, Third Canto, verses 28 and 29, there is a description of Krsna’s leaving His body. Maharaja Pariksit inquired from Sukadeva Gosvami, “When all the members of the Yadu dynasty met their end, Krsna also put an end to Himself, and the only member of the family who remained alive was Uddhava. How was this possible?" Sukadeva Gosvami answered that Krsna, by His own energy, destroyed the entire family and then thought of making His own body disappear. In this connection, Sukadeva Gosvami described how the Lord gave up His body. But this was not the destruction of Krsna’s body; rather, it was the disappearance of the Supreme Lord by His personal energy. (SB. 10.3.46, purport)

*Texts 4-25: The destruction of the Yadu dynasty*

In text 4, Sukadeva Gosvami begins to answer Maharaja Pariksit’s first question, which he asked in text 1: “After the great devotee Uddhava left for the forest, what did the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the protector of all living beings, do in the city of Dvaraka?” The answer to this question will lead us to the description of Sri Krsna’s departure from the world.

Sukadeva tells Pariksit that Sri Krsna went to the Sudharma Council Hall to address the Yadus, who had become fearful due to the inauspicious omens. Krsna too had observed the omens - the halo around the sun, the small earthquakes, and the unnatural red smear on the horizon. Speaking with authority the Lord said, “O leaders of the Yadu dynasty, please note all these terrible omens that have appeared in Dvaraka just like the flags of death. We should not remain here a moment longer. The women, children, and old men should leave this city and go to Sankhoddhara, and we men proceed to Prabhasa-ksetra, where the river Sarasvati flows toward the west.” (SB. 11.30.5-6) In Prabhasa the men should purify themselves by bathing, fasting, and meditating with focused minds. They should worship the devatas under the brahmanas’ guidance and then remunerate those brahmanas with gold, land, cows, dwellings, and other valuables. These acts, Krsna said, would counteract the current adversities facing the Yadus and award them good fortune.

The Yadu elders agreed to Krsna’s plan with the words “So be it.” They left Dvaraka quickly, sending away their women, children, and old men as Krsna had instructed, while they sailed from their island city and then proceeded by chariot to Prabhasa. There, the Yadu men performed the religious rites the Lord had recommended. But “their intelligence covered by Providence, they liberally indulged in drinking the sweet maireya beverage, which can completely intoxicate the mind.” (SB. 11.30.12) Intoxicated with both wine and arrogance, and bewildered by the Lord’s personal potency (krsna-maya-vimudhanam), the warriors quarreled and then began to fight among themselves. Armed and enraged, the Yadu heroes gave up their friendship and violently attacked and slaughtered one another. Thus they were completely bewildered by Lord Mukunda Himself (mukundena vimohta bhrsam, SB. 11.30.17).

“When all their bows had been broken and their arrows and other missiles spent, they seized the tall stalks of cane with their bare hands.As soon as they took these cane stalks in their fists, the stalks changed into iron rods as hard as thunderbolts. With these weapons the warriors began attacking one another again and again, and when Lord Krsna tried to stop them they attacked Him as well. In their confused state, O King, they also mistook Lord Balarama for an enemy. Weapons in hand, they ran toward Him with the intention of killing Him. O son of the Kurus, Krsna and Balarama then became very angry. Picking up cane stalks, They moved about within the battle and began to kill with these clubs. The violent anger of these warriors, who were overcome by the brahmanas’ curse and bewildered by Lord Krsna’s illusory potency, now led them to their annihilation, just as a fire that starts in a bamboo grove destroys the entire forest. When all the members of His own dynasty were thus destroyed, Lord Krsna thought to Himself that at last the burden of the earth had been removed.” (SB. 11.30.20—25)

In his comment on text 25, Jiva Gosvami explains that the Yadu dynasty was “the burden of the earth” in the sense that the Yadavas extreme unhappiness after Krsna’s departure would have been impossible for the earth to bear.

*Text 26: Lord Balarama departs*

“Lord Balarama then sat down on the shore of the ocean and fixed Himself in meditation upon the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Merging Himself within Himself, He gave up this mortal world.”

In his comment on text 27, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that when Lord Balarama “passed away,” He returned both to Maha-vaikuntha in His original form and to the Patala region in His partial expansion as Sesa. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also notes that texts 12-26 express not the factual truth “but the opinions of others.” The Yadavas had performed rituals and given charity as Sr. Krsna had advised (SB. 11.6.37-38), and so (he demtas, on the strength of the Lord’s words, overcame the brahmanas’ curse. The Lord earlier explained His own version of the Yadus’ disappearance pastime in Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.3.15: “When they quarrel among themselves, influenced by intoxication, with their eyes red like copper because of drinking \[madhu\], then only will they disappear; otherwise, it will not be possible. On My disappearance, this incident will take place.”

Srila Prabhupada gives the philosophical conclusion of this subject in his purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.3.15: “The Lord and His associates appear and disappear by the will of the Lord. They are not subjected to the laws of material nature. No one was able to kill the family of the Lord, nor was there any possibility of their natural death by the laws of nature. The only means, therefore, for their disappearance was the make-show of a fight amongst themselves, as if brawling in intoxication due to drinking. That so-called fighting would also take place by the will of the Lord, otherwise there would be no cause for their fighting.”

The Battle of Kuruksetra, with its battlefield extending across one hundred miles and filled with dead bodies, and the dying of the Yadu dynasty, after its countless family members beat one another to death, are gruesome scenes. And indeed the events were gruesome, as wars will be: “In the course of the battle, the warfield became strewn with the severed heads of heroes, their eyes still staring and their teeth still pressed against their lips in anger. Helmets and earrings were scattered from these severed heads. Similarly, many arms, decorated with ornaments and clutching various weapons, were strewn here and there, as were many legs and thighs, which resembled the trunks of elephants.” (SB. 8.10.39)

Yet Krsna wanted both the fighting at the Battle of Kuruksetra and between His own family members. Devotees with a deep understanding can envision Krsna’s divine will being enacted through such pastimes and know that His causeless mercy will flow to all who participate in them. Indeed, all those who died in Krsna’s presence at Kuruksetra achieved liberation: “\[Ejveryone who died in His presence attained complete liberation from material bondage and was transferred to the spiritual world.” (SB. 10.2.35, purport) And, of course, all the members of the Yadu dynasty, who were His eternal associates and who perished at Prabhasa-ksetra returned to associate with Him in the spiritual world: “The fortunes of the Yadu dynasty and that of the inhabitants of the land of Mathura cannot be materially estimated. If simply by knowing the transcendental nature of the birth and activities of the Lord one can get liberation easily, we can just imagine what is in store for those who actually enjoyed the company of the Lord in person as a family member or as a neighbor.” (SB. 1.10.26, purport)

*Texts 27-50: The departure of Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead*

*Texts 27-33: Setting the scene - Jara shoots his bow*

“Lord Krsna, the son of Devaki, having seen the departure of Lord Rama (Balarama), sat down silently on the ground under a nearby pippala tree.” (SB. 11.30.27) His beautiful, dark-complexioned, fourarmed form was fully decorated. The Lord sat with His left foot, pinkish lotus sole upward and resting on His left thigh. His effulgence was golden. Srila Sridhara Svami adds that Krsna’s form was also decorated by His lotus face and beautiful smile, His beautiful eyes, which were as attractive as lotuses, His limbs covered by a flower garland, and the weapons He was holding.

“Just then a hunter named Jara, who had approached the place, mistook the Lord’s foot for a deer’s face. Thinking he had found his prey, Jara pierced the foot with his arrow, which he had fashioned from the remaining iron fragment of Samba’s club.” (SB. 11.30.33)

*Texts 34-38: Jara’s sorrow*

Thinking he had pierced a wonderful four-armed person and terrified by the offense he had just committed, Jara fell before the Lord, his head on His feet. In his comment on text 33, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that the hunter mistakenly thought he had shot and pierced a deer. His arrow actually could not have pierced “the Lord’s eternal, blissful, and knowledge-filled limbs.” Rather, the hunter’s arrow only grazed the Lord’s foot. If it had been otherwise, “the hunter would surely have removed the arrow before placing his head on the Lord’s foot.”

“Jara said: O Lord Madhusudana, I am a most sinful person.I have committed this act out of ignorance. O purest Lord, O Uttama-sloka, please forgive this sinner. O Lord Visnu, the learned say that for any man, constant remembrance of You will destroy the darkness of ignorance. O master, I have wronged You! Therefore, O Lord of Vaikuntha, please kill this sinful hunter of animals immediately so he may not again commit such offenses against saintly persons. Neither Brahma nor his sons, headed by Rudra, nor any of the great sages who are masters of the Vedic mantras can understand the function of Your mystic power. Because Your illusory potency has covered their sight, they remain ignorant of how Your mystic power works. Therefore, what can I, such a low-born person, possibly say?” (SB. 11.30.35-38)

The BBT purport to text 37 includes Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s explanation of both the battle among the Yadavas and the shooting by the hunter of Lord Krsna. Cakravarti Thakura emphasizes the nonliteral, prearranged, dramatic quality of Krsna’s disappearance pastime: “According to the evidence, the quarrel among the members of the Yadu dynasty occurred at sunset; then the Lord sat down on the bank of the Sarasvati River. It is stated that a hunter then arrived with the intention of killing a deer, but it is highly unlikely - when more than 560 million warriors had just been killed in a great uproarious battle and the place had been flooded with blood and strewn with corpses - that a simple hunter would somehow come along trying to kill a deer. Since deer are by nature fearful and timid, how could any deer possibly be on the scene of such a huge battle, and how could a hunter calmly go about his business in the midst of such carnage? Therefore, the withdrawal of the Yadu dynasty and Lord Krsna’s own disappearance from this earth were not material historical events; they were instead a display of the Lord’s internal potency for the purpose of winding up His manifest pastimes on earth.”

*Texts 39-40: Sri Krsna replies to Jara*

“The Supreme Personality of Godhead said: My dear Jara, do not fear. Please get up. What has been done is actually My own desire. With My permission, go now to the abode of the pious, the spiritual world. So instructed by the Supreme Lord Krsna, who assumes His transcendental body by His own will, the hunter circumambulated the Lord three times and bowed down to Him. Then the hunter departed in an airplane that had appeared just to carry him to the spiritual sky.” (SB. I 1.10.19—40)

*Texts 41-50: Daruka’s final meeting with his Lord*

“At that time Daruka was searching for his master, Krsna. As he neared the place where the Lord was sitting, he perceived the aroma of tulasi flowers in the breeze and went in its direction. Upon seeing Lord Krsna resting at the foot of a banyan tree, surrounded by His shining weapons, Daruka could not control the affection he felt in his heart. His eyes filled with tears as he rushed down from the chariot and fell at the Lord’s feet.

“Daruka said: Just as on a moonless night people are merged into darkness arid cannot find their way, now that I have lost sight of Your lotus feet, my Lord, I have lost my vision and am wandering blindly in darkness. I cannot tell my direction, nor can I find any peace.” (SB. 11.30.41-43)

The Lord’s effulgent chariot then rose up into the sky, along with its horses and flag. His divine weapons soon followed. Daruka watched with astonishment, and then the Lord spoke.

*Texts 46-48: Krsna offers Daruka one final service*

Sri Krsna said: “O driver, go to Dvaraka and tell Our family members how their loved ones destroyed one another. Also tell them of the disappearance of Lord Sankarsana and of My present condition. You and your relatives should not remain in Dvaraka, the capital of the Yadus, because once I have abandoned that city it will be inundated by the ocean. You should all take your own families, together with My parents, and under Arjuna’s protection go to Indraprastha.” (SB. 11.30.46-48)

*Text 49: Krsna instructs Daruka*

To pacify Daruka’s distress, Krsna informs him that this pastime of the Yadu dynasty’s disappearance and then His own are only as real as a magician’s tricks: “You, Daruka, should be firmly situated in devotion to Me, remaining fixed in spiritual knowledge and unattached to material considerations. Understanding these pastimes to be a display of My illusory potency, you should remain peaceful. (SB. 1 1.30.46)

Hearing his Lord’s words, Daruka circumambulated Lord Krsna and lotus feet on his head as he accepted the Lord’s order. Daruka was pacified, for he had heard the Lord’s explanation that everything was happening by His desire and as a display of His energies. Daruka then sadly returned to Dvaraka.

In his comment on text 49, Srila Sridhara Svami expresses Krsna’s desire that Daruka not grieve unnecessarily on account of the disappearance of the Lord’s divine form. Srila Jiva Gosvami further explains Krsna’s instructions to Daruka in the Krsna Sandarbha (anuccheda 123): “Daruka, remaining indifferent to the lamentation that will arise in your heart if you see this pastime with external vision, fixed in knowledge and knowing the truth of My pastimes, free from agitation of the heart and trusting what you know - that it is My nature to be with My associates as an equal and yet to protect them, and that this disappearance pastime is an illusion I am revealing at this time - you will attain Me.”

“Others would be bewildered,” Srila Sridhara Svami states, “but it is not suitable for Daruka to be bewildered, since Daruka is eternal, having descended from Vaikuntha.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains, in his comment on text 46, that the Lord’s chariot was sent to Vaikuntha although Daruka, the Lord’s charioteer, remained behind to perform the service of informing others of the Lord’s departure. Once he had completed that service, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti explains, Daruka reentered Krsna’s unmanifest pastimes in Dvaraka.

**Chapter 31: The Disappearance of Lord Sri Krsna**

*Texts 1-6: Lord Sri Krsna departs*

Eager to witness Lord Krsna’s departure, Brahma and Siva, along with their consorts, as well as many great sages, the demigods headed by Indra, and other exalted persons, arrived at Prabhasa. All of them were chanting about Krsna’s glorious birth and activities. Crowding the sky with their airplanes, they showered down flowers with great devotion.

It was as if the demigods and their consorts were the attending aristocracy at the festive finale of a grand drama, for they knew the Lord would now conclude His pastimes in this universe. Their mood was philosophically accurate and excellent, hut it lacked the extreme ecstatic feelings of separation experienced by the intimate participants in Krsna’s lila.

Bhumidevi, the earth goddess, was one such intimate participant, and she describes her mood at Krsna’s departure in Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.16.35: “Who, therefore, can tolerate the pangs of separation from that Supreme Personality of Godhead? He could conquer the gravity and passionate wrath of His sweethearts like Satyabhama by His sweet smile of love, pleasing glance, and hearty appeals. When He traversed my surface, I would be immersed in the dust of His lotus feet and thus would be sumptuously covered with grass, which appeared like hairs standing on me out of pleasure.”

In his purport to this text Srila Prabhupada magnifies Bhumidevi s heartfelt mood: “There were chances of separation between the Lord and His thousands of queens because of the Lord’s being absent from home, but as far as His connection with earth was concerned, the Lord would traverse the earth with His lotus feet, and therefore there was no chance of separation. When the Lord left the surface of the earth to return to His spiritual abode, the earth’s feelings of separation were therefore more acute.”

Krsna’s disappearance lila continues: “Seeing before Him Brahma, the grandfather of the universe, along with the other demigods, who are all His personal and powerful expansions, the Almighty Lord closed His lotus eyes \[padma-netre nyamilayat\], fixing His mind within Himself, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Without employing the mystic agneyi meditation to burn up His transcendental body, which is the all-attractive resting place of all the worlds and the object of all contemplation and meditation, Lord Krsna entered into His own abode.” (SB. 11.31.5-6)

Lord Krsna had previously promised Brahma (SB. 11.6.31) that “when this annihilation is finished and I am en route to Vaikuntha, I will pay a small visit to your abode.” The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.5 humorously notes Srila Sndhara Svami’s comment on why the Lord closed His eyes: “Lord Krsna had previously answered the prayers of Lord Brahma and the other demigods, who had requested the Lord to descend within this universe for the protection of His servants, the demigods. Now the demigods arrived before the Lord, each one desiring to take the Lord to his own planet. To avoid these innumerable social obligations, the Lord closed His eyes as if absorbed in samadhi."

Further, commenting on text 6, Srila Sridhara Svami notes the error in thinking that the Lord leaves His body by His own will in the same way the yogis do - through the agneyi process. Sripada Madhvacarya explains a similar point, saying that all others, including the demigods, enter the supreme abode by burning their bodies through the agneyi meditation, but Lord Hari’s body is different from the body of yogis. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes how Krsna doesn’t use the mystic yoga processes at the time of His departure: “Taking His body, which was pure, like gold, as if being taken from the fire after heating it and without it being burned up, He entered His own abode. Thus the Lord showed doubtful persons that His body could not be burned.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami also comments on text 6 in the Krsna Sandarbha (anuccheda 93). He writes that Lord Krsna’s body is transcendental and the auspicious object of all meditation and trance (dharana-dhyana-mangalam). If His body were not real (that is, not eternal), meditation on Him would have no real and worthwhile object. But “even today,” Srila Jiva writes, “it is seen that worshipers of the Lord see Him and attain the result of seeing Him.”

“As soon as Lord Sri Krsna left the earth, Truth, Religion, Faithfulness, Glory, and Beauty immediately followed Him. Kettledrums resounded in the heavens and flowers showered from the sky.” (SB. 11.31.7)

Citing Srila Sridhara Svarni, the BBT purport describes the demigods’ festive mood as “jubilant because each one thought Lord Krsna was coming to his own planet.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura focuses on Sri Krsna’s departure in his comment on text 7, along with the disappearance of Truth, Religion, Faithfulness, Glory, and Beauty. Their departure, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains, allowed unfavorable, Kali-yuga qualities to become prominent.

*Texts 8-13: Understanding the Lord’s mysterious departure*

“Most of the demigods and other higher beings led by Brahma could not see Lord Krsna as He was entering His own abode, since He did not reveal His movements. But some of them did catch sight of Him, and they were extremely amazed. Just as ordinary men cannot ascertain the path of a lightning bolt as it leaves a cloud, the demigods could not trace out the movements of Lord Krsna as He returned to His abode. A few of the demigods, however - notably Lord Brahma and Lord Siva — could ascertain how the Lord’s mystic power was working, and thus they became astonished. All the demigods praised the Lord’s mystic power and then returned to their own planets.” (SB. 11.31.8-10)

In his comments on text 8, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura addresses the demigods’ amazement: “The devatas were astonished. ‘We thought that we were masters of yoga, but nevertheless we are unable to understand where He has gone.’ In this way they praised Krsna. Who can do such a thing? We are omniscient, but we are still unable to understand! We are masters of yoga, but nevertheless we are unable to discern the destination achieved by His yoga. Only His associate-devotees see that He has entered His own abode!”’

*Texts 11-13: Srila Sukadeva Gosvami’s analysis of Sri Krsna’s departure*

To emphasize the extraordinary and completely spiritual nature of Krsna’s disappearance, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami, the speaker of Srimad-Bhagavatam, now speaks about this mysterious pastime. In doing so he tries to mitigate his own distress and the distress of Pariksit Maharaja as they contemplate the Lord’s departure: “My dear King, you should understand that the Supreme Lord’s appearance and disappearance, which resemble those of embodied conditioned souls, are actually a show enacted by His illusory energy, just like the performance of an actor. After creating this universe He enters into it, plays within it for some time, and at last winds it up. Then the Lord remains situated in His own transcendental glory, having ceased from the functions of cosmic manifestation.” (SB. 11.31.11)

Sukadeva Gosvami now cites several clear examples to support that Krsna is beyond the influence of death: “Lord Krsna brought the son of His guru back from the planet of the lord of death in the boy’s selfsame body, and as the ultimate giver of protection He saved you also when you were burned by the brahmastra of Asvatthama. He conquered in battle even Lord Siva, who deals death to the agents of death, and He sent the hunter Jara directly to Vaikuntha in his human body. How could such a personality be unable to protect His own Self?” (SB.11.31.12)

Sukadeva concludes by revealing a preaching element born of the Lord’s disappearance: “Although Lord Krsna, being the possessor of infinite powers, is the only cause of the creation, maintenance, and destruction of innumerable living beings, He simply did not desire to keep His body in this world any longer. Thus He revealed the destination of those fixed in the self and demonstrated that this mortal world is of no intrinsic value.” (SB. 11.31.13)

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.13 makes Sukadeva’s final point clearer still: “Although Lord Krsna descended to this world to save the fallen souls, He did not want to encourage people in the future to loiter here unnecessarily. In other words, as soon as possible one should perfect one’s Krsna consciousness and go back home, back to Godhead. If Lord Krsna had remained longer on the earth, He would have unnecessarily increased the prestige of the material world.”

The BBT purport to text Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.11 is harmonious with Sukadeva Gosvami’s explanation of the Lord’s disappearance and the disappearance of His associates, the members of the Yadu dynasty: “According to Srila Jiva Gosvami, the so-called fight among the members of the Yadu dynasty was actually a display of the pastime potency of the Lord, since Lord Krsna’s personal associates are never subject to ordinary birth and death like conditioned souls. This being the case, certainly the Supreme Personality of Godhead Himself is transcendental to material birth and death, as clearly stated in this verse.”

The BBT purport goes on, adding a lengthy but intriguing analogy given by Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, centered on a word from text 11, natasya, “of an actor or magician”:

In front of a great king, a magician approaches a stack of valuable garments, jewels, coins, and so forth, all placed there by the king. Taking a jeweled necklace, the magician tells the king, “Now I am taking this necklace, and you can’t have it,” and he makes the necklace disappear. “Now I’m taking this gold coin, and you can’t have it,” he says, and makes the gold coin disappear. Next, challenging the king in the same way, the magician makes seven thousand horses disappear. Then the magician creates the illusion that the king’s children, grandchildren, brothers, and other family members have attacked each other and that nearly all are dead from the violent quarrel. The king hears the magician speaking and at the same time observes these things taking place before him as lie sits in the great assembly hall.

Then the magician says, “O King, I no longer wish to live. Just as I have studied magic, so also, by the mercy of the lotus feet of my guru, I have learned the mystic meditation of yoga. One is supposed to give up one’s body while meditating in a holy place, and since you have performed so many pious activities, you are a holy place yourself. Therefore I shall now give up my body.”

Thus speaking, the magician sits down in the proper yoga posture, fixes himself in pranayama, pratyahara, dharana, dhyana, and samadhi and becomes silent. A moment later, a fire generated from his trance blazes forth out of his body and burns it to ashes. Then all the wives of the magician, distraught with lamentation, enter into that fire.

Three or four days later, after the magician has returned to his own province, he sends one of his daughters to the king. The daughter tells him, “O King, I have just come to your palace, bringing along with me, invisibly, all your sons, grandsons, and brothers in good health — along with all the jewels and other items given by you. Please, therefore, give me whatever you consider fitting remuneration for the wisdom of the magic that has been exhibited before you.” In this way, even by ordinary magic one can simulate birth and death.
