In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.30.5, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also offers an extensive explanation as to why Krsna left behind a material body. His conclusion is brilliant, exhilarating, and astonishing:

Internally, the Lord thought as follows: Among all the persons who came to meet me from various places during the trip to Kuruksetra,

Kali came unnoticed by others and spoke to Me. “O master! When will I take charge of the earth?” I said, “You can take charge only when My pastimes are over.” After I disappear, with the right given by Me, Kali will pervade the earth. However, during My present appearance, dharma has increased to four legs and is even stronger now than in Satya-yuga. If dharma is so strong, how can Kali rule? Kali can only rule when one leg of dharma remains. One should not use the logic that “When the effect disappears the cause disappears” to conclude that when I disappear, the four legs of dharma will also disappear. Why? The devatas will still be alert, for they are famous and purifiers of the whole world. Moreover, I have already destroyed those who are unfavorable to dharma within the world’s population. Now, if I ascend to Vaikuntha in the sight of all persons, as Rama did with all the inhabitants of Ayodhya, the favorable devotees will double in number. Those who are already intensely favorable will increase their prema a hundredfold out of great longing in prema, and those who are neutral will become devotees on seeing this extraordinary event. Dharma will thus increase. How will even a little influence of Kali be possible? By what method will I restrict dharma and increase adharma so that Kali can enter and rule?’

The Lord then thought: Here is the method! I will remain as I do now in Dvaraka with my associates, the Yadus, but will become invisible to the eyes of all who are materialistic. The devatas, who are My potencies, such as Cupid and Kartikeya, have already entered into My eternal associates, such as Pradyumna. Making some fake forms for the eyes of ordinary people, which will appear to be Pradyumna and others, I will have them go to Prabhasa with the other inhabitants of Dvaraka. There I will have them drink wine after meditating and giving charity. I will then send them to Svarga according to their individual qualifications as devotees. Then I, in another form, will next depart for Vaikuntha with the other inhabitants of Dvaraka, as Rama did, \[while My root form of Krsna and His associates will remain invisibly in Dvaraka\]. But I will let the common people think that the Yadus left Dvaraka, went to Prabhasa, and under the control of the brahmanas’ curse, drank wine and killed each other. They will also think I, Krsna, along with Balarama, gave up Our human bodies and ascended to Our spiritual abodes. Thus they will think that My body was temporary and made of matter, which is a great offense. Others will claim that just as the Kurus all died in the Battle of Kuruksetra, Krsna died with His family at Prabhasa. By people’s hearing, speaking, and praising such preaching of wrong ideas by idiots who think they are learned, immediately only one leg of dharma will remain.

Just as eyes afflicted with jaundice see a shining white conch to be yellow, people whose minds and eyes are afflicted by maya will see My departure pastimes, which are actually eternal and full of knowledge and bliss, as afflicted by material misfortune. They will see and conclude that I gave up My body along with all My associates, like Pradyumna, and that the bodies of My queens, such as Rukmini, were burned in the funeral fire. Not only the materialists will see this, but even persons such as Arjuna will see this by My divine will. Sages like Vaisampayana and Parasara will describe ibis in (heir works, and Siva, my devotee, taking birth in Kali-yuga, will preach this in a commentary of the Vedanta-sutras in order to spread Kali’s influence. Persons with no intelligence, repeatedly studying these sutras, will explain their meaning according to that adhir mayakhye ’neka-saktiman sa eva bhagavad-dehah: “The body of the Lord, possessing unlimited powers, is a subtle covering of may a on Brahman.”

Thinking in this way, with the idea of producing great disturbance, the Lord, expressing fear and agitation, spoke this verse.

*Text 14: Phala-sruti - the fruit of hearing of the Lord’s departure for His abode*

“Anyone who regularly rises early in the morning and carefully chants with devotion the glories of Lord Sri Krsna’s transcendental disappearance and His return to His own abode will certainly achieve that same supreme \[param, anuttamam\] destination. (SB. 11.31.14)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “The words param (‘supreme’) and anuttamam (‘unsurpassable’) indicate that the Lord s disappearance pastime is composed solely of eternity, knowledge, and bliss. It also suggests that intelligent persons regard as insignificant the opinion of common people who consider Krsna s disappearance material.

*Texts 15-26: The departure of the remaining Yadavas and the destruction of Dvaraka*

“As soon as Daruka reached Dvaraka, he threw himself at the feet of Vasudeva and Ugrasena and drenched their feet with his tears, lamenting the loss of Lord Krsna. Daruka delivered the account of the total destruction of the Vrsnis, and upon hearing this, O Pariksit, the people became deeply distraught in their hearts and stunned with sorrow. Feeling the overwhelming pain of separation from Krsna, they struck their own faces while hurrying to the place where their relatives lay dead. When Devaki, Rohini, and Vasudeva could not find their sons, Krsna and Rama, they lost consciousness out of anguish.” (SB. 11.31.15-18)

The BBT purport adds a short comment to text 18 that gives this sad lild a fuller perspective: “According to Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, the original Devaki, Rohini, and other ladies of Dvaraka actually remained in Dvaraka, invisible to the eyes of the material world, whereas the demigods who represented partial aspects of Devaki, Rohini, and so on went to Prabhasa to see their dead relatives.”

Daruka was able to see these “invisible forms” - that is, these persons in their spiritual forms, who live eternally in the spiritual, eternal Dvaraka - because Daruka is also an eternal associate of that realm.

“Tormented by separation from the Lord, His parents gave up their lives at that very spot. My dear Pariksit, the wives of the Yadavas then climbed onto the funeral pyres, embracing their dead husbands.” (SB. 11.31.19)

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that the above description should be understood and explained as “apparent” and not as actual fact.

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.11 cited Srila Jiva Gosvami saying that the entire “fight among the members of the Yadu dynasty was actually a display of the pastime potency of the Lord.” Krsna told Daruka (in SB.11.30.49), man-maya-racitam etam vijnayopasamarh vraja: “Understanding these pastimes to be a display of My illusory potency, you should remain peaceful.” Therefore Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes in his commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.19 that the above description should be understood and explained as “superficial” and not as actual fact. They are likened to a magical performance, according to Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.31.11. Clearly the descriptions surrounding Krsna’s disappearance are of what had apparently occurred and are essentially a mystically performed drama directed by the master of all mystic powers.

“The wives of Lord Balarama also entered the fire and embraced His body, and Vasudeva’s wives entered his fire and embraced his body. The daughters-in-law of Lord Hari entered the funeral fires of their respective husbands, headed by Pradyumna. And Rukmini and the other wives of Lord Krsna - whose hearts were completely absorbed in Him - entered His fire.” (SB. 11.31.20)

On text 29 Sripada Madhvacarya writes that although Rukmini disappeared in the fire and Satyabhama in the forest, neither actually gave up their bodies, as both of their bodies were purely spiritual.

“Arjuna felt great distress over separation from Lord Krsna, his dearmost friend. But he consoled himself by remembering the transcendental words the Lord had sung to him.” (SB. 11.31.21)

Srila Sridhara Svami offers an example of the words Krsna had sung io Arjuna which Arjuna now remembered: “I am never manifest to the foolish and unintelligent. For them I am covered by My eternal creative potency (yoga-maya) and so the deluded world knows Me not, who am unborn and infallible.” (Bhagavad-gita 7.25) Srila Jiva Gosvami adds Bhagavad-gita 18.65 to the list: “Thus you will come to Me without fail. I promise you this because you are My very dear friend.

The description of Krsna’s mausalya-lila continues: “Arjuna then saw to it that the funeral rites were properly carried out for the dead, who had no remaining male family members. He executed the required ceremonies for each of the Yadus, one after another. As soon as Dvaraka was abandoned by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, the ocean flooded it on all sides, O King, sparing only His palace.” (SB. 11.31.22-23)

In an attempt to lift Maharaja Pariksit’s spirits, Sukadeva Gosvami reminds the king of Dvaraka s true nature: “Lord Madhusudana, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, is eternally present in Dvaraka. It is the most auspicious of all auspicious places, and merely remembering it destroys all contamination.” (SB. 11.31.24)

Supporting the Bhagavatam’s statement in text 24, Srila Jiva Gosvami quotes a similar text from the Visnu Parana (5.38.9): “The ocean then swallowed up the abandoned Dvaraka, but it did not drown the house of the Lord of the Yadus, Krsna. O brahmana, the ocean did not touch His palace because there the Supreme Lord Kesava is still present today. Therefore this place connected with the pastimes of Lord Visnu is most pious — capable of destroying all sinful reactions. Anyone who sees this place becomes freed from sins.” Srila Jiva Gosvami also notes that “a place that removes sins” implies that that place is not temporary but eternal, and therefore worth remembering.

“Arjuna took the survivors of the Yadu dynasty — the women, children, and old men - to Indraprastha, where he installed Vajra as ruler of the Yadus.Hearing from Arjuna of the death of their friend, my dear King, your grandfathers established you as the maintainer of the dynasty and left to prepare for their departure from this world.” (SB. 11.31.25-26)

*Texts 27-28: Phala-sruti - faithful hearing awards liberation from sins; chanting awards devotional service*

“A person who with faith engages in chanting the glories of these various pastimes and incarnations of Visnu, the Lord of lords, will gain liberation from all sins. The all-auspicious exploits of the all- attractive incarnations of Lord Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, and also the pastimes He performed as a child, are described in this Srimad-Bhagavatam and in other scriptures. Anyone who clearly chants these descriptions of His pastimes will attain transcendental loving service unto Lord Krsna, who is the goal of all perfect sages.” (SB. 11.31.27-28)

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on these final texts of the Eleventh Canto: “Hearing all of the pastimes of Sri Krsna with transcendental devotion causes one to attain His destination— He is even the destination of the paramahamsas who become attracted to His qualities, what to speak of the destination of His devotees.” In the Priti Sandarbha (anuccheda 158), Srila Jiva cites this text to indicate the specific sweetness of Krsna’s Vrndavana pastimes: “In the Eleventh Canto, at the end of the narration about Krsna, the pastimes of Krsna in general are said to act as stimulants for bhakti. But His childhood pastimes are singled out as most excellent. The excellence of Krsna’s manifested pastimes in Vrndavana are of many types. Some show excellence of aisvarya, such as Krsna showing Brahma that He is the lord of millions of universes and the form of eternity, knowledge, and infinite bliss. Some pastimes show compassion, such as when Krsna awards Putana the position of a nurse. And some show sweetness.” Srila Jiva Gosvami then cites fourteen texts from the Tenth Canto that indicate Krsna’s sweetness.He concludes anuccheda 158, saying, “What is the use of adding still more examples? Knowers of rasa will already understand everything”

Supremely wise Sri Uddhava, whom Krsna favored with instructions in almost every chapter of the Eleventh Canto and who received from Krsna the order to go to Badarikasrama, was blessed to see the Lord’s beautiful form immediately before He completed His mausala-lila. Earlier in the Bhagavatam, Uddhava shared his thoughts on the Lord’s disappearance: “Lord Sri Krsna, who manifested His eternal form before the vision of all on the earth, performed His disappearance by removing His form from the sight of those who were unable to see Him \[as He is\] due to not executing required penance. The Lord appeared in the mortal world by His internal potency, yoga-maya. He came in His eternal form, which is just suitable for His pastimes. These pastimes were wonderful for everyone, even for those proud of their own opulence, including the Lord Himself in I lis form as the Lord of Vaikuntha. Thus \[Sri Krsna’s\] transcendental body is the ornament of all ornaments.” (SB. 3.2.11-12)

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.2.12 glorifies the Lord’s matchless pastimes: “When the Lord’s pastimes are visible to the human eye, they are called prakate, and when they are not visible they are called aprakata. In fact, the Lord’s pastimes never stop, just as the sun never leaves the sky. The sun is always in its right orbit in the sky, but it is sometimes visible and sometimes invisible to our limited vision. Similarly, the pastimes of the Lord are always current in one universe or another, and when Lord Krsna disappeared from the transcendental abode of Dvaraka, it was simply a disappearance from the eyes of the people there.... All His pastimes were manifested not by the material energy but by His spiritual energy. The excellence of His rasa-lila at Vrndavana and His householder life with sixteen thousand wives is wonderful even for Narayana in Vaikuntha and is certainly so for other living entities within this mortal world. His pastimes are wonderful even for other incarnations of the Lord, such as Sri Rama, Nrsimha and Varaha. His opulence was so superexcellent that His pastimes were adored even by the Lord of Vaikuntha, who is not different from Lord Krsna Himself.”

## Canto twelve

## Dialogue 8. Maharaja Pariksit departs from this world

*Canto twelve: chapters 1-6*

**Chapter 1: The Degraded Dynasties of Kali-yuga**

*Texts 1-14: The succession of kings up to the dynasties of Nanda and the Mauryas*

Beginning the Twelfth Canto, Sukadeva Gosvami now changes topics. He begins by completing a list of rulers he began back in the Ninth Canto - his earlier description was diverted by his desire to narrate the amazing birth, activities, and departure from the earth of Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead. That krsna-katha Sukadeva initiated at the end of Canto Nine flowed continuously through cantos Ten and Eleven, until here again he picks up the thread of listing the ruling lineages.

The last king of the Puru dynasty Sukadeva named in the Ninth Canto was Puranjaya,the son of Uparicara Vasu, who appeared after Krsna’s appearance in the world. Krsna departs and Kali-yuga begins its relentless grind. King Puranjaya is assassinated by his prime minister, Sunaka, who installed his own son Pradyota on the throne. Thus a true Kali-yuga dynasty of rulers is inaugurated.

Pradyota’s lineage survives 138 years, and that of Sisunaga, the dynasty replacing Pradyota’s, 360 years. Powerful King Nanda, the son of a ksatriya man and a sudra woman, begins the next dynasty and ends the dominance of pure ksatriya warrior kings.

Kali-yuga now begins to gain momentum. No one is strong enough to challenge Nanda, and the king wreaks havoc among the remaining ksatriya dynasties.From Nanda onward, virtually all the kings in Kali-yuga are irreligious sudras.

Nanda’s eight sons control the earth for one hundred years. Then, Sukadeva Gosvami describes, “a certain brahmana \[Canakya\] will betray the trust of King Nanda and his eight sons and will destroy their dynasty. In their absence the Mauryas will rule the world as the age of Kali continues. This brahmana will enthrone Candragupta, whose son will be named Varisara. The son of Varisara will be Asokavardhana.” (SB. 12.1.11-12) Ten Maurya kings rule the earth for a total of 137 years.

Each of the kings Sukadeva lists mounts the throne, reigns, and is dethroned or dies, leaving only his name on a list to be washed away by the relentless waves of time. Lord Brahma hints at how temporary royal dynasties (and by extrapolation, everyone else) are after hearing King Kakudmi’s request to find his daughter Revati a suitable husband: “O King, all those whom you may have decided within the core of your heart to accept as your son-in-law have passed away in the course of time. Twenty-seven catur-yugas have already passed. Those upon whom you may have decided are now gone, and so are their sons, grandsons, and other descendants. You cannot even hear about their names. ” (SB. 9.3.32)

In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.1.1-2, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that the goal of listing these kings and their exploits is simply to evoke detachment in King Pariksit.Srila Sridhara Svami states in his own comments on texts 1 and 2 of this first chapter that the Canto’s opening chapters have a common theme: “In order that intelligent persons not hesitate in the necessity of taking shelter of the supreme shelter, the effects of time are spoken of in the first four chapters.”

*Texts 15-41: Continued succession of non-ksatriya kings*

The ten Sunga kings form the next dynasty and rule the earth for more than a hundred years. “Vasudeva, an intelligent minister coming from the Kanva family, will kill the last of the Sunga kings, a lusty debauchee named Devabhuti, and assume rulership himself. (SB. 12.1.18) While subjugating the earth, the kings of the Kanva dynasty show few good qualities. They rule for 345 years. “The last of the Kanvas, Susarma, will be murdered by his own servant, Bali, a low-class sudra of the Andhra race. This most degraded Maharaja Bali will have control over the earth for some time.” (SB. 12.1.20)

The thirty kings after Bali will be sovereigns over the earth for a total of 456 years. Ten Gardabhis will rule after them, and then sixteen excessively greedy rulers of the Kankas. Due to their impious example and greed, all these non-ksatriya kings will cause the population of Kali-yuga to become further degraded. “Eight Yavanas will then take power, followed by fourteen Turuskas, ten Gurundas, and eleven kings of the Maula dynasty. These Abhiras, Gardabhis, and Kankas will enjoy the earth for 1,099 years, and the Maulas will rule for 300 years. When all of them have died off there will appear in the city of Kilakila a dynasty of kings consisting of Bhutananda, Vangiri, Sisunandi, Sisunandi’s brother Yasonandi, and Praviraka. These kings of Kilakila will hold sway for a total of 106 years.” (SB. 12.1.28—31) The Kilakilas will be followed by their sons, the Bahlikas, who will be succeeded by seven Andhras, then seven Kausalas. Kings of the Vidura and Nisadha provinces will separately rule in different parts of the world.

The consciousness of these kings and dynasties who relentlessly vied for power is far different from those who had attained profound realizations after Krsna released them from Jarasandha’s prison. Those kings prayed to Krsna: “Previously, blinded by the intoxication of riches, we wanted to conquer this earth, and thus we fought one another to achieve victory, mercilessly harassing our own subjects. We arrogantly disregarded You, O Lord, who stood before us as death. But now, O Krsna, that powerful form of Yours called time, moving mysteriously and irresistibly, has deprived us of our opulences. Now that You have mercifully destroyed our pride, we beg simply to remember Your lotus feet.” (SB. 10.73.12-13)

With the glorious goal of deepening Maharaja Pariksit’s mood of taking sole shelter at the lotus feet of Krsna, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami’s list continues his roll call of Kali-yuga leaders, all rascals who helped spread the poison of the age through their rule.

The Magadha king named Visvasphurji will turn civilized citizens into low-class, uncivilized men, and he will use his power to further disrupt the ksatriya order.At that time the brahmanas of provinces like S.mrastra, Avanti, Abhira, Sura, Arbuda, and Malava will forget all their regulative principles and will act as if they are members of the lowest class. Sudras, fallen brahmanas, and meat-eaters will rule, and having given up the path of Vedic civilization, they will lose all spiritual strength. Many uncivilized, uncharitable kings, who possess fierce tempers and who are great devotees of irreligion and falsity will then rule at the same time. “These barbarians in the guise o kings will devour the citizenry, murdering innocent women, children, cows, and brahmanas and coveting the wives and property of other men. They will be erratic in their moods, have little strength of character, and be very short-lived. Indeed, not purified by any Vedic rituals and lacking in the practice of regulative principles, they will be completely covered by the modes of passion and ignorance. The citizens governed by these low-class kings will imitate the character, behavior, and speech of their rulers. Harassed by their leaders and by each other, they will all suffer ruination.” (SB. 12.1.39-41)

In his comments on texts 38-40, Srila Sridhara Svami reveals details about these rulers’ improprieties: “These kings... will be fixed in irreligion and untruth. They will be stingy with charity, and their moods will be predominated by elation and lamentation... They wi torment the citizens by taking away their wealth... The citizens living under their rule will become endowed with the same personal character, behavior, and speech as their kings.”

**Chapter 2: The Symptoms of Kali-yuga**

*Texts 1-16: Horrors of Kali-yuga*

The four ages cycle from one to the next (SB. 12.2.39) and now, with the horrific approach of Kali-yuga inevitable, Sukadeva Gosvami’s words remind Maharaja Pariksit that his term as king has been completed and his time to return to the spiritual world has arrived. Maharaja Pariksit, already an exalted devotee, continues to act as an exemplar even as his departure from this world approaches. As the king’s teacher, Sukadeva evokes further detachment by recounting the horrendous characteristics of the rapidly developing age of Kali: “Then, O King, religion, truthfulness, cleanliness, tolerance, mercy, duration of life, physical strength, and memory will all diminish day by day because of the powerful influence of the age of Kali. (SB. 12.2.1)

In a lecture he gave on March 18, 1968 in San Francisco, Srila Prabhupada spoke about the eight qualities listed above and how they diminish day by day in Kali-yuga:

First thing is religiosity. As the Age of Kali will make progress, people will become more and more irreligious. And they will become more and more liars. They’ll forget to speak what is true. Cleanliness will also diminish... If one is to advance, he has to clean himself. According to Vedic civilization, one has to take bath thrice daily. Actually, in India they take… Especially the brahmanas. So cleanliness is next to godliness... But as the days of this Kali-yuga will make progress, this system of hygienic cleanliness, cleanliness both inside and outside - outside by taking bath, inside by becoming Krsna conscious - two kinds of cleanliness. Simply if we take bath with soap outside and inside keep all rubbish things, that is not cleanliness... Unless we are clean, unless we are pure, how can we advance to approach the Supreme? The Supreme is described as the purest... So this cleanliness inside and outside, that will also decrease.

People are advised, especially those who are following penance, austerity, yogic principle, or devotional life, they should learn to excuse. In our dealings, there are so many faulty dealings between ourselves. So if we take everything very seriously, then it is very difficult to live. So ksama, forgiveness, will reduce. Nobody will forgive. Retaliation, vengeance, that will increase.

Srila Prabhupada next comments on ayuh, duration of life. “Perhaps your grandfather lived for one hundred years. Your father lived for eighty years. And nowadays, sixty or seventy years. Gradually, it will so reduce that if a man lives for twenty to thirty years he will be considered a very grand old man. If he lives for twenty to thirty years he’ll be considered, ‘Oh, you have got very good life.’ That will come, gradually. This is the progressive age for material civilization. We are proud of making advancement of our civilization, but these nice things are being reduced. That means that our advancement is in the reducing of nice things. This is our advancement.”

In the same lecture, Srila Prabhupada specifically comments on the reduction of the quality of mercy: “Daya means mercy. What is daya? Who is less strong, like animals, birds, beasts, you should be very merciful. Just like children you should be very merciful to children. According to Vedic injunctions, children, women, brahmanas, old men, and cows.... These five, according to Manu-samhita, or Hindu law, can commit no offense. They cannot be criminally prosecuted. Excused. If a brahmana has committed some fault or a woman has committed some fault or a child has committed some fault or a cow has transgressed the law, oh, there is no punishment for them. Daya. They should be shown always mercy. They require protection, especially… That is required in human civilization. Cow protection is very important. Woman’s protection is very important. Brahmana s protection is very important. Children s protection is very important.... So daya means you should show your mercifulness to those who are weak. So this will reduce, daya.”

In a room conversation at New Vrindavan, June 26, 1976, Srila Prabhupada elaborates further on the absence of mercy in Kali-yuga: “There is no mercy. There is no mercy to the animals. Now there is no mercy even to one’s child. One s own child, they \[are\] killing. Just see how degraded! YPhat to speak of having no daya, no mercy for the animals — all right, you are not so advanced — but the mother s mercy to her own child will be diminished. This is the foretelling \[of Sukadeva Gosvami five thousand years ago\]. This is called tri-kala-jha. Who expected that mother will kill the child? But Vyasadeva, five thousand years ago, said, ‘Yes, mercy will be reduced.

Sukadeva Gosvami continues: “In Kali-yuga, wealth alone will be considered the sign of a man’s good birth, proper behavior, and fine qualities. And law and justice will be applied only on the basis of one’s power.” (SB. 12.2.2)

Srila Prabhupada noted this Kali-yuga tendency in a lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.2.1, given on March 18, 1968 in San Francisco. “Suppose a man is a great philosopher, a great learned scholar. That is a very good qualification. So these things will not be considered. If a man is very learned scholar or coming of a very respectable family and has got all good qualities, that will be neglected. Another man, if he has all the bad qualities but he has got money, he’s respected. He’ll be respected. This is the symptom of this age.”

Or, as Srila Prabhupada said in a lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.15.46 in Los Angeles on December 24, 1973: ‘If you are poor man, then you are dishonest. People will understand that Tbis man is actually not honest because he does not know how to earn money by hook or crook.’”

Srila Prabhupada continues, cynically equating one’s ability to get justice in Kali-yuga with the amount of money in one’s possession: “If you have no money, then you will never get justice in the court. This is Kali-yuga. Nowadays the high-court judges, they may take bribes to give a favorable judgment. You can purchase judgment. So if you have no money, then don’t go to court. It is pushing good money after bad money.”

Sukadeva Gosvami continues: “Men and women will live together merely because of superficial attraction, and success in business will depend on deceit. Womanliness and manliness will be judged according to one’s expertise in sex, and a man will be known as a brahmana just by his wearing a thread.” (SB. 12.2.3)

Srila Prabhupada commented on some of these Kali-yuga characteristics in that same San Francisco lecture: “Maya means false dealing. Vyavahare. Even in ordinary dealing there will be cheating and faultiness - even in ordinary. Even you go to purchase something from a store, oh, there is false dealing.”

About men and women living together without being married: “Boys and girls are intermingling freely, and if she likes, that’s all right. This is Kali-yuga. No future calculation, whether in future marriage is sanctified life, the man and the woman live peacefully, make spiritual culture, each one will help the other so that they will live very happily and become advanced in spiritual life...That is the system. But nowadays, in Kali-yuga, it will be simply liking. Liking means next moment disliking. That is a fact. You see. Liking has no value. As soon as you base on liking, then you expect next moment disliking. That’s all.” And, referring to the lack of brahminical culture: “One man can purchase a two-cent worthless thread and put it on the... ‘Oh, I come from a brahmana family.’ Without any education, without any acceptance of spiritual master, and without anything, simply by showing the thread, that ‘I have got this thread,’ he becomes a brahmana or vipra, or twice-born or... Nonsense. But this will be done in Kali-yuga.”

Sukadeva Gosvami continues his description: “A person’s spiritual position will be ascertained merely according to external symbols, and on that same basis people will change from one spiritual order to the next. A person’s propriety will be seriously questioned if he does not earn a good living. And one who is very clever at juggling words will be considered a learned scholar.A person will be judged unholy if be does not have money, and hypocrisy will be accepted as virtue. Marriage will be arranged simply by verbal agreement, and a person will think he is fit to appear in public if he has merely taken a bath.” (SB. 12.2.4-5)

In a Srimad-Bhagavatam (1.15.46) lecture Srila Prabhupada gave in Los Angeles on December 24, 1973, he mocked being accepted as learned simply if one is expert in juggling words: “If a man talks expertly, it doesn’t matter what he talks. Nobody requires to understand him. Then he is pandita. \[Srila Prabhupada speaks some gibberish.\] Haperkulasvena bagavad dagvendikali gundulas, by the lacticism of wife... If you go on speaking, nobody will understand, \[laughter\] Nobody will understand, and people, ‘Oh, see how learned he is.’ \[laughter\] Actually, it is happening. There are so many rascals. They are writing book, and ‘Oh, such and such, oh...’ ‘What you have understood?’ ‘Oh, it is inexplicable. Inexplicable.’That is going on.”

Regarding money being the sole measure of one’s standing in Kali-yuga society, Srila Prabhupada remarked (in a Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.2.1 lecture in San Francisco on March 18, 1968): “If you have got money, some way or other, whatever you may he, you are very respected... Formerly a man was respectable by his birth in a respectable family an by his behavior. A brahmana was respected because his behavior was so nice. He was truthful, he was clean, he was man of knowledge, and he was faithful in scriptures. He had so many qualifications. Therefore he was respected.”

Srila Sukadeva Gosvami continues his description of Kali-yuga, the ocean of superficiality and faults: “A sacred place will be taken to consist of no more than a reservoir of water located at a distance, and beauty will be thought to depend on one’s hairstyle. Filling the belly will become the goal of life, and one who is audacious will be accepted as truthful. He who can maintain a family will be regarded as an expert man, and the principles of religion will be observed only for the sake of reputation.” (SB. 12.2.6)

About pilgrimage to distant sacred places, Srila Prabhupada remarked: “A pilgrimage place - it must be far away. Just like in Calcutta there is the Ganges. So nobody cares for the Calcutta Ganges. But they go to Hardwar. The same Ganges. The Ganges is coming from Hardwar down to the Bay of Bengal, but people like to go to Hardwar, taking so much hardship, to take bath there, because that becomes tirtha. In every religion they have got tirtha. The Muslims, they have got Mecca and Medina. The Christians, they have got Jerusalem. Similarly, the Hindus must travel very far. It will then be tirtha. But actually tirtha means tirthi-kurvanti tirthani. Where there is a saintly person, that is a tirtha. Not to go ten thousand miles and simply take a dip in the water and come back.” (Lecture on Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.15.46, Los Angeles, December 24, 1973)

About filling the belly being people’s central interest, Srila Prabhupada noted in the same lecture: “Now, in Kali-yuga, the interest will be if you can eat some day very sumptuously, then your all interest is fulfilled. That’s all. Means people will be so hungry, so nothing to eat; therefore if they can eat some day very sumptuously, that will he fulfillment of all interests.”

And still the Age of Kali worsens: “As the earth thus becomes crowded with a corrupt population, whoever among any of the social classes shows himself to be the strongest will gain political power. Losing their wives and properties to such avaricious and merciless rulers, who will behave no better than ordinary thieves, the citizens will flee to the mountains and forests.” (SB. 12.2.7-8)

In the same Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.15.46 lecture, Srila Prabhupada criticized the untrained, unqualified, and corrupt politicians of Kali-yuga, who exploit the citizens rather than protect them: “So it doesn’t matter whether he is a brahmana or a ksatriya or vaisya or sudra or cartdala. One who is powerful in getting votes, he will occupy the presidential post or the royal post. Just see. Formerly the system was that not the brahmana, vaisya, or sudra can occupy the royal throne. Only the ksatriyas. Now, in the Kali-yuga, there is no such thing - who is a ksatriya, who is a brahmana, who is a... Anyone, hook and crook you get your votes, democracy, and occupy ... And whatever you may be... You may be rascal number one, but you will be posted on the supreme exalted presidential post. Now, these classes of men, who gain the government post by votes, mostly their qualification is that they are greedy government men. Their business is plundering you. We actually see that every year they are exacting heavy tax, and whatever money is received, they divide among themselves. And the citizens’ condition remains tire same. In every government we can see that. In this way, gradually all people will be so harassed that they will like to give up their family. They will go to live in the forest.”

Sukadeva Gosvami: “Harassed by famine and excessive taxes, people will resort to eating leaves, roots, flesh, wild honey, fruits, flowers and seeds. Struck by drought, they will become completely ruined. The citizens will suffer greatly from cold, wind, heat, rain, and snow. They will be further tormented by quarrels, hunger, thirst, disease, and severe anxiety. The maximum duration of life for human beings in Kali-yuga will become fifty years.” (SB. 12.2.9-11)

The point of increased longevity in modern times came up ma room conversation with Srila Prabhupada in New Vrindavan, June 25, 1976:

Devotee 1: They say that men are living longer now. The scientists, they say that there’s less disease. They say that a hundred years ago people had more disease than —

Srila Prabhupada: That these rascals say, we do not say. We have seen in our childhood that my grandmother, she died at the age of ninety-six years. There was no disease. The scientists say that there was disease, and now there is no disease?

Devotee 2: They say there is less disease now.

Srila Prabhupada: Less disease? Everyone is suffering from cancer.

*Texts 12-16: The end of Kali-yuga*

“By the time the age of Kali ends, the bodies of all creatures will be greatly reduced in size, and the religious principles of followers of varnasrama will be ruined. The path of the Vedas wil be completely forgotten in human society, and so-called religion will be mostly atheistic. The kings will mostly be thieves, the occupations of men will be stealing, lying, and needless violence, and all the social classes will be reduced to the lowest level of sudras. Cows will be like goats, spiritual hermitages will be no different from mundane houses, and familyties will extend no further than the immediate bonds of marriage. Most plants and herbs will be tiny, and all trees will appear like dwarf sami trees. Clouds will be full of lightning, homes will be devoid of piety, and all human beings will have become like asses. At that time, the Supreme Personality of Godhead will appear on the earth. Acting with the power of pure spiritual goodness, He will rescue eternal religion.” (SB. 12.2.12-16)

One can seek relief from the Age of Kali before the Lord appears on earth with His deadly sword as the Kalki amtdra. Again in the Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.15.46 lecture, quoted earlier, Srila Prabhupada spoke about escaping the iron shackles of Kali-yuga: So in this way there are so many symptoms. This is Kali-yuga. But there is remedy. Kaler dosa-nidhe rajann. The faults of this age are just like ocean. You cannot cross the Pacific Ocean. If you are put into the Pacific Ocean, you do not know how your life will be saved. It is very difficult. Even if you are very expert swimmer, it is not possible to cross the Pacific Ocean. Similarly, Kali-yuga, as it is stated in the Srimad-Bhagavatam, is infected with so many anomalies that there is no way out. But there is one medicine only: kirtanad eva krsnasya mukta-sangah param vrajet. That is also described, that ‘if you chant Hare Krsna mantra,’ kirtanad eva krsnasya, ‘especially the name of Krsna,’ krsnasya, mukta-sangah, ‘you will be relieved from the infection of Kali-yuga.’”

*Texts 17-24: The Kalki avatara’s actions inaugurate Satya-yuga*

“Lord Kalki will appear in the home of the most eminent brahmana of Sambhala village, the great soul Visnuyasa.” (SB. 12.2.18) As always, the Lord’s mission will be to protect both His devotees and the principles of religion. With sword in hand and an unequaled effulgence, Lord Kalki will mount His swift horse Devadatta and kill millions of thieves who dared dress as kings. The citizens will thus be freed from tyranny and become purified by the breeze carrying the Lord’s fragrance.

In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.2.21, Srila Sridhara Svami writes about Kalki avatara inaugurating the Age of Satya: “The minds of those residents of the cities and villages will become pure. The reason for this is that their minds will be touched by that wind that has been made most piously fragrant by the decorative cosmetics of the body of Lord Vasudeva, by His sandalwood pulp and so on.”

Sukadeva Gosvami adds that once the people are freed, the Lord’s transcendental form will appear in their hearts and they will abundantly repopulate the earth with progeny that are in the mode of goodness. Thus by Kalki’s mercy, Satya-yuga will begin again. Astronomically, this occurs when the moon, sun, and Brhaspati (Jupiter) are together in Karkata (Cancer), and all three simultaneously enter the lunar mansion Pusya.

*Texts 5-38: Kali-yuga increases in strength before Satya-yuga is reestablished*

Sukadeva Gosvami then announces that he has finished recounting the kings in the Sun and Moon dynasties, past, present, and future, which he had begun in the Ninth Canto. From Maharaja Pariksit s birth up to the coronation of King Nanda is a span of 1,150 years. In texts 27-28 and 31, Sukadeva Gosvami tells Maharaja Pariksit of the astronomical placement of the constellations as Kali-yuga advents.

Kali could gather momentum and flourish, Sukadeva explains, after Krsna departs: “The Supreme Lord, Visnu, is brilliant like the sun and is known as Krsna. When He returned to the spiritual sky, Kali entered this world, and people then began to take pleasure in sinful activities. As long as Lord Sri Krsna, the husband of the goddess of fortune, touched the earth with His lotus feet, Kali was powerless to subdue the planet.” (SB. 12.2.29-30)Kali will only assume full strength when King Nanda and his dynasty gain power. Those who scientifically understand the past declare that on the very day that Lord Sri Krsna departed for the spiritual world, the influence of the Age of Kali began.” (SB. 12.2.33)

In addition to the ksatriya dynasties mentioned, a tracing of the genealogical records of all the members of society - including the brahmanas, vaisyas, and sudras — could also be listed, as mentioned in Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.2.35. And as has been shown with the ksatriya kings, one would assume these historical records would reveal the other social orders also sliding into degradation due to Kali’s influence.

*Texts 34-38: The reestablishment of the golden age of Satya-yuga at the end of Kali-yuga*

Sukadeva Gosvami continues, “After the one thousand celestial years of Kali-yuga, Satya-yuga will manifest again. At that time the minds of all men will become self-effulgent. Thus I have described the royal dynasty of Manu, as it is known on this earth. One can similarly study the history of the vaisyas, sudras, and brahmanas living in the various ages.” (SB. 12.2.34-35)

During Kali-yuga, human society will no longer follow varnasrama-dharma. As a result, people will lose their absolute reference point for ethical and moral standards. Basic, underlying spiritual truths, such as that the soul is eternal and transmigrates through different bodies based on one’s actions in this and other lives, will he replaced by atheistic theories. People will lose their sense of lifes purpose and meaning as scientists replace pure-hearted spiritualists as societys unquestioned authorities. Distinctions between right and wrong, good and evil, favorable and unfavorable will be blurred. Sinful lifestyles based on temporary pleasure will be propagated, and as a result, violence, incurable disease, fear, and anxiety will increase. Faith and trust will become increasingly rare, and when they do, they will be seen as naive. The carefully preserved, millenniums-old traditions and wisdom will now be ridiculed, rejected as irrelevant, mythological, or unprogressive — or will be fashioned into expensive weekend seminars. People will begin to see moral restrictions as barriers to freedom and then become easy prey to their lower tendencies.

Thus ferocious Kali-yuga will march forth on all fronts, with even those who temporarily rise to power during this dark age joining all the others and drowning in the relentless, ruthless ebb and flow of time.

Yet, Sukadeva Gosvami points out, this last point is also true of kings in all ages. “These personalities, who were great souls, are now known only by their names. They exist only in accounts from the past, and only their fame remains on the earth.” (SB. 12.2.36)

Although in Kali-yuga the names of past, pious, powerful heroes and their deeds and ideals tend now to be forgotten in favor of remembering programming codes, and although the balance between piety and sin has been tipped heavily in favor of sin, Sri Krsna still arranges to revive human purity by reestablishing Satya-yuga and varnasrama-dharma. From the powerful Sun and Moon ksatriyas (both dynasties are destroyed early in Kali-yuga) arise two powerful ksatriya kings who even now live in the remote Himalayan village of Kalapa. At the end of the Age of Kali, these two kings, having been personally instructed by the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Vasudeva, will return to human society to reestablish varnasrama (SB. 12.2.37-38).

*Texts 39-44: The fate of foolish, materialistic kings*

**The continuing cycles of material existence**

This same general sequence of events, characterized by the continuous cycling of four ages - Satya, Treta, Dvapara, and Kali - occurs perpetually. Within these cycles, kings and others take birth and stake their claims over one property or another. Still, all are forced by time to renounce the work! and meet destruction. “Even though a person’s body may now have the designation ‘king,’ in the end its name will he ‘worms,’ ‘stool,’ or ‘ashes.’ What can a person who injures other living beings for the sake of his body know about his own self-interest, since his activities are simply leading him to hell?” (SB 12.2.41)

Srila Sridhara Svami’s comment on this point (stated in text 41) rephrases for emphasis Sukadeva Gosvami’s words: “Sukadeva condemns the propensity of violence against living beings... That same body now designated ‘king’ in the end is designated ‘worms,’ ‘stool,’ or ‘ashes.’ What does one know of his own best interest if for the sake of that body he becomes the enemy of living entities and commits violence against them? He does not know anything about his own self-interest, for due to committing such violence he will suffer in hell.”

Yet although such kings are unsure of their own fate, Sukadeva Gosvami continues, they sentimentally think: “This unbounded earth was held by my predecessors and is now under my sovereignty. How can I arrange for it to remain in the hands of my sons, grandsons, and other descendants?” (SB 12.2.42) Although they have accepted the body as the self and their possessions as their own, such kings are forced to abandon their current royal identity along with their triumphant deeds of conquest and pass into oblivion. “My dear King Pariksit, all these kings who tried to enjoy the earth by their strength were reduced by the force of time to nothing more than historical accounts.” (SB. 12.2.44)

Sukadeva Gosvami again applies the knife of detachment to free Maharaja Pariksit from any lingering scent of desire for kingdom or possessions or royal identity. The king’s own time now looms, with mere hours remaining until his passing from the earth.

**Chapter 3: The Bhumi-Gita**

*Texts 1-13: Bhumidevi describes the foolishness of kings who vie to control her*

Sukadeva Gosvami has noted that the foolish try to control the earth and then, before dying, pass their kingdoms to their descendants. Now, explains Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura, Bhumidevi, Mother Earth, will expand on this topic.

Bhumi had long ago prayed to the Supreme Lord to advent Himself and relieve her of the burden of the hundreds of thousands of military phalanxes made up of conceited demons dressed as kings. After listing the names and deeds of this succession of kings, who reign well into Kali-yuga, Sukadeva Gosvami now speaks of the earth’s plight during the increasingly horrific period following Lord Krsna’s departure from the earth: “Seeing the kings of this earth busy trying to conquer her, the earth herself laughed. She said: ‘Just see how these kings, who are actually playthings in the hands of death, are desiring to conquer me.’” (SB. 12.3.1)

Clearly, Bhumidevi’s disgust applies not only to kings but to all those who spend their lives trying to conquer, control, and exploit any part of the material world. Bhumi first describes the fatal flaw of demonic kings: “Great rulers of men, even those who are learned, meet frustration and failure because of material lust. Driven by lust, these kings place great hope and faith in the dead lump of flesh called the body, even though the material frame is as fleeting as bubbles of foam on water.” (SB. 12.3.2)

Srila Sridhara Svami comments: “Yena refers to kamena, lust. Bewildered by lust, the kings put their faith in this lump of flesh called the material body, which is likened to the bubbles on foam. Surely their lust will remain unfulfilled.”

Why would a ruler see his rise to a temporary position of power as a way to exploit others? It can only be because he mistakes his body for the self and becomes lost in meditation on imagined pleasures. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura characterizes the next two texts as an expansion on Bhumidevi’s description of lust. Unqualified Kali-yuga kings scheme hungrily: “‘First I will conquer my senses and mind; then I will subdue my chief ministers and rid myself of the thorn- pricks of my advisors, citizens, friends, and relatives, as well as the keepers of my elephants. In this way I will gradually conquer the entire earth. Because the hearts of these leaders are bound by great expectations, they fail to see death waiting nearby.” (SB. 12.3.3-4) Bhumi next speaks of their absurd, insatiable desires: “After conquering all the land on my surface, these proud kings forcibly enter the ocean to conquer the sea itself. What is the use of their self-control, which is aimed at political exploitation? The actual goal of self-control is spiritual liberation.” (SB. 12.3.5)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments: “After conquering the earth, they enter the ocean to steal the ocean’s jewels. Those who control their senses simply to attain a kingdom are fools.”

Bhumi wonders why, after having observed the past, such kings cannot predict their own futures: “Although in the past great men and their descendants have left me, departing from this world in the same helpless way they came into it, even today foolish men are trying to conquer me.” Futile, yet unbound ambition drives the engines of their lives: “For the sake of conquering me, materialistic persons fight one another. Fathers oppose their sons, and brothers fight one another, because their hearts are bound to possessing political power. Political leaders challenge one another: ‘All this land is mine! It’s not yours, you fool!’ Thus they attack one another and die.” (SB. 12.3.6-8) Bhumi continues: None of the many powerful rulers of the past, whether good or evil, were able to hold onto their control of me, even though they appeared unconquerable or had exalted qualities, the power to control others, were learned, or were great heroes. Time has reduced all of them to mere accounts in the histories. “None of them could permanently establish their rule.” (SB. 12.3.13)

*Texts 14-15: Hearing about kings and hearing about Krsna*

In the next two texts, 14 and 15, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami again gives his reason for telling all this to Maharaja Pariksit (both in the Ninth Canto and here): “O mighty Pariksit, I have related to you the narrations of all these great kings, who spread their fame throughout the world and then departed. My real purpose was to teach transcendental knowledge (vijnana) and renunciation. Stories of kings lend power and opulence to these narrations but do not in themselves constitute the ultimate aspect of knowledge.” (SB. 12.3.14)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura expands on Sukadeva’s point by first describing why Sukadeva related pastimes of devotee-kings who had attained the Lord, such as King Priyavrata. Visvanatha explains that hearers of the Bhagavatam should listen to these kings’ realizations, including how they renounced their positions. “O mighty Pariksit,” Sukadeva emphasizes, “You too will be like them.”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 250), Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.14, referring to Sukadeva Gosvami’s statement that he wished to teach vijnana: “Vijnanam means knowledge about the uselessness of material things. These stories were recited with a desire to speak of renunciation and the uselessness of material things. These stories of dead men are mere words. They are not related to the spiritual goal. What is that spiritual goal that is best for human beings? The next verse answers this: every day, at all times during the day, one should hear the narrations of the Lord.

Sukadeva Gosvami continues this line of thought as he talks about attaining “the ultimate aspect of knowledge,” which he defines as hearing and chanting about Krsna: “The person who desires pure devotional service to Lord Krsna should hear the narrations of Lord Uttamasloka’s glorious qualities, the constant chanting of which destroys everything inauspicious. The devotee should engage in such listening in regular daily assemblies and should also continue his hearing throughout the day.” (SB. 12.3.15)

How potent are the qualities and activities of Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead! How potent are hearing and chanting His glories! How glorious the results for those who follow this prescription! And how glorious is the Srimad-Bhagavatam for offering the perfect facility for absorption in these processes!

The BBT purport expands on the meaning of text 15: “Since any topic related to Lord Krsna is auspicious and transcendental, the direct narration of Lord Krsna’s own activities, political and non-political, is certainly the supreme subject matter for hearing. The word nityam here indicates regulated cultivation of the topics of Lord Krsna, and abhiksnam indicates constant remembrance of such regulated spiritual experiences.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura sums up the gift of facility to hear about Krsna that the Srimad-Bhagavatam offers: “Hear about the Lord’s great devotees, hear about Krsna’s eternal associates \[for hearing about His eternal associates is superior to hearing about His great devotees\], hear constantly about the Lord’s activities, for drey reveal His qualities, and hear the Bhagavatam’s Tenth Canto, for the Lord’s pastimes, although found in other cantos, are present everywhere in Canto Ten.”

*Texts 16-40: Questions from Maharaja Pariksit; answers from Sukadeva Gosvami*

*Texts 16-17: Maharaja Pariksit’s final questions*

After hearing the foolish Kali-yuga kings condemned (SB. 12.1.41), Pariksit Maharaja asks a compassionate question: “\[H\]ow can persons living in the age of Kali rid themselves of the cumulative contamination of this age? O great sage please explain this to me.” (SB. 12.1.16) I he King further inquires: “Please explain the different ages of universal history, the special qualities of each age, the duration of cosmic maintenance and destruction, and the movement of time, which is the direct representation of the Supreme Soul, the Personality of Godhead, Lord Visnu.” (SB. 12.3.17)

*Texts 18-19: The exalted characteristics of Satya-yuga*

Sukadeva Gosvami replies: In “Satya-yuga, the age of truth, religion is present with all four of its legs intact and is carefully maintained by the people of that age. These four legs of powerful religion are truthfulness, mercy, austerity, and charity. The people of Satya-yuga are for the most part self-satisfied, merciful, friendly to all, peaceful, sober, and tolerant. They take their pleasure from within, see all things equally, and always endeavor diligently for spiritual perfection.” (SB. 12.3.18-19)

*Texts 20-21: The downward spiral begins - the characteristics of Treta-yuga*

“In Treta-yuga each leg of religion is gradually reduced by one quarter by the influence of the four pillars of irreligion - lying, violence, dissatisfaction, and quarrel.” (SB. 12.3.20)

From the BBT purport: “By falsity truth is diminished, by violence mercy is diminished, by dissatisfaction austerity is diminished, and by quarrel charity and cleanliness are diminished.”

“In the Treta age people are devoted to ritual performances and severe austerities. They are not excessively violent or very lusty after sensual pleasure. Their interest lies primarily in religiosity, economic development, and regulated sense gratification, and they achieve prosperity by following the prescriptions of the three Vedas. Although in this age society evolves into four separate classes, O King, most people are brahmanas.” (SB. 12.3.21)

*Texts 22-23: Diminishing qualities in Dvapara-yuga*

“In Dvapara-yuga the religious qualities of austerity, truth, mercy, and charity are reduced to one half by their irreligious counterparts -dissatisfaction, untruth, violence, and enmity. In the Dvapara age people are interested in glory and are very noble. They devote themselves to the study of the Vedas, possess great opulence, support large families, and enjoy life with vigor. Of the four classes, the ksatriyas and brahmanas are most numerous.” (SB. 12.3.22-23)

*Texts 24-25: Characteristics of Kali-yuga, the iron age of quarrel*

“In the age of Kali only one fourth of the religious principles remains. That last remnant will continuously be decreased by the ever-increasing principles of irreligion and will finally be destroyed. In the Kali age people tend to be greedy, il-behaved, and merciless, and they fight one another without good reason. Unfortunate and obsessed with material desires, the people of Kali-yuga are almost all sudras and barbarians.” (SB. 12.3.24-25)

*Texts 26-30: The modes of nature dominant in each ages*

Time sets into motion the material modes - goodness, passion, and ignorance - and causes a specific mode to dominate each of the ages. Srila Sukadeva Gosvami describes the dominant mode in Satya-yuga: “When the mind, intelligence, and senses are solidly fixed in the mode of goodness, that time should be understood as Satya-yuga, the age of truth. People then take pleasure in knowledge and austerity.” (SB. 12.3.27)

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes in his comment on text 26 t hat in any particular yuga the qualities of all four yugas periodically manifest. Thus even in Kali-yuga, dharma has strength from time to time and does not decrease. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura goes i m to explain that this characteristic is seen even in people, because the modes also cycle within an individual person.

Sukadeva Gosvami continues: “\[W\]hen the conditioned souls are devoted to their duties but have ulterior motives and seek personal prestige, you should understand such a situation to be the age of Treta, in which the functions of passion are prominent.” (SB. 12.3.28)

The people of Satya-yuga perform dharma with no desire for mate- i ml results; those living in Treta-yuga perform dharma with a desire for material results.

“When greed, dissatisfaction, false pride, hypocrisy, and envy become prominent, along with attraction for selfish activities, such a lime is the age ot Dvapara, dominated by the mixed modes of passion and ignorance.” (SB. 12.3.29)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that Dvapara-yuga is characterized by a fondness for dharma with material motives and also for adharma, irreligious acts. During this age, rajas and tamas attain prominence, and greed and other inauspicious qualities also appear.

“When there is a predominance of cheating, lying, sloth, sleepiness, violence, depression, lamentation, bewilderment, fear, and poverty, that age is Kali, the age of the mode of ignorance.” (SB. 12.3.30)

*Texts 31-44: Further horrendous characteristics of Kali-yuga*

Sukadeva Gosvami now describes more of the faults that are natural to people living in Kali-yuga: “Because of the bad qualities of the Age of Kali, human beings will become shortsighted, unfortunate, gluttonous, lustful, and poverty-stricken. The women, becoming unchaste, will freely wander from one man to the next. Cities will be dominated by thieves, the Vedas will be contaminated by speculative interpretations of atheists, political leaders will virtually consume the citizens, and the so-called priests and intellectuals will be devotees of their bellies and genitals. The brahmacaris will fail to execute their vows and become generally unclean, the householders will become beggars, the vanaprasthas will live in the villages, and the sannyasis will become greedy for wealth. Women will become much smaller in size, and they will eat too much, have more children than they can properly take care of, and lose all shyness. They will always speak harshly and will exhibit qualities of thievery, deceit, and unrestrained audacity. Businessmen will engage in petty commerce and earn their money by cheating. Even when there is no emergency, people will consider any degraded occupation quite acceptable. Servants will abandon a master who has lost his wealth, even if that master is a saintly person of exemplary character. Masters will abandon an incapacitated servant, even if that servant has been in the family for generations. Cows will be abandoned or killed when they stop giving milk. In Kali-yuga men will be wretched and controlled by women. They will reject their fathers, brothers, other relatives, and friends and will instead associate with the sisters and brothers of their wives. Thus their conception of friendship will be based exclusively on sexual ties. Uncultured men will accept charity on behalf of the Lord and will earn their livelihood by making a show of austerity and wearing a mendicant’s dress. Those who know nothing about religion will mount a high seat and presume to speak on religious principles. In the Age of Kali, people’s minds will always be agitated. They will become emaciated by famine and taxation, my dear King, and will always be disturbed by fear of drought. They will lack adequate clothing, food, and drink, will be unable to properly rest, have sex, or bathe themselves, and will have no ornaments to decorate their bodies. In fact, the people of Kali-yuga will gradually come to appear like ghostly, haunted creatures. In Kali-yuga men will develop hatred for each other even over a few coins. Giving up all friendly relations, they will be ready to lose their own lives and kill even their own relatives. Men will no longer protect their elderly parents, their children, or their respectable wives. Thoroughly degraded, they will care only to satisfy their own bellies and genitals.” (SB. 12.3.31-42)

In the next two texts, 43 and 44, Sukadeva Gosvami describes the only remedy for Kali-yuga’s ever-increasing virulence as the end of the yuga approaches. In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 274), Srila Jiva Gosvami cites these two texts to illustrate how in Kali-yuga, it will only become possible to find devotion and surrender to the Lord through the power of nama-kirtana. Those who offend the holy name will become indifferent or averse to the Lord. “O King, in the age of Kali people’s intelligence will be diverted by atheism, and they will almost never offer sacrifice to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the supreme spiritual master of the universe. Although the great personalities who control the three worlds all bow down to the lotus feet of the Supreme Lord, the petty and miserable human beings of this age will not do so.” (SB. 12.3.43)

*Text 44: Neglect of Krsna’s holy name*

“Terrified, about to die, a man collapses on his bed. Although his voice is faltering and he is hardly conscious of what he is saying, if he utters the holy name of the Supreme Lord he can be freed from the reaction of his fruitive work and achieve the supreme destination. But still people in the age of Kali will not worship the Supreme Lord.” (SB. 12.3.44)

In his comment on this text, Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that close to the end of Kali-yuga, people’s indifference toward the Lord will be due to their minds being “distorted by atheism,” and that this distortion will only occur lit the minds of those who are averse to the Lord’s holy name.

*Texts 45-52: Removing the contamination of Kali-yuga*

*Text 45: Removing the age’s pervasive contaminations*

In Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.16, Maharaja Pariksit asked Sukadeva Go Svami how those living during Kali-yuga can rid themselves of the age’s contaminations and disabilities. After describing more about the age’s faults, Sukadeva now addresses this essential topic: “In the Kali-yuga, objects, places, and even individual personalities are all polluted. The almighty Personality of Godhead, however, can remove all such contamination from the life of one who fixes the Lord within his mind.” (SB. 12.3.45)

Srila Jiva Gosvami explains that texts 45-47 describe what the Lord’s name bestows as He manifests in this most personal form.

*Text 46: How to become purified from the faults inherent in Kali-yuga*

As light automatically erases darkness, the light of Krsna’s presence automatically removes the darkness of Kali-yuga’s faults: “If a person hears about, glorifies, meditates upon, worships, or simply offers great respect to the Supreme Lord, who is situated within the heart, the Lord will remove from his mind the contamination accumulated during many thousands of lifetimes.” (SB. 12.3.46)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that not only does the above process destroy the faults inherent in Kali-yuga, it also destroys the reactions to sins committed recently and in other lifetimes.

*Text 47: The purifying effect of the Lord’s presence in the heart*

“Just as fire applied to gold removes any discoloration caused by traces of other metals, Lord Visnu within the heart purifies the minds of the yogis.” (SB. 12.3.47)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that it takes fire, not water or some other substance, to remove impurities like copper from gold. Similarly, it is only Visnu in the hearts of the yogis who can remove the sins and impurities in the internal workings of their consciousness. Such purification cannot he achieved through yama, niyama, or any other such limbs of yoga.

*Text 48: The ultimate cause of purification - the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s appearance in the heart*

“By one’s engaging in the processes of demigod worship, austerities, breath control, compassion, bathing in holy places, strict vows, charity, and chanting of various mantras, one’s mind cannot attain the same absolute purification as that achieved when the unlimited Personality of Godhead appears within one’s heart.”

*Text 49: Sukadeva Gosvami’s conclusive advice to Maharaja Pariksit*

“Therefore, O King, endeavor with all your might to fix the Supreme Lord Kesava within your heart. Maintain this concentration upon the Lord, and at the time of death you will certainly attain the supreme destination.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami writes that texts 49 and 50 bring together all the ideas that are significant to Maharaja Pariksit and tell him what to do with everything he has heard. “With all your might,” Sri Jiva explains, “means with all endeavor.” Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura comments that while persons such as Ajamila remembered the Lord, they were not attentive. Still, their remembrance was effective due to Lord Kesava’s supreme potency, and they were given love for Him. If Pariksit Maharaja remembers Him with all attention, he will certainly attain Him — and Maharaja Pariksit is capable of such concentration because he is a topmost, intimate devotee.

*Text 50: The result of meditating on the Lord at the time of death*

“My dear King, the Personality of Godhead is the ultimate controller. He is the Supreme Soul \[sarvatma\] and the supreme shelter \[sarva-samsrayah\] of all beings. When meditated upon by those about to die, He reveals to them their own eternal spiritual identity \[atma-bhavam\].”

In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 86), Srila Jiva Gosvami comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.50 to eloquently express the glories of bhakti and Krsna’s benevolence: “The Lord produces bhava for Himself (atma-bhavam)! What is the use of jnana, which takes effort to bring results?”

In his own comment, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura offers hope based on the Lord’s merciful nature: “A dying person’s meditation on the Lord will cause that person to attain prema for Him. \[One may ask:\] How does the Lord know that they are meditating on Him? Although others may not know, He knows, because He is the soul of all (sarvatma). \[One may ask further:\] Why does the Lord give prema just because one meditates on Him once? He does so because He is the shelter of all beings (sarva-samsrayah), and from Him arise all practices (sadhanas) as well as all the results of those sadhanas. What is so remarkable about this for the Lord? He is so magnanimous!”

*Texts 51-52: The Age of Kali’s great benediction*

“My dear King, although Kali-yuga is an ocean of faults, there is still one good quality about this age: Simply by chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra, one can become free from material bondage and be promoted to the transcendental kingdom. Whatever result was obtained in Satya-yuga by meditating on Visnu, in Treta-yuga by performing sacrifices, and in Dvapara-yuga by serving the Lord’s lotus feet can be obtained in Kali-yuga simply by chanting the Hare Krsna maha-mantra.” (SB. 12.3.51-52)

According to Srila Jiva Gosvami, this text explains the reasons for what was previously described in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.5.36: “Those who are actually advanced in knowledge are able to appreciate the essential value of this Age of Kali. Such enlightened persons worship Kali-yuga, because in this fallen age all perfection of life can easily be achieved by the performance of sahkirtana."

Srila Jiva Gosvami continues: “That same Age of Kali, although truly an ocean of faults that defeat the goals of life, has one great quality: respect for the chanting of the Lord’s holy name.... Thus because a chanter of the holy name is not confronted with obstacles, he will become perfect.”

As always, Srila Jiva Gosvami’s message is consistent. In the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 86), he explains Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.51: “There is one good quality in Kali-yuga - that is, from chanting alone, which does not require the kind of effort jnana requires, one attains the Supreme Lord.”

To further glorify the power of chanting Krsna’s names and remembering Him through one’s chanting, Sri Jiva cites a reference from the Visnu Purana in the bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 115): “The moment that one does not think of Vasudeva, that moment immediately becomes destructive, full of fault, illusion, and mistakes.” In anuccheda 270 he adds: “Appearing in Kali-yuga for people most unfortunate by nature, sarikirtana very easily gives all results among the great processes for the respective yugas and makes those processes (and the persons taking to them) successful. Thus in Kali-yuga the Lord is especially pleased by sankirtana.” Sri Jiva then cites the Skanda Purana: “Chanting the Lord’s name, the best austerity for the people, should particularly he performed in Kali-yuga to please the Lord.”

Commenting on text 52, Sri Jiva writes: “Devotional service consisting of the process of chanting comprises the immeasurable mercy of the Personality of Godhead for the conditioned souls. His mercy is focused exclusively on those persons who are most unfortunate in terms of property, birth, qualities, and activities… That the people are very degraded in the Age of Kali is expressed in the Brahma-vaivarta Purana: ‘Thus in the Age of Kali the practices of austerities, yoga meditation, Deity worship, sacrifice, and so on, along with their various subsidiary functions, are not properly carried out, even by the most expert embodied souls.’ Therefore, that process of chanting, appearing among the naturally fallen people of Kali-yuga, easily awards them all the results of the great processes of spiritual advancement found in each of the other ages. Thus the people become successful in life, because by chanting in the Age of Kali, the Supreme Lord becomes especially satisfied. As stated in the Caturmasya-mahatmya of the Skanda Purana: The most perfect penance that can be executed in this world is the chanting of the name of Lord Sri Hari. It should be performed especially in the Age of Kali in order to satisfy Lord Visnu.’ Speaking this same idea, this text \[SB. 12.3.52\] states that chanting is indeed the ocean of all transcendental qualities, even in the Age of Kali. Whatever is accomplished by practicing the yuga-dharma of Satya-yuga \[or of other ages\] is accomplished in Kali simply by chanting the name of Hari.”

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.3.50 and 51 inspire readers to chant Krsna’s holy names sincerely: “Now in two verses it is said that Kali is the best of all yugas. Although Kali is an ocean of faults, one good quality rules like a king \[over his kingdom\|. As one king alone kills many thieves, this one good quality destroys all the faults of Kali that were just mentioned. What is that quality? It is through chanting alone, which is independent of meditation and other processes, that one attains the highest human goal, prema. Or, chanting by itself can produce results, and then what to speak if one combines meditation \[and the other bhakti processes\] with chanting.”

**Chapter 4: Four Categories of Universal Annihilation**

*Texts 1-4: Annihilation one - “occasional” (naimittika), or the annihilation at the end of Brahmas day*

In the seventeenth text of the last chapter, Maharaja Pariksit asked Sukadeva Gosvami about “the duration of cosmic maintenance and destruction” as well as about “the movement of time.” Sukadeva Gosvami’s answers to these questions will point to Krsna’s functioning in this world as unstoppable time, the great destroyer of everything in existence, and “the direct representation of the Supreme Soul, the Personality of Godhead, Lord Visnu.”

First, Sukadeva says that he has already described how time is measured (Third Canto, chapter 11), as well as the various lengths of time and the characteristics of each of the four yugas. Now he will describe the four types of annihilation, beginning with an accounting of the length of Brahma’s day and how long the annihilation lasts.

“One thousand cycles of four ages constitute a single day of Brahma, known as a kalpa. In that period, O King, fourteen Manus come and go. After one day of Brahma, annihilation occurs during his night, which is of the same duration. At that time all the three planetary systems are subject to destruction.” (SB. 12.4.2- 3) During this annihilation, Lord Narayana lies down on His bed of Ananta Sesa and absorbs the entire universe within Himself as Lord Brahma sleeps.

*Texts 5-22: Annihilation two - annihilation at the end of Brahma’s life (prakrtika)*

A more complete annihilation occurs in the middle and at the end of Brahma’s life. At that time the basic elements of creation are annihilated and the universe itself is confronted with destruction. First, there is no rain. Starving, those living on the earth begin to eat one another. The sun scorches the land and dries up all the water, even the ocean. Slowly, the burning universe glows like a burning ball of cow dung. Winds blow for more than a hundred years, and the dust- filled sky is ever gray. Then it begins to rain, flooding the earth and the whole universe, turning it into a single ocean. The essential elements of creation then dissolve, one after the other, gross element into its subtler cause, until everything, impelled by time, rests in the original, unmanifest pradhana. “That unmanifest nature is not subject to the six kinds of transformation caused by the influence of time. Rather, it has no beginning and no end. It is the unmanifest, eternal, and infallible cause of creation. The situation is just like that of complete sleep, or of voidness. Indeed, it is indescribable. Authorities in spiritual science explain, however, that since pradhana is the original substance, it is the actual basis of material creation. This is the annihilation called prakrtika, during which the energies belonging to the Supreme Person and His unmanifest material nature, disassembled by the force of time, are deprived of their potencies and merge together totally. (SB. 12.4.19-22)

*Texts 23-34: Annihilation three - the ultimate annihilation of material existence (atyantika)*

The false ego causes the soul to see objects as if they are separate from the Absolute Truth and meant for the individual soul’s enjoyment. The false ego, therefore, is considered the heart of illusion. So the ultimate annihilation of material existence (atyantika) occurs when the soul finally peels off its false ego and sees everything in existence in its true relationship with the Absolute. In texts 23-31, Sukadeva Gosvami will help Maharaja Pariksit gain this realization by describing the unknowable Absolute Truth using readily observable examples.

But first he begins with philosophy, describing the relationship between (1) how one perceives (through the intelligence and senses) and (2) what is perceived (the sense objects) - and both of these points with (3) the Paramatma manifestation of the Absolute Truth: “It is the Absolute Truth alone who manifests in the forms of intelligence, the senses, and the objects of sense perception, and who is their ultimate basis. Whatever has a beginning and an end is insubstantial because of being an object perceived by limited senses and because of being nondifferent from its own cause.” (SB. 12.4.23)

Everything that can he perceived in the realm of matter, temporary though it may be, ultimately manifests from the eternal Absolute Truth. That Absolute Truth is therefore reality, for it is the source and basis of its own many manifestations.

All objects capable of being perceived by the limited senses are considered insubstantial because they are ephemeral. The BBT purport to text 23 explains: “\[A\] 11 subtle and gross material manifestations are made visible by the potency of the Supreme Lord and again become invisible, or unmanifest, at the time of annihilation. They are therefore in essence not separate from the source of their expansion and withdrawal.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura indicates that this text describes the oneness of existence, which impersonalists achieve after realizing Brahman as the cause of this insubstantial world of duality. These impersonalists boldly say, “This world is illusory.’ Their realization of the unity of Brahman is explained in the next nine texts (SB. 12.4.23-31). Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that intelligence, the senses, and their objects are simply transformations of the potencies of Brahman, which is therefore their cause - and thus also their shelter. All these products come into being and are destroyed, so from the spiritual point of view, the products, being temporary, are unreal.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura presents a text from the Gopala-tapani Upanisad (tasam madhy brahma gopala-puri)to show that, unlike the fleeting world of illusion, Krsna’s abode is beyond the modes of nature and is therefore eternal. He also presents Krsna’s words in Srimad-Bhagavatam 11.25.26 (nirguno mad-apasrayah) to prove that one who has taken shelter of Him is also transcendental, beyond the modes of nature, and eternal.

In texts 24-31, the great teacher Sukadeva Gosvami uses common examples to further illustrate the relationship between everything that exists and the Absolute Truth.

*Text 24: Light*

“A lamp, the eye that views by the light of that lamp, and the visible form that is viewed are all basically nondifferent from the element fire.
