By this bona fide hearing process, the neophyte devotee becomes cleansed of all material rubbish, and thus he becomes attached to one of the many transcendental forms of the Lord, as described in the Vedas.

This attachment of the devotee to a particular form of the Lord is due to natural inclination. Each and every living entity is originally attached to a particular type of transcendental service because he is eternally the servitor of the Lord. Lord Caitanya says that the living entity is eternally a servitor of the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Sri Krsna. Therefore, every living entity has a particular type of service relationship with the Lord, eternally. This particular attachment is invoked by practice of regulative devotional service to the Lord, and thus the devotee becomes attached to the eternal form of the Lord, exactly like one who is already eternally attached. This attachment for a particular form of the Lord is called svarupa-siddhi. The Lord sits on the lotus heart of the devotee in the eternal form the pure devotee desires, and thus the Lord does not part from the devotee.

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comments on Srimad-Bhagavatam 3.9.11 are also striking:

The devotees, however, even without knowledge, cross over the ocean of birth and death. From this verse it is clear that by devotion these devotees make even You subservient. It can also be explained. bhakti-yoga paribhavita, inspired only by bhakti-yoga, the Lord in all respects (pari) reveals Himself to those who approach Him with fixed devotion. Thus it is understood that the means of evoking the Lord’s manifestation is only bhakti-yoga. Due to their devotion, You come onto the lotus of their hearts, and having come, You stay. That You do not go away has already been stated in Bhagavatam 3.9.5: napaisi natha, “You are never separated from the lotus of their hearts.” The path to reach You is first heard from the guru’s mouth and then seen and perceived directly. By that same path (hearing from one’s guru) You enter into the lotus of their hearts. This implies that among all the paths, the devotees \[who have heard from the guru’s mouth\] perfectly ascertain the exact way of practicing sadhana-bhakti. The further implication is that if someone has a desire to attain the Lord, he should also seek to thoroughly ascertain the path. Moreover, if even without hearing, Your devotee fixes his mind on a particular form of Yours in meditation, You then manifest that exact form. So says the revered Sridhara Svami. Or else it means: Those practicing devotees, by their intelligence, meditate on a certain form according to their particular mood, and You manifest that exact body for them, which is their siddha-deha, their body of perfection, making them obtain it in all its splendor. Oh, how submissive to Your devotees You are! This is the purport.

*Texts 27-50: The sun god’s personal features and associates*

*Texts 27-28: Saunaka Rsi inquires about the sun god and his associates*

Saunaka Rsi now asks Suta Gosvami to speak about the sun god, for as Yajnavalkya indicated in his prayers (SB. 12.6.67-72), the sun god manifests the energy of Lord Hari. In addition, the sun, as Suta Gosvami just explained in Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.11.17, is the Lord’s form in which He is worshiped by the devatas.

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.11.27-28 explains Saunaka Rsi’s inquiry about those aspects of the sun that are in relation to Lord Hari: “After hearing an account of the exalted conversation between Sukadeva Gosvami and Maharaja Pariksit, Saunaka now inquires about the sun as the expansion of the Supreme Lord. Although the sun is the king of all planets, Sri Saunaka is specifically interested in this effulgent globe as the expansion of Sri Hari, the Supreme Personality of Godhead.”

Saunaka Rsi wants to hear details about the sun: “Please describe to us, who have great faith in your words, the different sets of seven personal features and associates the sun god exhibits during each month, along with their names and activities. The associates of the sun god, who serve their lord, are personal expansions of the Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari in His feature as the presiding deity of the sun.” (SB. 12.11.27-28)

*Texts 29-50: The functions of the sun god and the categories of his associates*

Suta Gosvami first clarifies some basic principles: “The sun travels among all the planets and thus regulates their movements. It has been created by Lord Visnu, the Supreme Soul of all embodied beings, through His beginningless material energy.... Being the source of the material energy, the Personality of Godhead Lord Hari in His expansion as the sun god is described in nine aspects, O Saunaka: the time, the place, the endeavor, the performer, the instrument, the specific ritual, the scripture, the paraphernalia of worship, and the result to be achieved.” (SB. 12.11.29, 31)

In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.11.30, Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that by the logic of “nondifferent from it,” Lord Hari is the sun. Such phrases as “the one Soul of the worlds” are adjectives modifying Lord Hari. In his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.11.29, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains the sense in which the sun is not the Supreme Lord: “One should not think that the sun, which in Srimad-Bhagavatam is compared to Krsna, who has a spiritual body of eternity, bliss, and knowledge, is material. That is, the sun has been created by Visnu, who is the soul of all embodied beings, but it is not Visnu Himself. Rather, the sun is a form of His fiery potency - of His power or effulgence created by beginningless maya. Thus it is another of His vibhutis. The sun initiates the livelihood of the worlds.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment on text 31 details the performance of sacrifices. These sacrifices, all based on rites offered at specific times, indicate how the sun initates and engages Vedic followers in pious activities that elevate them to the heavenly planets.

Srila Sridhara Svami, commenting on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.11.32, notes that the Personality of Godhead assumes the form of time and travels separately in the twelve months to sustain the universe. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti concurs: “The Supreme Personality of Godhead, assuming the form of time, takes on the form of the sun.”

Thus the Supreme Personality of Godhead manifests His potency as the sun god and as time in order to institute sacred actions throughout each month of the year. He also regulates the planetary motions. Each month, a different set of six associates accompanies the sun god: an Apsara, a Raksasa, a Naga, a Yaksa, a sage, and a Gandharva.As the sun god travels, “the sages glorify the sun god with the hymns of the Sama, Rg, and Yajur Vedas, which reveal his identity, the Gandharvas also sing his praises, and the Apsaras dance before his chariot. The Nagas arrange the chariot ropes and the Yaksas harness the horses to the chariot, while the powerful Raksasas push from behind.” (SB. 12.11.48) 66,000 brahmana sages, known as the Valakhilyas, face the sun god and offer prayers as he arcs through the sky.

All these personalities are the Supreme Personality of Godhead’s energies - either as the Lord’s expansion in the form of the sun god or in the form of servants of that form. By their potency, these deities remove the “sinful reactions of those who remember them each day at dawn and sunset.” (SB. 12.11.45)

In this way, Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead moves the planets and acts as time to engage souls in auspicious Vedic rites. “For the protection of all the worlds, the Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari, who is unborn and without beginning or end, thus expands Himself during each day of Brahma into these specific categories of His personal representations.” (SB. 12.11.50)

**Chapter 12: The Topics of Srimad-Bhagavatam Summarized**

*Texts 1-4: The glories of hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam*

*suta uvaca*

*namo dharmaya mahate*

*namah krsnaya vedhase*

*brahmanebhyo namaskrtya*

*dharman vaksye sanatanan*

“Suta Gosvami said: Offering my obeisances to the supreme \[mahate\] religious principle, devotional service; to Lord Krsna, the supreme creator; and to all the brahmanas, I shall now describe the eternal principles of religion \[dharman sanatanan\].” (SB. 12.12.1)

Before Srila Suta Gosvami mentions the word bhakti, he offers his respects to die supreme religious principle, which is eternal and which reveals the eternal; Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is attained by bhakti, and whose activities are eternal and beyond the modes of nature; and the brahmanas, such as Srila Vyasadeva, who reveal bhakti, the eternal religious principle.

Both Srila Sridhara Svami and Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura state in their comments on this first text of chapter 12 that the supreme (mahate) religious principle to which Srila Suta Gosvami is referring is indeed bhakti: “To the great (mahate) means to that which is characterized by devotion to Lord Hari.” (Srila Sridhara Svami) And “To the great (mahate) means to that which is characterized by devotional service.” (Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura)

In his purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam. 7.11.2, Srila Prabhupada also asserts that bhakti is the eternal religious principle (sanatana-dharma) common to all souls:

Sanatana-dharma means devotional service. The word sanatana refers to that which is eternal, which does not change but continues in all circumstances. We have several times explained what the eternal occupational duty of the living being is. Indeed, it has been explained by Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. Jivera ‘svarupa’ haya-krsnera ‘nitya-dasa’: the real occupational duty of the living entity is to serve the Supreme Personality of Godhead. Even if one prefers to deviate from this principle he remains a servant because that is his eternal position; but one serves maya, the illusory, material energy. The Krsna consciousness movement, therefore, is an attempt to guide human society to serving the Personality of Godhead instead of serving the material world with no real profit.

His obeisances complete, Suta Gosvami then speaks of the special position of the Bhagavatam, which exclusively narrates the immensely purifying pastimes of the Supreme Lord: “O great sages, I have narrated to you the wonderful pastimes of Lord Visnu, as you inquired about them from me. Hearing such narrations is the suitable engagement for a person who is actually a human being. This literature fully glorifies the Supreme Personality of Godhead Hari, who removes all His devotees’ sinful reactions. The Lord is glorified as Narayana, Hrsikesa, and the Lord of the Satvatas.” (SB. 12.12.2-3)

In his important comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.12.3, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura speaks of the necessity to hear the Bhagavatam’s krsnadmtha while one also engages oneself in the processes of religion: “\[I\]n the Age of Quarrel, three legs of sin and only one leg of piety remain, and that also is subject to diminution. Therefore the process of harisankirtana has been established. In the Age of Kali, by performing the sankirtana of Lord Hari, the living entities’ wrong engagements and sinful propensities on the platform of fruitive work are directly subdued. If in the processes of Deity worship, performance of sacrifice, and meditation some other object apart from Lord Hari is imagined to be the basis, the achievement of any proper result is automatically obstructed. Therefore, it is by engaging in the narration of the sankirtana of Lord Hari that these four engagements become properly directed to their actual object.”

Sri Suta Gosvami continues: “This literature describes the mystery of the Supreme Absolute Truth \[brahma param guhyam\], the source of the creation and annihilation of this universe. Also presented are divine knowledge of Him together with the process of its cultivation, and the transcendental realization one achieves.” (SB. 12.12.4)

The Bhagavatam describes Brahman. Although Brahman is indescribable, Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains, it is still indirectly described through narrations of the creation and annihilation of the universe jnana, the method of attaining Brahman realization, is also described.

*Texts 5-46: Suta Gosvami recounts all the topics discussed in Srimad-Bhagavatam*

As if listing the Bhagavatam’s table of contents, Srila Suta Gosvami now tells the sages of Naimisaranya some of the important points the Srimad-Bhagavatam has discussed. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura indicates that this list, however, does not contain all the topics discussed in the Bhagavatam: “The very famous chapter about Krsna’s birth, the punishment of Asvatthama, the passing of Bhisma, the story of Citraketu, the destruction of Tripura, the story of Ambarisa, the killing of Aghasura, and the bewilderment of Brahma are omitted or passed over very briefly. And sometimes stories are placed in a different order.”

**Canto by canto, Suta Gosvami’s list**

Texts 5-6: Canto One - devotional service, with its subsidiary feature of renunciation; the history of the sage Narada; the history of Maharaja Pariksit, including the king’s decision to fast until death in response to hearing that he had been cursed by a brahmana boy; and the beginning of the dialogue between Pariksit and Sukadeva Gosvami.

Text 7: Canto Two - attaining liberation at the time of death through yoga; the discussion between Narada and Brahma; a list of the Lord’s in- carnations; and a sequential description of the creation of the universe.

Texts 8-13: Canto Three - Vidura’s discussions with both Uddhava and Maitreya; the winding up of the creation into the the abdomen of Lord Visnu at the time of annihilation; the primal creation (sarga) beginning from prakrti, which includes the creation of the universal egg and the universal form; the movements of time and Brahma generated from the lotus; Hiranyaksa killed and the earth delivered from the Garbhodaka Ocean; Brahma’s creation of demigods, animals, demons; Rudra; the appearance of Svayambhuva Manu and Satarupa; the offspring of the wives of Prajapati Kardama and the Kapila incarnation along with His instructions to His mother, Devahuti.

Texts 14-16: Cantos Four and Five - the progeny of the nine great brahmanas; the destruction of Daksa’s sacrifice; the histories of Dhruva Maharaja and King Prthu, and King Pracinabarhi’s discussion with Narada (Canto Four); the life of Maharaja Priyavrata; the character and activities of King Nabhi, Lord Rsabha, and King Bharata; a description of the earth’s continents, regions, oceans, mountains, and rivers; and a description of the celestial sphere, the subterranean regions, and hell (Canto Five).

Texts 17-18: Cantos Six and Seven - the rebirth of Prajapati Daksa as the son of the Pracetas, and the progeny of Daksa’s daughters, who “initiate” the races of demigods, demons, human beings, animals, serpents, and birds; the births and deaths of Vrtrasura (Canto Six); the birth of Diti’s sons Hiranyaksa and Hiranyakasipu; and the history of the great Prahlada Maharaja (Canto Seven).

Texts 19—26: Cantos Eight and Nine — The reign of each Manu; the liberation of Gajendra; the special incarnations of Lord Visnu in each manvantara, such as Lord Hayasirsa; the Lord’s appearance as Kurma, Matsya, Narasimha, anti Vamana; the demigods’ churning of the Milk Ocean to obtain nectar; the great battle between the demigods and the demons (Canto Eight); the dynasties of various kings, and the birth and dynasty of Iksvaku; the dynasty of the pious Sudyumna; the histories of Ila and Tara; the descendants of the sun god, including kings Sasada and Nrga; the histories of Sukanya, Saryati, Kakutstha, Khatvariga, Mandhata, Saubhari, and Sagara; the pastimes of Lord Ramacandra; how King Nimi abandoned his material body; the descendants of King Janaka; the pastimes of Lord Parasurama, who annihilated the ksatriya dynasties; the kings in the Moon dynasty, such as Aila, Yayati, Nahusa, Dusmanta’s son Bharata, Santanu, and Santanu’s son Bhisma; the dynasty founded by King Yadu, Yayati’s eldest son (Canto Nine).

Texts 27-41: Canto Ten - “How Sri Krsna, the Supreme Personality of Godhead and Lord of the universe, descended into this Yadu dynasty, how He took birth in the home of Vasudeva, and how He then grew up in Gokula - all this is described in detail.” (SB. 12.12.27)

Commenting on text 27, Srila Jiva Gosvami points to the fact that Krsna simultaneously took birth in Mathura and Gokula: “And ‘His growing up in Gokula’ implies, by the use of the word ‘and,’ His birth there as well. Otherwise, simply ‘His growing up’ would have been stated. The proof of this fact \[that Lord Krsna took birth in two places\], is made in Sri Krsna Sandarbha in connection with the verses beginning nandas tv atma-ja utpanne \[SB. 10.5.1-2: ‘Nanda Maharaja was naturally very magnanimous, and when Lord Sri Krsna appeared as his son, he was overwhelmed by jubilation. Therefore, after bathing and purifying himself and dressing himself properly, he invited brahmanas who knew how to recite Vedic mantras. After having these qualified brahmanas recite auspicious Vedic hymns, he arranged to have the Vedic birth ceremony celebrated for his newborn child according to the rules and regulations, and he also arranged for worship of the demigods and forefathers.’\].”

Suta Gosvami continues his summary of Canto Ten: Krsna’s childhood pastimes of sucking out Putana’s life air, breaking the cart, trampling Trnavarta, killing Bakasura, Vatsasura, and Aghasura, and the pastime of Lord Brahma hiding Krsna’s calves and cowherd boyfriends in a cave; Krsna and Balarama killing Dhenukasura, Balarama destroying Pralambasura, and Krsna saving the cowherd boys from a raging forest fire; Krsna chastising Kaliya, His rescuing Nanda Maharaja from a great snake; the young gopi's severe vows, which satisfied Krsna; Krsna’s mercy to the wives of the Vedic brahmanas, who felt remorse; Krsna lift- ing Govardhana Hill, followed by the worship and bathing ceremony performed by Indra and the surabhi cow; Krsna’s nocturnal pastimes with the cowherd girls; the killing of Sankhacuda, Arista, and Kesi, the arrival of Akrura and subsequent departure of Krsna and Balarama, and the lamentation of the gopis; Krsna’s tour of Mathura; Krsna and Balarama killing Kuvalayapida, Mustika, Canura, Karhsa, and other demons; Krsna returning to life the dead son of Sandipani Muni; how Krsna, while residing in Mathura in the company of Uddhava and Balarama, satisfied the Yadu dynasty; Krsna annihilating each of the armies Jarasandha brought to Mathura; Krsna killing Kalayavana and establishing Dvaraka; Krsna bringing from heaven the parijata tree and the Sudharma assembly hall; Krsna kidnapping Rukmini by defeating His rivals in battle; Krsna’s battle with Banasura, where He defeated Lord Siva by making him yawn and then lopped off almost all of Banasura s arms; killing the master of Pragjyotisapura and rescuing the princesses he held captive; the deaths of Sisupala, Paundraka, Salva, Dantavakra, Sambara, Dvivida, Pitha, Mura, Pancajana, and other demons, along with burning Varanasi to the ground; Krsna relieving the earth s burden by arranging the Battle of Kuruksetra.

*Texts 42-43: Canto Eleven*

“How the Lord withdrew His own dynasty on the pretext of the brahmanas’ curse; Vasudeva’s conversation with Narada; the extraordinary conversation between Uddhava and Krsna, which reveals the science of the self in complete detail and elucidates the religious principles of human society; and then how Lord Krsna gave up this mortal world by His own mystic power - the Bhagavatam narrates all these events.”

*Texts 44-46: Canto Twelve*

“This work also describes people’s characteristics and behavior in the different ages, the chaos men experience in the age of Kali, the four kinds of annihilation and the three kinds of creation. There are also an account of the passing away of the wise and saintly King Visnurata \[Pariksit\], an explanation of how Srda Vyasadeva disseminated the branches of the Vedas, a pious narration concerning Markandeya Rsi, and a description of the detailed arrangement of the Lord’s universal form and His form as the sun, the soul of the universe.” (SB. 12.12.44-45)

Suta Gosvami adds: “Thus, O best of the brahmanas, I have explained herein what you have inquired from me. This literature has glorified in full detail the activities of the Lord’s pastime incarnations.” (SB. 12.12.46)

*Texts 47-69: The power of chanting and hearing about Krsna, and the glories of Srimad-Bhagavatam*

*Texts 47-50: The potency of Krsna s names, pastimes, and the Srimad-Bhagavatam*

“If when falling, slipping, feeling pain, or sneezing one involuntarily cries out in a loud voice, ‘Obeisances to Lord Hari!’ one will be automatically freed from all his sinful reactions.” (SB. 12.12.47)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that this text answers the question using kaimutya-nyaya, “If this is true, then how much more true is it that.” The result of hearing and chanting about Krsna’s pastimes, as they have just been narrated is as follows: “If casually chanting the Lord’s name bestows such great results, how much more will be bestowed if one chants about His pastimes with faith?”

The BBT purport repeats Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, who explains, “Lord Sri Caitanya is always loudly chanting the song haraye namah krsna in the courtyard of Srivasa Thakura. This same Lord Caitanya will free us from our materialistic enjoying propensity if we also loudly chant the glories of the Supreme Lord Hari.”

Sri Suta Gosvami continues: “When people properly glorify the Supreme Personality of Godhead or simply hear about His power, the Lord personally enters their hearts and destroys unlimited misfortune, just as the sun removes the darkness or as a powerful wind drives away the clouds.” (SB. 12.12.48)

The Lord enters the hearts of those who glorify Him. In those hearts He destroys misfortune, as the sun chases away the darkness of night err the wind drives away the darkness caused by a cloud-filled sky. Suta Gosvami’s final recommendation is that one should ignore literature horn of the material platform and should instead read, hear, and chant Srimad-Bhagavatam. Krsna purifies the hearts of those eager to hear Srimad Bhagavatam. Suta Gosvami made this same point in Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.2.17: “Sri Krsna, lhe Personality of Godhead, who is the Paramatma in everyone’s heart and the benefactor of the truthful devotee, cleanses desire for material enjoyment from the heart of the devotee who has developed the urge to hear His messages, which are in themselves virtuous when properly heard and chanted.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura’s comments on this point are strong and inspiring: “Those living beings who are not interested in discussions about the Personality of Godhead are bound by misfortune. Krsna-katha is definitely needed to ward off the karmic reactions conditioned souls have accumulated and which lead them to evil destinations. In their roles as enjoyers of the various sense objects of this temporary world, the conditioned living beings remain incapable of achieving the close association of Vaikuntha, because they have no ability to hear about such places. And because what they do hear is not properly told, they do not develop the direct experience that comes from proper hearing. But when topics of Vaikuntha are chanted and heard properly, they enter the jivas’ hearts and minds and destroy their propensities for enjoyment \[karma\] and renunciation \[jnaria\]. Just as a strong wind drives away the clouds, and as sunlight destroys the night, so when the kirtana of Lord Hari enters the ears, all tendencies for enjoyment and renunciation are destroyed.”

Sri Suta Gosvami further glorifies Srimad-Bhagavatam: “Words that do not describe the transcendental Personality of Godhead \[asat-katha\] but instead deal with temporary matters are simply false and useless \[asatih\]. Only those words that manifest the transcendental qualities of the Supreme Lord are actually truthful, auspicious, and pious.” (SB. 12.12.49)

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s powerful comment indicates the nature of words that glorify the Supreme Lord: “The conclusion of this scripture is that one should glorify Krsna. Glorification of other things, though not done badly, should not be done. Glorification of the Lord, even if done badly by animalistic men, should be done. Glorification of other things or persons, although spoken with truthful words - those same words are considered false. Although the words may be sweet, they are painful. Even if these words are uttered by learned persons, they are useless. Why? Because they do not speak about Bhagavan. Thus true words are false, sweet words are harsh, and learned words are useless. If words glorify the Lord but are false, coming only from one’s imagination, then they yet remain true. Although words may be inauspicious because they destroy a householder’s world, they are actually auspicious \[if they glorify Krsna\]. And although low-class people say that descriptions of the Lord taking the wives of others \[in the night\] are impure, those descriptions are pure, because both descriptions and the deeds they describe indicate not the Lord’s faults but His good qualities.”

*Texts 50-52: Two of three texts that are like bija syllables of the Bhagavatam*

Suta Gosvami’s glorification of the Bhagavatam continues: “Those words describing the glories of the all-famous Personality of Godhead \[anugiyate\] are attractive, relishable, and ever fresh. Indeed, such words are a perpetual festival for the mind, and they dry up the ocean of misery.” (SB. 12.12.50)

Srila Jiva Gosvami writes about these two texts in the Bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 269): “Asatih means ‘not true.’ Asat-katha means to speak about things other than the Lord and His devotees. Words are illusory and untrue when describing topics other than the Lord. Words concerning His pastimes, in which His fame is sung (anugiyate), are true and auspicious. Why? Because they manifest the Lord’s qualities in the heart of the singer. This means those words produce attraction (rati) for the Lord. It is said: ‘O king! The Lord goes wherever topics glorifying Him are spoken, just as a cow goes to her calf out of affection,’ and ‘I do not give up that person who recites topics about Me constantly, is attracted to hearing about Me, and whose mind is attracted to My hari-katha.’ (Visnu-dharma)

“Anugiyate,” Srila Jiva continues, “implies that one who has a pleasant voice should sing the Lord’s pastimes as well as about His name, form, and qualities.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes more in the mood of his previous comment: “Although the topic of Krsna’s following Prasena into Jambavan’s cave is unpleasant, it is also pleasant. Although Rama’s giving up Sita is not pleasant, it is also pleasant. Although the stories of the Lord are old, they are ever new. Although pursuit of Marica and Ravana’s theft of Sita destroys the mind’s happiness, they also create a festival in the mind. Although one falls into an ocean of lamentation upon seeing Krsna give up His wives and sons, the event dries up the ocean of lamentation.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura encourages us still further lo continue hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam: “Narrations about the Supreme Personality of Godhead give rise to the living entity’s eternal auspiciousness. Chanting the Lord’s glories can dry up the unfathomable water of the ocean of misery, which is based on people’s imperfections. Krsna-katha can produce an eternal festival in the minds of the jivas, and these topics become constantly newer and newer; they give the highest transcendental taste and are most attractive. But discussing topics that have nothing to do with Lord Krsna simply drown the mind in an ocean of misery. Discussions of the glories of the Personality of Godhead transform spiritual poverty into health for the spirit soul, who then lives in his natural habitat of variety (in the spiritual realm).”

In contrast to his praise of words that describe the Supreme Lord, Suta Gosvami now criticizes any words spoken for any other purpose: “Those words that do not describe the glories of the Lord, who alone can sanctify the atmosphere of the whole universe, are considered to be like unto a place of pilgrimage for crows, and are never resorted to by those situated in transcendental knowledge. The pure and saintly devotees take interest only in topics glorifying the infallible Supreme Lord.” (SB. 12.12.51)

Here Suta echoes Narada Muni: “Those words that do not describe the glories of the Lord, who alone can sanctify the atmosphere of the whole universe, are considered to be like unto a place of pilgrimage for crows, and are never resorted to by those situated in transcendental knowledge. The pure and saintly devotees take interest only in topics glorifying the infallible Supreme Lord.” (SB. 1.5.10)

Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that both text 51 and the next two texts glorify the supreme position of devotees. He also notes that although spoken in somewhat different forms, these three texts are placed both at the beginning of Srimad-Bhagavatam (SB. 1.5.10-12) and at its end (SB. 12.12.51-53). He compares these three texts to the bija (seed) syllable placed at the beginning and end of any great mantra.

“On the other hand, that literature which is full of descriptions of the transcendental glories of the name, fame, forms, pastimes, and so on of the unlimited Supreme Lord is a different creation, full of transcendental words directed toward bringing about a revolution in the impious lives of this world’s misdirected civilization. Such transcendental literatures, even though imperfectly composed, are heard, sung, and accepted by purified men who are thoroughly honest. (SB. 12.12.52)

In his comment, Srila Jiva Gosvami emphasizes the attraction Krsna’s devotees have for their Lord’s glories: “That creation of words, that use of language, is a revolution to overturn people’s sins. Glorification of Krsna destroys the sins of all \[who hear it\]. Because of this, those who speak such glorification sing it aloud when hearers are present, and if no hearers are present they recite this glorification to themselves.”

*Text 53: The third of the Bhagavatam’s bija-like texts*

“Knowledge of self-realization, even though free from all material affinity, does not look well if devoid of a conception of the Infallible \[God\]. What, then, is the use of even the most properly performed fruitive activities, which are naturally painful from the very beginning and transient by nature, if they are not utilized for the devotional service of the Lord?” (SB. 12.12.53)

*Texts 54-56: Further glories of Srimad-Bhagavatam*

Srila Sridhara Svami notes that the previous text and texts 54-55 indicate that even more respect should be given to hearing and chanting about the Personality of Godhead than to the processes of knowledge and fruitive work.

*Text 54: The contrast between performing varnasrama duties and hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam*

“The great endeavor one undergoes in executing the ordinary social and religious duties of the varnasrama system, in performing austerities, and in hearing from the Vedas culminates only in the achievement of mundane fame and opulence. But by respecting and attentively hearing the recitation of the transcendental qualities of the Supreme Lord, the husband of the goddess of fortune, one can remember His lotus feet.” (SB. 12.12.54)

*Text 55: The result of remembering Krsna*

What is the result of remembering Sri Krsna? Sura Gosvami tells us: “Remembrance of Lord Krsna’s lotus feet destroys everything inauspicious and awards the greatest good fortune. It purifies the heart and bestows devotion for the Supreme Soul \[paramatma-bhaktim\], along with knowledge enriched with realization and renunciation.” (SB. 12.12.55)

Srila Jiva Gosvami comments in the bhakti Sandarbha (anuccheda 276) that the main gift of remembering the Lord’s lotus feet is that one receives prema-bhakti for Krsna (paramatma-bhaktim). “Other results \[knowledge and renunciation\] are secondary.”

Not only does remembrance of the Lord destroy all inauspiciousness, comments Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura, but genuine and unlimited auspiciousness follows one who remembers Krsna.

*Text 56: The goal - worship Krsna*

Sri Suta Gosvami continues: “O most eminent of brahmanas, you are all indeed extremely fortunate, since you have already placed within your hearts Lord Sri Narayana - the Personality of Godhead, the supreme controller and the ultimate Soul of all existence - beyond whom there is no other god. You have undeviating love for Him, and thus I request you to worship Him.” (SB. 12.12.56)

*Text 57: Srimad-Bhagavatam - both the speaker and the hearer benefit*

Suta Gosvami now expresses his own fortune, because the sages’ questions have wakened him to full remembrance of the words he heard from the lotus mouth of his spiritual master, Srila Sukadeva Gosvami: “I also have now been fully reminded of the science of God, which I previously heard from the mouth of the great sage Sukadeva Gosvami. I was present in the assembly of great sages who heard him speak to King Pariksit as the monarch sat fasting until death.” (SB. 12.12.57)

*Texts 58-68: Phala'srutis - seven blessings for those who hear the Bhagavatam*

*Text 58: Inauspiciousness destroyed*

“O brahmanas, I have thus described to you the glories of the Supreme Lord Vasudeva, whose extraordinary activities are most worthy of glorification. This narration destroys all that is inauspicious.” (SB. 12.12.58)

“What to speak of purifying himself,” Srila Jiva Gosvami comments, “Suta Gosvami emphatically cries out that these topics purify everyone.” Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura notes, in his comment on text 59, that faithfully hearing about Lord Hari is the first step on the path of devotional service. He adds that Lord Sri Gaurasundara broadcast this fact to the world.

*Text 59: One is purified*

“One who with undeviating attention constantly recites this literature at every moment of every hour, as well as one who faithfully hears even one verse or half a verse or a single line or even half a line, certainly purifies his very self.” (SB. 12.12.59)

*Text 60: A long life, and sinful reactions purged*

“One who hears this Bhagavatam on the Ekadasi or Dvadasi day is assured of long life, and one who recites it with careful attention while fasting is purified of all sinful reactions.” (SB. 12.12.60)

*Text 61: Fear conquered*

“One who controls his mind, fasts at the holy places Puskara, Mathura, or Dvaraka, and studies this scripture will be freed from all fear.” (SB. 12.12.61)

*Text 62: All desirable things bestowed*

“Upon the person who glorifies this Purana by chanting or hearing it, the demigods, sages, Siddhas, Pitas, Manus, and kings of the earth bestow all desirable things.” (SB. 12.12.62)

*Text 63: The results of Vedic study bestowed*

“By studying this Bhagavatam, a brahmana can enjoy the same rivers of honey, ghee, and milk he enjoys by studying the hymns of the Rg, Yajur, and Sama Vedas.” (SB. 12.12.63)

In his comment on text 65, Srila Jiva Gosvami notes that the fruits mentioned in these verses are offered to encourage us to be eager to study Srimad-Bhagavatam.

“A brahmana who diligently reads this essential compilation of all the Puranas will go to the supreme destination, which the Supreme Lord Himself has herein described.”

*Text 65: Benedictions to inspire materialists*

“A brahmana who studies the Srimad-Bhagavatam achieves firm intelligence in devotional service, a king who studies it gains sovereignty over the earth, a vaisya acquires great treasure, and a sudra is freed from sinful reactions.” (SB. 12.12.65)

*Text 66 : The speciality of Srimad-Bhagavatam*

The Srimad-Bhagavatam is clearly a unique gift to humanity. Suta Gosvami tells us what is so special about the Bhagavatam: because it sings constantly about the Lord, the powerful Srimad-Bhagavatam destroys the entirety of the contaminations brought on by Kali-yuga. “Lord Hari, the supreme controller of all beings, annihilates the accumulated sins of the Kali age, yet other literatures do not constantly glorify Him. But that Supreme Personality of Godhead, appearing in His innumerable personal expansions, is abundantly and constantly described throughout the various narrations of this Srimad-Bhagavatam.” (SB. 12.12.66)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura notes that other literary works glorify work (karma) or powerful persons (such as devatas like Brahma), but they do not glorify Visnu - or if they do glorify Him, their glorification is limited and minor. The Bhagavatam alone profusely glorifies Bhagavan, who has unlimited forms. In every line and in every topic the Lord is fully glorified. The Srimad-Bhagavatam is therefore gloriously unique among literary works.

Srila Jiva Gosvami says something similar in his comment on this text, which he gives in anuccheda 107 of the Paramatma Sandarbha. In addition he notes, “This verse also indicates the uniqueness of the Bhagavatam, since the Supreme Lord Bhagavan’s form cannot be understood through other works.”

Srila Prabhupada deeply valued the Bhagavatam's power. His nights were dedicated not to sleeping hut to translating it into English. His days were spent working toward seeing to its publication and distribution. Srila Prabhupada’s faith in Srimad-Bhagavatam was full and heartfelt. Carrying his First Canto translations with him as he left Calcutta for New York City, it is obvious from the words he wrote on his arrival in 1965 that he felt confident in the power of the Bhagavatam: “How will they understand the mellows of devotional service? O Lord, I am simply praying for Your mercy so that I will be able to convince them about Your message. All living entities have become under the control of the illusory energy by Your will, and therefore, if You like, by Your will they can also be released from the clutches of illusion. I wish that You may deliver them. Therefore if You so desire their deliverance, then only will they be able to understand Your message. The words of Srimad-Bhagavatam are Your incarnation, and if a sober person repeatedly receives it with submissive aural reception, then he will be able to understand Your message.”

Here Srila Prabhupada seems to equate attaining the Lord’s mercy with repeatedly hearing Srimad-Bhagavatam.

*Texts 67-69: Obeisances*

*Texts 67-68: Obeisances to the Supreme Lord, who created the Bhagavatam*

Srila Suta Gosvami ends this twelfth chapter by offering repeated obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead: “I bow down to that unborn \[ajam\] and infinite \[anantam\] Supreme Soul \[atma-tattvam\], whose personal energies effect the creation, maintenance, and destruction of the material universe. Even Brahma, Indra, Sankara, and the other lords of the heavenly planets cannot fathom \[durava- sita\] the glories of that infallible \[acyutam\] Personality of Godhead.” (SB. 12.12.67)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura shows how the respects offered in this text are specifically offered to Krsna: “ ‘I bow to the unborn.’ Are you offering respects to Brahma, who is known as ajah, unborn? No. ‘I offer respects to the unlimited (anantam).’ Oh, is that pradhanal No. 'I le is the very form of consciousness (atma-tattvam).’ Is that the jival No. ‘I le possesses powers for creating, maintaining, and destroying the universe.’ Is that Siva? No. In their prayers, the devatas, such as Brahma and Siva, are unable to understand Acyuta’s glories.”

“I offer my obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is the eternal Lord and the leader of all other deities, who by evolving His nine material energieshas arranged within Himself the abode of all moving and nonmoving creatures, and who is always situated in pure, transcendental consciousness.” (SB. 12.12.68)

*Text 69: Obeisances to Srila Sukadeva Gosvami*

After offering his obeisances to the Supreme Lord, Srila Suta Gosvami offers them to his spiritual master: “Let me offer my respectful obeisances unto my spiritual master, the son of Vyasadeva, Sukadeva Gosvami. It is he who defeats all inauspicious things within this universe. Although in the beginning he was absorbed in the happiness of Brahman realization and was living in a secluded place, giving up all other types of consciousness, he became attracted by the pleasing, most melodious pastimes of Lord Sri Krsna. He therefore mercifully spoke this supreme Purana, Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is the bright light of the Absolute Truth and which describes the activities of the Lord.” (SB. 12.12.69)

Finding in this text both the glories of Sukadeva Gosvami and the Srimad-Bhagavatam, Srila Sridhara Svami comments: “Suta offers respects to his guru, whose heart was full (nibhrtam) of its own bliss (sva-sukham), by which all other thoughts were destroyed. But in spite of his firmness in that happiness he became attracted from the core of his being (sarah) to the pastimes of the Lord. I offer respects to he who spread the Bhagavatam, which reveals the topmost benefit (purusartha).”

Srila Jiva Gosvami glorifies the Bhagavatam in a number of texts. In the Bhagavata Sandarbha he comments on the unique power of the Bhagavatam: “There may be excellence in other works, but a direct encounter with Bhagavan, the crest jewel of those things that are to be obtained (purusartha), the highest object of knowledge in all scriptures concerning knowledge, is easily attained in the Bhagavatam.”

Srila Jiva Gosvami describes the Bhagavatam’s exalted power by asking, “By other scriptures and their methods, can the Supreme Lord immediately become fixed in the heart?” He replies to his own question: “Well, maybe a little, but only after a long time.” He continues: “Bhagavan is immediately fixed in the heart of those who even desire to hear Srimad-Bhagavatam."

Sri Jiva asks: “Why then doesn’t everyone hear the Bhagavatarn?” His reply: “Those who hear must have piety. Without piety the desire to hear does not arise.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura expands Suta Gosvami’s glorification of the Bhagavatam: “Having offered respects to Krsna, Sri Suta offers respects to his guru, saying that Sukadeva’s heart was completely filled with Brahman, and because of that, his mind was devoid of all else. But in spite of his having achieved this blissful state, he nevertheless became strongly attracted by the pleasing pastimes of Krsna. Thus his mind was drawn away from Brahman, and he became capable of tasting rasa, the sweet taste of the loving exchanges between Krsna and His dearest devotees. His realization was that the experience of Krsna’s pastimes was sweeter than the taste of Brahman, and thus he became fixed in those pastimes. Mercifully desiring others to also taste the sweetness of Krsna’s pastimes, he disseminated the teachings of the Bhagavatam, which contains pastimes that reveal the tattva of lila and rasa.”

**Chapter 13: The Glories of Srimad-Bhagavatam**

*Texts 1-2: Additional obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead*

In the first two texts of the final chapter of Srimad-Bhagavatam, Suta Gosvami offers his respects to the Supreme Lord without speaking the Lord’s name. First he describes the Lord’s unique position as the unlimited, the supreme object of glorification for the demigods and those who chant the Vedic mantras, and the Person on whom perfected yogis meditate. Thus Suta offers respects to the one who is the ultimate object of worship for all those who follow the Vedic culture. He is the goal of all bona fide processes of spiritual advancement: “Unto that personality whom Brahma, Varuna, Indra, Rudra, and the Maruts praise by chanting transcendental hymns and reciting the Vedas with all their corollaries, pada-kramas, and Upanisads, to whom the chanters of the Sama Veda always sing, whom the perfected yogis see within their minds after fixing themselves in trance and absorbing themselves within Him, and whose limit can never be found by any demigod or demon - unto that Supreme Personality of Godhead I offer my humble obeisances. ” (SB. 12.13.1)

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura describes the processes that allow a soul to see this unlimited Lord, who is beyond the abilility of the greatest demigods, sages, and mystics to know fully: “The karma-yogi, hatha-yogi, raja-yogi, and jnana-yogi are all under the sway of the mind (mano-dharma). Therefore whatever meditation they engage in is all more or less tinged by sense gratification \[karma\] or renunciation \[jnana\]. But the bhakti-yogis reject all such contamination, and in a perfectly pure mental trance engage with their internal eyes in medi- tation on what lies beyond the senses. Certainly that transcendental Lord on whom they meditate is not within the scope of the empirecists’ meditation. He is something completely beyond the enjoyers and sense objects of the visible and invisible worlds, where the sense perceivers dwell. Only those who have eyes smeared with the ointment of pure love of God can see this Supreme Deity.”

It’s interesting that Suta, the great speaker of the Bhagavatam, now glorifies one specific lila-avatara, Kurmadeva: “When the Supreme Personality of Godhead appeared as Lord Kurma, a tortoise, His back was scratched by the sharp-edged stones lying on massive, whirling Mount Mandara, and this scratching made the Lord sleepy. May you all be protected by the winds caused by the Lord’s breathing in this sleepy condition. Ever since that time, even up to the present day, the ocean tides have imitated the Lord’s inhalation and exhalation by piously coming in and going out.” (SB. 12.13.2)

The BBT purport is sweet: “At times we alleviate an itching sensation by blowing upon it. Similarly, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura explains, the breathing of the Supreme Personality of Godhead can alleviate the itching sensation within the minds of mental speculators, as well as the itching of the material senses of conditioned souls engaged in sense gratification. Thus by meditating on the windy breath of Lord Kurma — the tortoise incarnation — all categories of conditioned souls can be relieved of the deficiencies of material existence and come to the liberated, spiritual platform. One must simply allow the pastimes of Lord Kurma to blow within one’s heart like a favorable breeze; then one will surely find spiritual peace.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment is encouraging, as he draws parallels between Lord Kurina’s unique, awe-inspiring activities and the Srimad-Bhagavatam. Here is his comment, broken into four points.

1\. “Factually, the Lord in the form of Kurma churned the Milk Ocean, and the devatas caused the churning in name only. Similarly, the churning of the ocean of the Vedas to produce the Bhagavatam was done by the Lord alone, and the words of Srila Vyasadeva were only repeated by Sukadeva Gosvami.”

2\. “Kurma became sleepy due to the scratching caused by the edges of the stone during the rotation of the heavy Mandara Mountain. May the breathing of that sleepy Lord protect you.”

3\. “The Lord cheated the demons by taking the nectar obtained from the churning in the form of MohinI and gave it to the devatas, His devotees. Similarly, the Lord has churned the Vedas and produced the Bhagavatam, which contains the nectar of bhakti. Cheating the demons, may He give that nectar to you!”

4\. “Because of the traces of Kurma’s breathing, the oceans continue to ebb and flow. One may say that the oceans move because of tides, not because of the Lord’s breathing. But the tides are only a pretext. Truly, it is the Lord who causes those tides.”.

*Text 3: The contents of the final chapter of Srimad-Bhagavatam*

In the sixth chapter of Canto Twelve, Saunaka Rsi asked Suta Gosvami about the evolution of the Vedic literature. In chapter 12 of the Twelfth Canto, he first summarized the Vedas, Pur anas, and Tantras, then declared that the Vedic literature reaches its conclusion in the Srimad-Bhagavatam (texts 47—49 of the twelfth chapter). Now, after offering his repects to the Supreme Absolute Truth, Suta Gosvami lists the remaining contents of this final chapter of Srimad-Bhagavatam:

1\. The number of texts in each Purana (SB. 12.13.4-9).

2\. The subject of the Bhagavatam and its goal (SB. 12.13.10-12).

3\. The glories of Srimad-Bhagavatam and how to give it to others (SB. 12.13.13).

4\. The glories of hearing and chanting the Srimad-Bhagavatam (SB. 12.13.14-18).

And to conclude his recital of the Bhagavatam, Suta Gosvami will offer respects to the original speaker of the work, who is his own worshipful deity, his spiritual master, and will conclude with a request and then humble obeisances to the Supreme Lord Hari (SB. 12.13.19-23).

*Texts 4-9: The number of texts in each Parana*

The BBT purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.3 indicates the reason be- hind this enumeration: that it illustrates that the Srimad-Bhagavatam “is the best of all Puranas.’’ Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains in his comment on text 3 that “Just as the various rulers who come before the emperor of the world to praise him should be counted, so the various maha-puranas should be counted in the presence of the emperor among maha-puranas \[Srimad-Bhagavatam\].”

Suta Gosvami begins with a list of the number of verses in the eighteen major Puranas:

1\. Brahma Parana - 10,000

2\. Padma Parana - 5 5,000

3\. Sri Visnu Parana - 23,000

4\. Siva Parana - 24,000

5\. Srimad-Bhagavatam - 18,000

6\. Narada Parana - 25,000

7\. Markandeya Parana - 9,000

8\. Agni Purana - 15,400

9\. Bhavisya Pur aria - 14,500

10\. Brahma-Vaivarta Parana - 18,000

11\. Linga Purana - 11,000

12\. Varaha Purana - 24,000

13\. Skanda Purana - 81,100

14\. Vamana Purana - 10,000

15\. Kurma Parana - 17,000

16\. Matsya Parana - 14,000

17\. Garuda Purana - 19,000

18\. Brahmanda Parana - 12,000

Suta Gosvami concludes his enumeration: “Thus tin-total number of verses in all the Puranas is four hundred thousand. Eighteen thousand of these, once again, belong to the beautiful Bhagavatam.” (SB. 12.13.9)

In his comment on these texts, Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura also underscores the Bhagavatam’s unique position: “Just as Krsna is included in the listing of avataras since He appears in this world as an avatara - and yet His appearance is distinguished from other incarnations by the words krsnas tu bhagavan svavyam (SB. 1.3.28), so the Bhagavatam is included in the list of Puranas since it is also a Purana. But the Bhagavatam is again mentioned at the end as having eighteen thousand verses to indicate its role as the emperor among the Puranas. Just as the word svayam indicates the supreme position of Krsna in Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.3.28, so the word sri with Bhagavatam indicates that it is the most complete among all Puranas.”

*Texts 10-12: The Bhagavatam’s subject and goal*

The Srimad-Bhagavatam offers the conclusive, creamy essence of the entire Vedic culture: nigama-kalpa-taror galitam phalam, “O expert and thoughtful men, relish Srimad-Bhagavatam, the mature fruit of the desire tree of Vedic literatures.” (SB. 1.1.3)

*Text 10: Sri Krsna is the Bhagavatam’s original speaker*

“It was to Lord Brahma that the Supreme Personality of Godhead first revealed the Srimad-Bhagavatam in full. At the time, Brahma, frightened by material existence, was sitting on the lotus flower that had grown from the Lord’s navel.” (SB. 12.13.10)

The BBT purport identifies the Bhagavatam with Krsna Himself: “\[T\]he first verse of the Bhagavatam states, tene brahma hrda ya adi-kavaye: ‘Lord Krsna expanded perfect knowledge into the heart of Lord Brahma.’ Because conditioned souls can experience only temporary objects, which are created, maintained, and destroyed, they cannot readily understand that the Srimad-Bhagavatam is an eternal, transcendental literature and is nondifferent from the Absolute Truth.”

In the Tattva Sandarbha (anucchedas 18-19), Jiva Gosvami speaks of the Srimad-Bhagavatam as the supreme source of complete transcendental knowledge. He explains that knowledge arises from the mode of goodness (see Bhagavad-gita 14.6), and therefore the conclusions of the Puranas in the mode of goodness are accepted as stronger directives to attain the Absolute Truth than Puranas in the modes of passion and ignorance.As Srimad-Bhagavatam 1.2.24 states, “\[P\]assion \[rajas\] is better than ignorance \[tamas\], but goodness \[sattva\] is best because by goodness one can come to realize the Absolute Truth.”

Gopiparanadhana Prabhu, commenting on anuccheda 18, writes:

Thus the Puranas in the mode of goodness glorify Lord Hari, but those in passion and ignorance recommend the worship of other deities. Similarly, the Puranas in the mode of goodness address the more ultimate issues in life, such as its purpose, while those in lesser modes address more limited concerns, such as the purpose of the linga, as mentioned in the Linga Purana. Nevertheless, even these more limited Puranas instruct the reader to worship Hari so that those in the lower modes can be elevated.

But because there may be different interpretations even of the Puranas in the mode of goodness, Srila Jiva Gosvami defers to the Srimad-Bhagavatam as Srila Vyasadeva’s definitive commentary on the Vedanta-sutra, the universally accepted Vedic discourse on the Absolute Truth, which is also a compilation that reflects his fully matured realizations.Thus in Bhagavatam (1.1.3), Srimad-Bhagavatam refers to itself as the fully matured, ripened fruit of the Vedic literature (nigama-kalpa-taror galitam phalam) which contains the essence of the Vedas in the form of the Gayatri mantra expressed as dhimahi in its opening and closing texts (see SB. 1.1.1 and 12.13.19). Furthermore, in Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.14-18), we hear that it is unique among Puranas (text 14), that it contains the essence of the Vedanta-sutra (text 15), that it is supreme among the Puranas (texts 16 and 17), and that it is so powerful that it offers liberation even to jnanis (text 18).

*Texts 11-12: The Bhagavatam’s subject and goal*

“From beginning to end, the Srimad-Bhagavatam is full of narrations that encourage renunciation of material life, as well as nectarean \[amrta\] accounts of Lord Hari’s transcendental pastimes \[hari-hla-katha-vrata\], which give ecstasy to the saintly devotees and demigods \[sat-suram\]. This Bhagavatam is the essence of all Vedanta philosophy \[sarva-vedanta saram\] because its subject matter is the Absolute Truth, which, while nondifferent from the spirit soul, is the ultimate reality, one without a second. The goal of this literature is exclusive devotional service unto that Supreme Truth.” (SB. 12.13.11-12)

Srimad-Bhagavatam here expresses its goal. The BBT purport defines renunciation, vairagya, as “giving up everything that has no relation with the Absolute Truth.” It also glorifies the krsna-katha present in Srimad-Bhagavatam: “Saintly devotees and demigods are enthused by the nectar of the Lord’s spiritual pastimes, which are the essence of all Vedic knowledge.” And it concludes by echoing the Bhagavatam’s purpose: “Thus the ultimate goal of Srimad-Bhagavatam is to train the sincere reader in love of Godhead. Lord Krsna is supremely lovable because of His eternal, transcendental qualities. The beauty of this world is a dim reflection of the unlimited beauty of the Lord. Without compromise, Srimad-Bhagavatam persistently declares the glories of the Absolute Truth and is therefore the supreme spiritual literature, awarding a full taste of the nectar of love of Krsna in full Krsna consciousness.”

*Text 13: Offering Srimad-Bhagavatam as a gift*

“If on the full moon day of the month of Bhadra one places Srimad-Bhagavatam on a golden throne and gives it as a gift, he will attain the supreme transcendental destination.” (SB. 12.13.13)

The BBT purport describes how this is to be done: “One should place Srimad-Bhagavatam on a golden throne because it is the king of all literature. On the full-moon day of the month of Bhadra, the sun, which is compared to this king of literatures, is present in the constellation Leo and looks as if raised up on a royal throne. (According to astrology, the sun is said to be exalted in the sign of Leo.) Thus one may unreservedly worship Srimad-Bhagavatam, the supreme divine scripture.”

*Texts 14-18: The glory of hearing and chanting Srimad-Bhagavatam*

*Text 14: The Srimad-Bhagavatam is supreme among Puranas*

“All other Puranic scriptures shine forth in the assembly of saintly devotees only as long as that great ocean of nectar, Srimad-Bhagavatam, is not heard.” (SB. 12.13.14)

Srila ViSvanatha Cakravarti Thakura writes that other Puranas reign as kings uniil the Bhagavatam appears, since the Bhagavatam is like an emperor among kings. Similarly, “the other Puranas shine like stars in the night until the sunlike Bhagavatam rises.”

*Text 15: Srimad-Bhagavatam reveals the essence of Vedanta*

“Srimad-Bhagavatam is declared to be the essence of all Vedanta philosophy. One who has felt satisfaction from its nectarean mellow will never be attracted to any other literature.” (SB. 12.13.15)

In the Tattva Sandarbha (anucchedas 24-25), Srila Jiva Gosvami cites the above text to establish Srimad-Bhagavatam as the ultimate Vedic literature: “The philosophy of the Bhagavatam is the king of all philosophies \[and the opinion of the Bhagavatam rules over all other opinions\]. Sitting in an assembly of all sages, Sukadeva is the guru, acting as their teacher.”In his comments on these Tattva Sandarbha texts, Srila Baladeva Vidyabhusana notes, “Because the Bhagavatam has such great qualities, it is correctly stated in the First Canto (1.1.3) that it is the essence of all the Vedas and Itihasas."

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura explains further: “When a person has no understanding of the nectarean taste of Srimad-Bhagavatam, it does not give him pleasure. Such persons therefore indulge in tasting the mundane mellow of works other than Srimad-Bhagavatam. Reducing themselves to either enjoyers \[karmis\] or renounces \[jnanis\] they attain the presumption of being connoisseurs of the dryness that goes with having no taste. But those who are satisfied with the nectarean mellow of spiritual life have no attraction to literature that has no relationship with Lord Krsna.”

*Texts 16-17: Srimad-Bhagavatam is the greatest among the Puranas*

“Just as the Ganga is the greatest of all rivers, Lord Acyuta the supreme among deities, and Lord Sambhu \[Siva\] the greatest of Vaisnavas, so Srimad-Bhagavatam is the greatest of all Puranas. O brahmanas, in the same way that the city of Kasi is unexcelled among holy places, Srimad-Bhagavatam is supreme among all the Puranas.” (SB. 12.13.16-17)

*Text 18: The Srimad-Bhagavatam offers liberation to jnanis*

“Srimad-Bhagavatam is the spotless Purana. It is most dear to the Vaisnavas \[vaisnavanam priyam\] because it describes the pure and supreme knowledge of the paramahamsas. This Bhagavatam reveals the means for becoming free from all material work \[naiskarmyam\], together with the processes of transcendental knowledge, renunciation, and devotion. Anyone who seriously tries to understand Srimad-Bhagavatam, who properly hears and chants it with devotion, becomes completely liberated \[vimucyet\].” (SB. 12.13.18)

The BBT purport offers wise advice: “Because Srimad-Bhagavatam is completely free of contamination by the modes of nature, it is endowed with extraordinary spiritual beauty and is therefore dear to the pure devotees of the Lord. The word paramahamsyam indicates that even completely liberated souls are eager to hear and narrate Srimad-Bhagavatam. Those who are trying to be liberated should faithfully serve this literature by hearing and reciting it with faith and devotion.” Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s comment begins by explaining that Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.18 was spoken to explain the Bhagavatam’s supreme position: “This Pur ana alone is endowed with all glory, since it has no contamination arising from the three modes of nature. That the Srimad-Bhagavatam is dear to the devotees (vaisnavanarh priyam) shows the excellence of its bhakti. Even those (1) greedy to attain jnana arising from bhakti; (2) who have attained jnana; and (3) who are atmaramas, or self-satisfied, should take shelter of the Bhagavatam.... In the Bhagavatam, knowledge beneficial for paramahamsas is explained. This knowledge must necessarily be the best knowledge, as it arises from bhakti. Therefore even those practicing jnana should hear the Bhagavatam. It is completely free from karma (naiskarmyam).”

*Texts 19-23: Final meditations and the offering of obeisances*

*Text 19: Meditating on the Supreme Absolute Truth, and the origin of the disciplic succession of Bhagavatam speakers*

In Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.10, Suta Gosvami asserted that the Supreme Lord had first revealed Srimad-Bhagavatam to Brahma. Now, as part of his final meditation, in the Bhagavatam, on the Supreme Absolute Truth, Suta describes the succession of speakers descending from Brahma to Maharaja Pariksit: “I meditate upon that pure and spotless Supreme Absolute Truth \[satyam pararh dhimahi\], who is free from suffering and death and who in the beginning personally revealed this incomparable torchlight of knowledge to Brahma. Brahma then spoke it to the sage Narada, who narrated it to Krsna-dvaipayana Vyasa. Srila Vyasa revealed this Bhagavatam to the greatest of sages, Sukadeva Gosvami, and Sukadeva mercifully spoke it to Maharaja Pariksit.” (SB. 12.13.19)

The BBT purport describes the power of Srimad-Bhagavatam and what causes it to have such power: “The first verse of Srimad-Bhagavatam states, satyam param dhimahi - ‘I meditate upon the Supreme Truth’ - and now at the conclusion of this magnificent transcendental literature, the same auspicious sounds are vibrated... this verse clearly indicate\[s\] that Lord Krsna Himself originally spoke Srimad-Bhagavatam to Brahma and then continued to speak this literature through the agency of Narada Muni, Dvaipayana Vyasa, Sukadeva Gosvami, and other great sages. In other words, whenever saintly devotees vibrate Srimad-Bhagavatam, it is to be understood that Lord Krsna Himself is speaking the Absolute Truth through the agency of His pure representatives. Anyone who submissively hears this literature from the Lord’s bona fide devotees transcends his conditioned state and becomes qualified to meditate upon the Absolute Truth and serve Him.”

Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura concludes his comment on this text by describing the sought-after result of constant Bhagavatam study: “This Srimad-Bhagavatam is abundantly filled with the pastimes of Lord Krsna. The consequence of constantly studying it is that the spirit soul transcends his conditioned state and becomes qualified to meditate on and serve Lord Adhoksaja.”

In the Tattva Sandarbha (anuccheda 23), Srila Jiva Gosvami explains why Srlpada Sankaracarya neglected to comment on the Bhagavatam: “Although advocating Advaita (nondualistic monism) philosophy by the order of the Lord, in order to disguise himself, the avatara of Siva, Sankara, thinking of surpassing liberation and showing the Bhagavatam’s superiority to his own ideas by illustrating the joy of bhakti, only indirectly touched the Bhagavatam. Thus he described the Srimad-Bhagavatam but avoided adding an Advaita commentary to it. He feared giving a false interpretation of the Bhagavatam, which properly explains the Brahma-sutras.”

Sri Baladeva Vidyabhusana’s comment on this Tattva Sandarbha text explains further: “Thus because of the excellent qualities mentioned above, and although there are many Puranas, the Bhagavatam is described as the sun for Kali-yuga. The Bhagavatam is also accepted by ancient and modern scholars… But why didn’t Sankaracarya comment on it? Sri Sankaracarya thought, ‘In charge of destruction, I, Lord Siva, a devotee of Visnu, have followed His order in destroying the real conclusion of the Upanisads by explaining them in a certain way. But if I misinterpret His very dear Bhagavatam, He will become angry with me. Thus I cannot misinterpret the Bhagavatam. But \[by neglecting the Bhagavatam\] I will be deprived of great happiness (prema), which is understood to he the highest goal. Therefore I will touch upon it a little.’ Sankaracarya thus respected the Bhagavatam and did not comment on it, but described in His poems Yasoda’s seeing the universal form. Thus the Bhagavatam is respected by all.”

To allow readers to sample the bliss Sripada Sankaracarya longed to taste, I include below four of the eight sweet texts Sankaracarya composed in his Govindastaka:

(2)

Please bow down to Govinda, supreme bliss personified. Although He is the supreme master of the universe, He seemed to become frightened like an ordinary infant when Mother Yasoda chastised Him. When she asked, “Are You eating mud?” He opened His mouth to prove He was not - and showed her the fourteen planetary systems, including Lokaloka Mountain. He is the supporting pillar for this citylike universe of three worlds. Although He is beyond all vision, He is the source of everyone’s vision.

(3)

Please bow down to Govinda, supreme bliss personified. He relieves the earth of its burden by killing the demigods’ enemies, the demons, and He grants liberation by curing the disease of materialism. Although He never needs to eat, still He eats butter, and He also devours the whole universe at the time of annihilation. Although distinct from all the shadow manifestations of this world, He manifests in the sanctified desires of a pure heart. He is most auspicious and peaceful.

(5)

Please bow down to Govinda, supreme bliss personified. He stole the bathing damsels’ clothes and climbed a tree with them, and when the naked maidens asked for their clothes back, He told them to come closer, lie dispels lamentation and delusion. He is knowledge personified, realized by intelligence, and is also the personification of pure existence.

(6)

Please bow down to Govinda, supreme bliss personified. He is most beautiful. He is the original cause of all causes, and He has no cause. He is free from all superimpositions of illusion. He danced wonderfully on the hoods of the Kaliya serpent in the Yamuna. Although He is time, He is beyond all divisions of time. He knows everything, He destroys the defects of Kali-yuga, and He is the source of past, present, and future.

*Text 20: Obeisances to Krsna, the Bhagavatams original speaker and Suta Gosvami’s worshipable Deity*

Sri Suta Gosvami continues: “We offer our obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, Lord Vasudeva, the all-pervading witness, who mercifully explained this science to Brahma when he anxiously desired salvation.” (SB. 12.13.20)

Srila Prabhupada’s purport to Srimad-Bhagavatam 2.9.37 explains that Vasudeva, who first spoke the Bhagavatam to Brahma and who is Suta Gosvami’s worshipful Deity and the object of his obeisances, is Krsna, the cowherd boy, the origin of all, and the Supreme Personality of Godhead:

In the Gopala'tapani Upanisad (sruti) it is said, gopa-veso me purusah pur as tad avirbabhuva: the Lord appeared before Brahma as a cowherd boy, that is, as the original Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, Govinda, who is later described by Brahmaji in his Brahma-samhita (5.29):

*cintamani-prakarasadmasu kalpa-vrksa-*

*laksavrtesu surabhir abhipalayantam*

*laksmusahasra-sata-sambhrama-sevyamanam*

*govindam adi-purusarh tarn aharh bhajami*

Brahmaji desires to worship the original Personality of Godhead, Lord Sri Krsna, who resides in the topmost Vaikuntha planet, known as Goloka Vrndavana, where He is in the habit of keeping surabhi cows as a cowboy and where He is served by hundreds and thousands of goddesses of fortune (the gopis) with love and respect.

Therefore Lord Sri Krsna is the original form of the Supreme Lord (krsnas tu bhagavan svayam). That point is also clear from this instruction. The Supreme Personality of Godhead is Lord Krsna, and not Narayana or the purusa-avataras, which are His subsequent manifestations. Therefore Srimad-Bhagavatam means consciousness of the Supreme Personality of Godhead Lord Sri Krsna, and Srimad-Bhagavatam is the sound representation of the Lord as much as is the Bhagavad-gita. Thus the conclusion is that Srimad-Bhagavatam is the science of the Lord in which the Lord and His abode are perfectly realized.

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura describes the object of Suta Gosvami’s worship in his comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam 12.13.20, and how it is Krsna who inspires Brahma’s desire for prema: “Having ended the scripture, Suta Gosvami offers respects to his personal Deity. I offer respects to the son of Vasudeva, the witness, who directly sees whether I am a devotee or devoid of bhakti, whether I am wise or of corrupt intelligence, whether I know or do not know how to explain the intended meaning of the Bhagavatam. I take shelter of His mercy.... Even Brahma, without the Lord’s mercy, will not know the meaning of the Bhagavatam. Vasudeva mercifully explained it to him when he desired liberation. Prior to his asking for this knowledge, Brahma desired liberation. After hearing the Lord’s instructions, He became indifferent to liberation and desired prema.”

Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu accepted Srila Sridhara Svami’s commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam as the foundational, authorized commentary all subsequent commentators must follow. Sridhara Svami ends his Bhavartha-dipika commentary in this sweet and humble way: “This Bhavartha-dipika, which is very dear to the devotees of the Supreme Lord, has been composed by Sridhara, who is like the bumblebee decorating the lotus feet of Paramananda.May the supremely ecstatic (paramananda) Lord Nrhari, who is the supreme eternal spiritual master, be satisfied with my whimsical, childish chattering, which is made to dance by His own desire. I have elaborated on the secret essence of Srimad-Bhagavatam for the satisfaction of Sri Paramananda.

I have written according to his ideas, not hy the power of any ideas of my own. I low can a foolish person such as myself comment on Srimad-Bhagavatam, which is full of the most confidential ideas? How can I measure up to the standard of pure love for Krsna? But then, what can such love for Krsna not accomplish?”

*Text 21: Suta Gosvami offers obeisances to Sukadeva Gosvami, his spiritual master*

“I offer my humble obeisances to Sri Sukadeva Gosvami, the best of mystic sages \[yogi-indraya, the king of yogis\] and a personal manifestation of the Absolute Truth. He saved Maharaja Pariksit \[visnu-ratam\], who was bitten by the snake of material existence.” (SR 12.13.21)

The BBT purport explains a subtle point in this text: “Suta Gosvami now offers obeisances to his own spiritual master Sukadeva Gosvami. Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura clarifies that just as Arjuna was placed into material confusion so that the Bhagavad-gita might be spoken, so King Pariksit, a pure, liberated devotee of the Lord, was cursed to die so that Srimad-Bhagavatam might be spoken. Actually, King Pariksit is visnu-rata, eternally under the protection of the Lord. Sukadeva Gosvami liberated the king from his so-called illusion to exhibit the merciful nature of a pure devotee and the enlightening effect of his association.”

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura explains that Suta Gosvami respects Sukadeva as the king of yogis because he is the master of bhakti-yoga, jnana-yoga, karma-yoga, and astanga-yoga.

Srila Jiva Gosvami ends his commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam with prayerful words of praise for Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu: “May that Lord who is described in the Visnu-sahasra-nama, vardhgas candanahgadi/ sannyasa-krc chamah canto nistha-santi-parayanah, namely Sri Krsna Caitanya Mahaprabhu, protect me from my offenses and maintain me with a drop of His pure love.”

In his own final commentary on Srimad-Bhagavatam, Srila Bhaktisiddhanta Sarasvati Thakura again describes the freedom that comes from studying Srimad-Bhagavatam and glorifies the unique gift of Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu: “The result of studying the pastimes of Lord Krsna is that one is freed from the materialistic outlooks of karma and jnana, from all relationship with temporary objects, and from tire false idea of seeking material pleasure, which is born of ignorance. Certainly, acting through the disciplic descendants and followers of the supremely merciful Sri Vyasa, Lord Sri Krsnacandra, the eternal spiritual master of the entire universe, appearing in the form of Sri Krsna Caitanya, has given such extraordinary mercy to the conditioned souls - as has not been seen in many ages.”

*Texts 22-23: Suta Gosvami completes the Srimad-Bhagavatam*

Sri Suta Gosvami now speaks two slokas that conclude Srimad-Bhagavatam. He first expresses his most cherished and heartfelt desire: “O Lord of lords, O master, please grant us pure devotional service at Your lotus feet, life after life.” (SB. 12.13.22)

In the final text of Srimad-Bhagavatam, Srila Suta Gosvami offers his obeisances to the Supreme Personality of Godhead, who is nondifferent from the Bhagavatam and who is also its subject:

*nama-sahkirtanarh yasya*

*sarva-papa pranasanam*

*pranamo duhkha-samanas*

*tam namami harim param*

“I offer my respectful obeisances unto the Supreme Lord, Hari, the congregational chanting of whose holy names destroys all sinful reactions, and the offering of obeisances unto whom relieves all material suffering.” (SB. 12.13.23)

Srila Visvanatha Cakravarti Thakura’s concluding comments on the Srimad-Bhagavatam are extreme in their devotion, sweetness, and humility:

I offer respects to guru and Krsna, and to the ocean of mercy, Lokanatha.O Krsna Caitanya! O Gauranga, along with your associates! O unconditional ocean of mercy! Please fill me with premal Glory to the Divine Couple, who are expert in performing Their rasa pastimes in Vrndavana! Please lead me to your gopi associates! Be merciful to this commentary! Although I am ignorant, You have made me write this commentary. O Krsna! O Bhagavatam! Be pleased with this commentary! O protector of the cows, although I am unintelligent, please accept and protect it! Drink its milk and, if You are pleased, distribute it to Your devotees. This commentary has been completed on the sixth lunar day of the waxing moon of the month of Magha, 1626 Saka era.

May the devotees of the Lord relish this commentary! Since the most learned among those who are materially learned still have no taste for the Bhagavatam, whose sole function is to play in the waves of sweetness - a mood that is incomprehensible to the six philosophies - let it remain an unfortunate creation, defective in every word for them, though it is actually endowed with all good qualities and dances with divine wisdom.

There is no harm if the Bhagavatam contains (elements of other philosophies)... This exposition of bhakti, the jewel of human endeavors, is only seen by devotion and by the mercy of one’s guru. Therefore I offer repeated respects to my guru. O devotees! This foolish person with a fickle mind is crying at your door. Like a dog without a master, may he receive from you a little mercy! I

I offer respects to Govardhana, the best of the Lord’s servants. I offer repeated respects to Sri Radha-kunda and Sri Krsna-kunda.

**Epilogue**

This volume of the Srimad-Bhagavatam Overview is now complete. I have already published Unveiling His Lotus Feet, which is an overview of cantos One through Four. This second volume to be published is, of course, not in consecutive order, hut because I was studying and teaching cantos Eleven and Twelve, it seemed fitting to write this book second. The in- spiration impelling me to write these overviews is the opportunity then have given me to become absorbed in Srimad-Bhagavatam. I have found the Srimad-Bhagavatam to be a sweet and transcendental text dear to Srila Prabhupada, the Vaisnava deary as, and Sri Caitanya Mahaprabhu. I pray that my work has brought you hope, direction, and spiritual noun ishment. I pray it has awarded you happiness and courage. I pray that it has enlivened your spiritual intelligence and inspired in you a desire to deeply study the full Srimad-Bhagavatam as Srila Prabhupada presented it.

## Appendix 1. A guide to the Uddhava-gita

**Canto Eleven: Chapters 6-29**

What follows is a chapter-by-chapter guide to the entire Uddhava-gita - first a quick overview and then a chapter summary.

**Chapter 6: The Yadu Dynasty Retires to Prabhasa**

The sixth chapter describes how Brahma and other demigods approach Lord Krsna in Dvaraka and offer prayers to glorify His lotus feet. Brahma humbly informs Krsna that He has completed His mission on earth and asks Him to return to His own abode. Krsna accepts Brahma’s request, and the demigods leave.

Then serious disturbances rock Dvaraka, and Krsna suggests to the Yadu elders that they immediately go to Prabhasa to perform a sacrifice. Uddhava understands from these events that Lord Krsna is going to depart, and anticipates his separation from the Lord with great feeling. He approaches Krsna and begs not to be left behind but to be taken back to His abode, because service to his beloved friend is the essence of his life.

**Summary**

Attracted to Lord Krsna and eager to see Him before He concludes His earthly pastimes, the demigods, headed by Lord Brahma, approach the Lord in Dvaraka. They cover Krsna with heavenly garlands and praise Him (1-6). They then declare that taking shelter of His lotus feet and hearing His glories are the two processes that purify the heart and help one overcome the powerful material energy. Krsna is the cause of every- thing within the material creation, and yet He is completely transcendental to it. Therefore His association is purifying to the utmost degree. His association is especially potent when His pure devotees are discussing His glories and when one is in contact with the water that has touched His lotus feet. The demigods feel themselves fortunate to see Krsna’s lotus feet and to take shelter of them (7-19).

Brahma had once appealed to the Lord to remove the earth’s distress. Now, 125 years later, Brahma humbly informs Krsna that His mission on behalf of the demigods has been fulfilled and He can, if He so desires, return to His own abode. Brahma also asks the Lord to continue to protect the demigods and their followers (20-27). Krsna accepts Brahma’s words. All that remains for Him to do is to send the Yadu dynasty back to the Dvaraka in the spiritual world, because only Krsna is able to contain the dynasty He created to assist Him in His pastimes; the members of the Yadu dynasty were eternal associates of Krsna, and after His departure, His separation would become intolerable for them. They would become so agitated that they might destroy the earth. Therefore the Lord enacted the pastime of annihilating His own family, using as a vehicle the brahmanas’ curse (28-32).

After speaking about this with Brahma, Dvaraka experiences a series of disturbances. Krsna suggests to the senior Yadus that they should immediately go to Prabhasa to perform a sacrifice. This will free them from the danger, He says. The Yadus prepare to depart (33-39).
